survivors.title: get_resume_brief destroys the drift snapshot as a side effect, so a second call silently returns a briefing missing the SINCE YOU LEFT section
evidence: src/tools/get-resume-brief.mjs:28 — `const drift = await takeDriftSnapshot(driver, thread.id);`
src/drift/snapshot.mjs:86-92 — takes `snapshot[threadId]`, then writes back `remaining` = the snapshot with that thread's entries REMOVED, then returns `taken`
src/render/briefing.mjs:54-68 — `driftBlock` returns `null` when the entries array is empty, and `renderBriefing` (briefing.mjs:184) drops null blocks entirely
src/tools/get-resume-brief.mjs:40 — description: 'Render the preflight briefing for a thread as markdown ... The rendered string is the only payload.' No mention of any mutation.
src/tools/get-resume-brief.mjs:30-34 — also writes BRIEFING_INDEX, and never calls commit
survivors.mechanism: get_resume_brief calls takeDriftSnapshot (get-resume-brief.mjs:28). takeDriftSnapshot is a destructive read: snapshot.mjs:90 builds `remaining` by filtering the thread's key out of the snapshot object, snapshot.mjs:91 writes that back to the drift index file, and snapshot.mjs:92 returns the taken entries. The entries are now gone from storage. On the next call, snapshot.mjs:86 resolves `snapshot[threadId] ?? []`, snapshot.mjs:87-89 short-circuits to `[]`, and briefing.mjs:55-68 produces zero lines so `driftBlock` returns null and briefing.mjs:184 filters the whole section out. Verified empirically against a temp LocalDriver ledger: call 1 briefing contained 'SINCE YOU LEFT', call 2 did not.
survivors.model_impact: A model that re-renders the brief for any ordinary reason — the verbatim-print gate failed, the user asked to see it again, a retry after an ambiguous transport error, a second skill invocation in one session — permanently loses the branch-drift report and has no way to know it existed. The description explicitly frames the tool as a pure render with 'the rendered string is the only payload', so nothing warns the model. The lost information (a deleted or diverged branch) is exactly the class of fact the briefing exists to deliver.
survivors.failure_scenario: preflight calls get_resume_brief, the model mis-prints the briefing and calls it again to re-read it; the second briefing omits the 'diverged feat/x — BRANCH_GONE' line and the model reports to the user that nothing changed since last session.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced. src/tools/get-resume-brief.mjs:28 calls takeDriftSnapshot. src/drift/snapshot.mjs:86 reads snapshot[threadId]; :90 builds `remaining` by filtering that key out; :91 writes it back; :92 returns the taken entries. src/render/briefing.mjs:68 returns null when no lines were produced and :184 drops falsy blocks. My own probe against a temp LocalDriver (seeded via writeDriftSnapshot with one branch-gone entry): call 1 briefing contained 'SINCE YOU LEFT' = true, call 2 = false, and the persisted briefing index rendered string is driftless after call 2 (get-resume-brief.mjs:30-34). The finding is if anything UNDERSTATED on permanence: the merged/deleted cases are not regenerable by re-running reconcile, because src/drift/reconcile.mjs:43-46 writes the binding back with status 'merged'/'orphaned' and :32-34 skips every binding whose status is not 'active' on later runs. Only the 're-verify' disposition (src/drift/disposition.mjs:49-57, binding_status null) leaves the binding active and thus regenerable. One listed trigger is wrong: a failed verbatim-print gate does NOT force a re-call, because hooks/lib/stop.mjs:12 embeds the full pledged text in the block reason. The other triggers (user asks to see it again, retry after ambiguous transport error, second preflight invocation in one session) stand, and hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:99 runs reconcile once per session start, so a second get_resume_brief inside that session is always driftless.

survivors.title: update_thread replaces spine.out_of_scope wholesale while its own description teaches scope-carrying merge semantics for the two sibling arrays, silently deleting prior entries
evidence: src/tools/update-thread.mjs:56-58 — `const spine = { ...thread.spine, ...submitted, ...}`; `out_of_scope` is only ever overwritten by this spread, unlike open_risks/key_decisions which get `replaceScopedItems` at :59-68
src/tools/update-thread.mjs:18-27 — `replaceScopedItems` carries every unnamed scope forward; it is applied to open_risks and key_decisions only

src/tools/update-thread.mjs:130 — description says 'A risks or decisions array replaces only the scopes it mentions and carries every scope it does not, so submitting the current step's items never deletes another step's.' out_of_scope is never mentioned as an exception.
src/tools/schemas.mjs:39-46 — replaceScopesInput accepts only open_risks and key_decisions, so there is no way to express intent for out_of_scope either way
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:31 — instructs writing `out_of_scope` alongside open_risks in the same call, with no warning that it is replace-all
survivors.mechanism: patchSpine builds `submitted = {...spinePatch}` (update-thread.mjs:37) and then constructs the new spine at update-thread.mjs:56-69. open_risks and key_decisions are explicitly rebuilt through replaceScopedItems, which merges by scope. out_of_scope receives no such treatment — it arrives only via the `...submitted` spread at line 58, so any submitted array replaces the stored one entirely. Verified: after `update_thread(spine:{out_of_scope:['alpha rewrite','beta migration']})` followed by `update_thread(spine:{out_of_scope:['gamma refactor']})`, the stored value is `["gamma refactor"]`.
survivors.model_impact: The description spends its longest passage teaching the model that submitting the current step's items never deletes another step's. A model that generalizes that rule — which is the only reasonable reading — will write out_of_scope incrementally each session and silently destroy every entry written by every prior session. The write returns success and echoes the truncated array, so there is no signal. Out-of-scope entries are precisely the 'we already decided not to do this' facts a future session most needs.
survivors.failure_scenario: Session 3 sets out_of_scope to three boundary decisions. Session 4's debrief adds one new boundary and calls update_thread with a single-element out_of_scope. The three earlier boundaries are gone; session 5's briefing shows one 'NOT IN SCOPE' line and the model re-proposes work that was explicitly ruled out.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced. src/tools/update-thread.mjs:56-69 builds the new spine as `{...thread.spine, ...submitted, open_risks: replaceScopedItems(...), key_decisions: replaceScopedItems(...)}` — out_of_scope reaches the result only through the `...submitted` spread at :58 and is therefore overwritten wholesale. src/tools/spine-input.mjs:10 freezes SCOPED_SPINE_FIELDS to ['open_risks','key_decisions'] only, and src/tools/schemas.mjs:39-46 lets replace_scopes name only those two, so out_of_scope has no scope machinery at all. My probe: update_thread with out_of_scope ['alpha rewrite','beta migration'] then ['gamma refactor'] left the stored value as ["gamma refactor"]. The description at src/tools/update-thread.mjs:130 devotes its longest passage to the carry-forward rule and never exempts out_of_scope, and skills/debrief/SKILL.md:31 instructs writing out_of_scope in the same call as open_risks under the same four-part gate.

survivors.title: record_decision writes spine.key_decisions[].title with no length gate, bypassing the 120-char cap update_thread enforces on the identical field
evidence: src/tools/record-decision.mjs:68-70 — `: [...thread.spine.key_decisions, { ref, title: args.title, scope }]` — appended verbatim
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:76 — `await driver.writeThread(updated);` — record_decision never calls assertSpineCaps anywhere in the file
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:91 — input schema: `title: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` — no maxLength
src/model/caps.mjs:9 — `decisionTitleMaxChars: 120`
src/model/caps.mjs:79-86 — decisionViolations enforces it, reached only from src/tools/update-thread.mjs:77 `assertSpineCaps(submitted)`
src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:29 — write-time decisionItem `title: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` — no maxLength, so the last validation layer does not catch it either
survivors.mechanism: record_decision resolves a scope (record-decision.mjs:52-55), then appends `{ref, title: args.title, scope}` to thread.spine.key_decisions (record-decision.mjs:70) and writes the thread (record-decision.mjs:76). The only cap enforcement for decision titles lives in caps.mjs:79-86, which is only invoked from update-thread.mjs:77. local-driver.mjs:148 `assertValidThread(thread)` validates against thread.schema.mjs, whose decisionItem title (line 29) has no maxLength. Verified: a 400-char title was accepted and stored by record_decision, and the same 400-char title submitted through update_thread was refused with `CapViolationError: spine.key_decisions item title exceeds 120 chars`.
survivors.model_impact: Two tools write the same field in the same record; one enforces a cap, the other does not, and neither description names a number. A model told 'caps are enforced' by update_thread's description learns a rule that record_decision does not apply, so identical content succeeds or fails depending on which tool it happened to route through. The over-cap title is then rendered into every future briefing via briefing.mjs:125, and any later update_thread call that resubmits that decision entry is refused for content the server itself wrote.
survivors.failure_scenario: A model records a decision with a 200-char descriptive title (accepted). In a later session it tries to re-scope that decision via update_thread's key_decisions array, faithfully copying the stored title, and is refused with a cap error for a value it did not author and cannot shorten without contradicting the decision file.

verdict.correction: record_decision does write spine.key_decisions[].title with no length gate, and update_thread refuses the identical value — that part is exactly right. But the consequences are bounded, not critical: the briefing truncates the title to 120 chars at render (src/render/briefing.mjs:9-12 truncate, applied at :125), so nothing is displayed over-cap and no record is corrupted; and a stored over-cap title never blocks later writes unless the caller resubmits that entry, because src/tools/update-thread.mjs:77 asserts caps on `submitted` only, while carried-forward stored items pass through replaceScopedItems (:18-27) uninspected. The accurate claim is a cross-tool validation-coverage gap producing an inconsistent accept/reject for identical content, not a data-integrity failure.
verdict.reasoning: Re-derived: src/tools/record-decision.mjs:70 appends `{ ref, title: args.title, scope }` verbatim; :76 writes the thread; the file imports no cap helper (:1-4) and its schema declares `title: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` at :91 with no maxLength. src/model/caps.mjs:9 sets decisionTitleMaxChars 120 and :79-86 enforces it, reachable only from src/tools/update-thread.mjs:77. The write-time backstop src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:148 validates against src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:29, which is `title: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` — no maxLength. My probe: a 400-char title was accepted by record_decision and stored (read back, length 400); the same 400-char title through update_thread returned `CapViolationError: spine.key_decisions item title exceeds 120 chars`.

survivors.title: scope is validated only by regex, so risks and decisions can be filed under a criterion id that does not exist and become permanently invisible in every briefing
evidence: src/schema/patterns.mjs:24 — `WRITABLE_SCOPE_PATTERN = '^(c[1-9][0-9]*|thread)$'` — matches c1 through c999999 regardless of what the thread contains
src/tools/schemas.mjs:18 and :30 — riskInputItem.scope and decisionInputItem.scope are pattern-only
src/tools/spine-input.mjs:12-19 — assertWritableScope rejects only the literal 'legacy'; no existence check
src/tools/spine-input.mjs:26-34 — normalizeScopeList re-tests the same regex; still no existence check
src/model/selection.mjs:39-42 — `visibleScopes` = {'thread'} plus the anchor criterion's id, and nothing else
src/render/briefing.mjs:105 and :121 — risks and decisions are filtered by `visibleScopes.has(r.scope)` / `.has(d.scope)`
src/render/briefing.mjs:150-156 — the NOT SHOWN block reports only counts, never the scope name
survivors.mechanism: normalizeRisks (spine-input.mjs:58-72) and normalizeDecisions (spine-input.mjs:74-84) accept whatever scope string the caller passes provided it matches WRITABLE_SCOPE_PATTERN and is not 'legacy'. Nothing cross-checks against thread.completion_criteria. The stored item then reaches the briefing, where selectCurrent (selection.mjs:35-49) builds visibleScopes from only 'thread' plus the single anchor criterion, and briefing.mjs:105/121 filter everything else out. Since no criterion with that id exists, it can never become the anchor, so the item is unreachable forever. Verified: `update_thread(spine:{open_risks:[{text:'ghost risk — nobody will ever see this', scope:'c99'}]})` on a three-criterion thread was accepted and stored as `{"text":"ghost risk — ...","scope":"c99","refs":[]}`.
survivors.model_impact: A model that miscounts criteria by one, or reuses a scope id remembered from a different thread, writes a risk that the ledger accepts, acknowledges, and then never shows to anyone. The write path reports success; the read path silently omits it; the NOT SHOWN counter attributes it to 'other steps', which is a false explanation. This is the exact failure mode the ledger exists to prevent — a fact captured and then lost.
survivors.failure_scenario: A model files 'do not upgrade ajv past 8.x — the pattern semantics change' scoped to c4 on a thread that has three criteria. Every subsequent briefing omits it; NOT SHOWN reports '1 risk(s) from other steps', and no step ever reveals it.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced. src/schema/patterns.mjs:24 defines WRITABLE_SCOPE_PATTERN as '^(c[1-9][0-9]*|thread)$' — a pure shape test. src/tools/schemas.mjs:18 and :30 apply it as the only schema constraint on risk/decision scope. src/tools/spine-input.mjs:12-19 (assertWritableScope) rejects only the literal 'legacy'; :26-34 (normalizeScopeList) re-tests the same regex; neither consults thread.completion_criteria. src/tools/spine-input.mjs:65 and :81 accept `risk.scope ?? resolveWriteScope(thread)` with no existence check. Visibility: src/model/selection.mjs:39-42 builds visibleScopes as {'thread'} plus the anchor criterion id only, and src/render/briefing.mjs:105 / :121 filter on `visibleScopes.has(...)`. src/render/briefing.mjs:150-156 reports only counts and attributes the hidden item to 'other steps'. My probe on a three-criterion thread: `open_risks:[{text:'ghost risk — nobody will ever see this', scope:'c99'}]` was accepted and stored as {"text":"ghost risk — ...","scope":"c99","refs":[]}. Reachability caveat that does not save it: src/model/criteria.mjs:3-11 issues ids monotonically, so c99 would only become an anchor after 99 criteria exist on that thread.

survivors.title: The same decision ref can be stored twice in spine.key_decisions under different scopes and renders twice in the briefing; nothing deduplicates by ref
evidence: src/tools/record-decision.mjs:68 — dedup is `thread.spine.key_decisions.some((d) => d.ref === ref)`, evaluated once at insert time against whatever is stored then
src/tools/update-thread.mjs:18-27 — replaceScopedItems keys its replacement set on `item.scope`, never on `item.ref`, so an entry with the same ref under a different scope is carried, not replaced
src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:105 — `key_decisions: { type: 'array', items: decisionItem }` — no uniqueItems, no ref uniqueness constraint
src/render/briefing.mjs:119-127 — decisionsBlock maps every visible entry with no dedup
src/model/selection.mjs:39-42 — 'thread' and the anchor criterion id are BOTH always visible, so a ref stored under each renders twice
survivors.mechanism: record_decision appends `{ref, title, scope}` with scope defaulting to resolveWriteScope (record-decision.mjs:53, selection.mjs:20-23) — typically the current criterion id. A later update_thread that submits the same ref with `scope:'thread'` goes through replaceScopedItems, which computes `replaced = new Set([...incoming.map(i => i.scope), ...authoritative])` (update-thread.mjs:22) and carries every stored item whose scope is not in that set (update-thread.mjs:23-26). The criterion-scoped copy survives; the thread-scoped copy is added. Verified end to end: after record_decision (scope c1) then update_thread with the same ref at scope 'thread', the rendered briefing's DECIDED ON THIS STEP block contained '- 0001 — Use event sourcing for billing' twice.
survivors.model_impact: A model doing the natural thing — promoting a step-scoped decision to a standing thread-scoped one — creates a duplicate rather than a move, with no error and no signal in the return value. The duplicate is then re-read as two decisions in every briefing, inflating the apparent decision count and wasting briefing budget. There is no tool that can remove one copy: replace_scopes can only clear a whole scope, which would also destroy the other decisions filed there.
survivors.failure_scenario: A model records decision 0007 while working criterion c2, then in debrief lists it under scope 'thread' because it is a standing constraint. The next session's briefing shows decision 0007 twice; the model treats it as two separate decisions and reasons about a conflict that does not exist.

verdict.correction: The duplicate is real, silent, and renders twice — confirmed. But the closing claim that no tool can remove one copy is wrong. update_thread's own documented mechanism removes it: naming the scope in replace_scopes replaces that scope with whatever the call submits for it, and src/tools/update-thread.mjs:26 returns `[...carried, ...incoming]`, so a caller can name the scope and resubmit only the survivors — or, when the scope holds only the duplicate, name it and submit nothing. Accurate claim: promoting a decision to thread scope copies rather than moves it, with no error and no dedup by ref; the fix is a documented second call, not an unrecoverable state.
verdict.reasoning: Re-derived: src/tools/record-decision.mjs:68 dedups on `d.ref === ref` at insert time only; src/tools/update-thread.mjs:22 keys the replacement set on `item.scope`, never on `item.ref`; src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:105 declares `key_decisions: { type: 'array', items: decisionItem }` with no uniqueItems; src/render/briefing.mjs:119-127 maps every visible entry with no dedup; src/model/selection.mjs:39-42 makes 'thread' and the anchor id both visible. My probe: record_decision at scope c1 then update_thread with the same ref at scope 'thread' stored both, and a third update at scope c2 stored a third copy of ref 0002-event-sourcing. Then `update_thread(replace_scopes:{key_decisions:['c1']})` with no key_decisions submission cleanly removed the c1 copy and left the thread-scoped one — refuting the un-removability claim.

survivors.title: amend_criteria's oneOf plus params-stripping error formatting produce up to 13 mutually contradictory clauses that never name the offending property, making retry non-convergent
evidence: src/tools/schemas.mjs:72-109 — criteriaAmendOperation is a three-branch oneOf, each branch with its own required list and additionalProperties:false

src/schema/validators.mjs:9-11 — `errors.map((e) => `${e.instancePath || '(root)'} ${e.message}`.trim()).join('; ')` — ajv's `e.params` is discarded, which is where additionalProperty, allowedValue and allowedValues live
src/tools/registry.mjs:36 — `new Ajv({ allErrors: true })` — every branch's failures are collected, not just the closest
src/tools/registry.mjs:46 — ToolValidationError message is exactly formatValidationErrors output

src/tools/registry.mjs:64 — `throw new ToolValidationError(name, [...validate.errors])` — the structured errors array is attached but bin/ledger-server.mjs:57 serializes only `{error: error.name, message: error.message}`, so the model never sees it
survivors.mechanism: With allErrors:true and a oneOf, ajv reports the failures of all three branches. formatValidationErrors keeps only instancePath and message. Measured against the live registry: `{op:'insert', text:'do the thing'}` (missing only `kind`) yields a 484-char message with 9 clauses, of which 8 are wrong — it demands `id`, `decision_ref`, and that `op` 'must be equal to constant'. `{op:'insert', text, kind, after:'c1'}` (the caller used `after` instead of `before`) yields a 689-char message containing 'must NOT have additional properties' six times without ever naming `after`, because that name lives in `e.params.additionalProperty` which validators.mjs:10 drops.
survivors.model_impact: This is the same class as the record_decision incident but worse, because the error text actively points at wrong fixes. A model reading 'must have required property id; must have required property decision_ref' on an insert will add id and decision_ref, which then trips additionalProperties on the insert branch and produces a different equally wrong wall. The `after`/`before` case is strictly unrecoverable from the message: no clause identifies which property is unexpected, so the model must guess by deletion. Each retry costs a full tool round-trip plus ~500-700 chars of misleading text in context.
survivors.failure_scenario: A model inserts a detour with `{op:'insert', text:'fix the flaky test', kind:'detour', after:'c2'}`. It receives 13 clauses naming no property, deletes `kind` on the theory that 'must NOT have additional properties' refers to it, and now gets the missing-kind wall instead. Two more retries follow before it strips down to the minimal shape.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced exactly. src/tools/schemas.mjs:72-109 is a three-branch oneOf, each branch with its own required list and additionalProperties:false. src/tools/registry.mjs:36 constructs `new Ajv({ allErrors: true })`; :46 makes ToolValidationError's message exactly formatValidationErrors output; src/schema/validators.mjs:9-11 maps errors to `${e.instancePath || '(root)'} ${e.message}` and discards e.params, which is where ajv puts additionalProperty/allowedValue. bin/ledger-server.mjs:57 serializes only {error, message}, so the structured errors attached at registry.mjs:64 never reach the model. My own run through callTool: `{op:'insert', text:'do the thing'}` produced a 484-character message with 9 semicolon-separated clauses, demanding required properties 'id' and 'decision_ref' and 'op must be equal to constant'; `{op:'insert', text, kind:'planned', after:'c1'}` produced 689 characters and 13 clauses containing 'must NOT have additional properties' six times, never naming `after`. Both figures match the finder's to the character.

survivors.title: open_risks[].text must contain a literal U+2014 em dash with surrounding spaces; the input schema says only minLength 1 and the 831-char description never mentions it
evidence: src/tools/spine-input.mjs:5 — `const RISK_SENTENCE = /^[^\n]+ — [^\n]+$/;` — the separator is U+2014 flanked by literal spaces
src/tools/spine-input.mjs:60-63 — every risk in the submitted array is tested and the first failure throws
src/tools/schemas.mjs:17 — `text: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` — no pattern, no hint
src/tools/update-thread.mjs:130 — the 831-char description covers scoping and caps at length and never mentions the risk sentence shape
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:30 — the rule exists only here: 'Shape each one as `<specific constraint or action> — <why, in plain words>`'
survivors.mechanism: normalizeRisks tests each risk.text against RISK_SENTENCE (spine-input.mjs:60) and throws a ToolError naming the required shape. Because the shape is expressed only in the handler and in a skill file, tools/list gives the model no way to comply on the first attempt. Verified against the live registry: 'ajv drops params - the offending key is never named' (hyphen) REFUSED; the same text with an en dash U+2013 REFUSED; only U+2014 accepted. The error message that teaches the fix itself contains the required em dash, so the model must copy an easily-confused character out of an error string.
survivors.model_impact: Guaranteed first-call failure for any caller not driven verbatim by the debrief skill, and a likely second failure since hyphen and en dash are the two most probable substitutions. Worse, the failure is all-or-nothing: update_thread bundles completion_criteria toggles with the spine patch (update-thread.mjs:112-122), and normalizeRisks throws at update-thread.mjs:42-46 before anything is written, so one malformed risk sentence discards the criteria toggles submitted in the same call. The model must resubmit the entire payload.
survivors.failure_scenario: A debrief call sets active_goal, next_step, six risks, twelve out_of_scope entries and flips four criteria to done. Risk three uses an en dash. The whole call is refused; the model resubmits the entire ~4KB payload, and if any other risk also uses the wrong dash it pays the round trip again.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced. src/tools/spine-input.mjs:5 is `const RISK_SENTENCE = /^[^\n]+ — [^\n]+$/;` — U+2014 flanked by literal spaces; :60-63 throws on the first risk that fails. src/tools/schemas.mjs:17 declares `text: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` with no pattern, and the 831-char description at src/tools/update-thread.mjs:130 (length measured via listTools) never mentions the sentence shape; the rule appears only at skills/debrief/SKILL.md:30. My probe against callTool: hyphen '-' REFUSED, en dash U+2013 REFUSED, em dash U+2014 ACCEPTED. The all-or-nothing claim also holds: src/tools/update-thread.mjs:113 computes the criteria toggles into an in-memory value, :120 calls patchSpine which throws at :42-46, and nothing is persisted until writeThread at :123 — so a malformed risk discards the criteria toggles submitted in the same call.

survivors.title: No tool in the set returns a thread record or resolves a slug to a ULID, and rebuild_index — the tool preflight calls to produce the roster — returns only counts
evidence: src/tools/registry.mjs:19-34 — the complete list of 14 tools; the only non-mutating reads are get_resume_brief (which itself mutates, see resume-brief-consumes-drift) and read_decision
src/tools/rebuild-index.mjs:4-7 — `const counts = await rebuildIndex(ctx.driver); return { counts };`
src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:45-54 — the resumable roster (id, slug, title, status, next_step, done, total, detours_open) is built here
src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:64-67 — the roster is written to index files via writeIndexFile and never returned
src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:69-76 — the return value is six integers
skills/preflight/SKILL.md:15-17 — step 1 calls rebuild_index 'so the resumable roster is current before you show anything', step 2 then says 'the SessionStart context surfaces this roster'
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:11 — 'Its `thread_id` is the active thread the SessionStart context surfaced'
survivors.mechanism: Twelve of the fourteen tools require a `thread_id` matching ULID_PATTERN (e.g. update-thread.mjs:136, transition-thread.mjs:58, record-decision.mjs:89). The only sources of a ULID inside the tool surface are the return values of open_thread / create_successor / bind_branch — i.e. tools that create work. rebuild_index computes the full resumable roster including every thread id (index/rebuild-index.mjs:45-54) but returns only `{threads, bindings, by_slug, by_branch, children, resumable}` counts (index/rebuild-index.mjs:69-76). The by-slug map is likewise written to a file (index/rebuild-index.mjs:64) and never exposed.
survivors.model_impact: The tool set is not self-sufficient: it depends on out-of-band SessionStart hook text for the single value every write needs. If that text is compacted away, if debrief runs in a long session, or if a subagent is dispatched to write the ledger, the model has no in-protocol way to recover a thread_id and cannot even discover that threads exist. The one tool it is instructed to call for the roster hands back six integers, which reads as a successful roster fetch and yields nothing usable — a model will plausibly print counts or hallucinate the roster.
survivors.failure_scenario: A long session compacts the SessionStart block. The user says 'wrap up'. The model calls rebuild_index, receives `{counts:{threads:7,resumable:3,...}}`, has no thread_id, and either asks the user for a 26-character ULID or calls open_thread and starts a duplicate thread.

verdict.correction: Two of the three claims hold: nothing in the tool surface maps a slug to a ULID (the by-slug map is written to a file at src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:64 and never returned), and rebuild_index returns six integers (src/tools/rebuild-index.mjs:5-6, src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:69-76). The title's 'No tool returns a thread record' is false as written — open_thread, create_successor, update_thread, transition_thread, amend_criteria, archive_thread and reopen all return the full record; the real gap is that none of them is reachable without already holding the ULID. And the MODEL IMPACT claim that 'the model has no in-protocol way to recover a thread_id' is refuted: record_decision writes `Thread-Id: <ULID>` into the decision frontmatter (src/tools/record-decision.mjs:22) and read_decision returns that markdown to the caller (src/tools/read-decision.mjs:14), so read_decision('0001') recovers a thread ULID with no out-of-band input; on a git backend reconcile also returns thread_ids (src/drift/classification.mjs:96, src/drift/disposition.mjs:25 via src/tools/reconcile.mjs:9). Accurate claim: there is no enumeration or slug-resolution tool, and the only in-protocol recovery paths are indirect and conditional.
verdict.reasoning: I read all 14 entries in src/tools/registry.mjs:19-34 and each tool's schema. Twelve require a ULID thread_id (e.g. update-thread.mjs:136, transition-thread.mjs:58, record-decision.mjs:89, get-resume-brief.mjs:46). rebuild_index and read_decision are the only argument-free / non-ULID entry points. hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:100-101 confirms the roster is supplied out of band by the SessionStart hook via formatRoster (hooks/lib/roster.mjs:23-36), matching skills/preflight/SKILL.md:17 — that dependency is real. rebuild_index's description does say 'return the counts' (src/tools/rebuild-index.mjs:11), so it is not misdescribed, only useless for the roster step preflight assigns it.

survivors.title: Every mutating tool echoes the complete thread record; a 43-byte spine edit returns ~1,570 tokens of data the caller already holds
evidence: src/tools/update-thread.mjs:125 — `return { thread: updated, recovery_degraded };`

src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:117, src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:47, src/tools/archive-thread.mjs:30, src/tools/reopen.mjs:32, src/tools/open-thread.mjs:21, src/tools/create-successor.mjs:24 — all return the full thread the same way
bin/ledger-server.mjs:54 — `JSON.stringify(result)` — the whole object goes into the model's context as text
src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:38-55 — the record carries 16 top-level fields including every criterion, every risk with refs, every decision and every out_of_scope entry
survivors.mechanism: Measured against the live registry with a realistic thread (8 criteria, 6 risks with refs, 9 decisions, 12 out_of_scope entries, capped-length scalars): one `update_thread` whose only change was a 43-character next_step returned 6,269 bytes (~1,570 tokens). Breakdown: completion_criteria 1,137 bytes, open_risks 1,855, key_decisions 873, out_of_scope 1,359 — roughly 5,200 bytes, ~83%, is content the caller submitted in earlier calls and did not touch in this one. Adding created_at/updated_at/id/slug/status boilerplate, ~97% of the payload is not new information.
survivors.model_impact: debrief performs several writes per session (append_session_event, one record_decision per straggler, amend_criteria, update_thread, transition_thread). At ~1,500 tokens each for the thread-returning ones, a single wrap-up burns 5-8k tokens re-reading state it just wrote. Since the same record is echoed several times in one turn with small diffs, the model must also reconcile near-identical blobs, which invites it to reason from a stale echo. A minimal acknowledgement (id, status, updated_at, and the fields that changed) would carry the same information.
survivors.failure_scenario: A debrief on a mature thread issues record_decision x3, amend_criteria x1, update_thread x1, transition_thread x1; six of those return the full record, costing roughly 8k tokens of pure echo in a context already near its limit.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and independently measured. Every mutating handler returns the full record: src/tools/update-thread.mjs:125, amend-criteria.mjs:117, transition-thread.mjs:47, archive-thread.mjs:30, reopen.mjs:32, open-thread.mjs:21, create-successor.mjs:24. bin/ledger-server.mjs:54 stringifies the whole result into the model's context. src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:38-55 lists 16 required top-level fields including every criterion, risk with refs, decision and out_of_scope entry. My own measurement on a realistic near-cap thread (8 criteria, 6 risks with 2 refs each, 9 decisions, 12 out_of_scope entries): an update_thread whose only change was a 43-character next_step returned 7,969 bytes (~2.0k tokens), of which completion_criteria 1,609, open_risks 2,689, key_decisions 1,216 and out_of_scope 1,419 — about 87% content the caller had submitted in earlier calls. The finder's 6,269-byte figure is the same phenomenon on a slightly smaller fixture.

survivors.title: transition_thread's done path has two hard preconditions stated in neither the schema nor the 95-char description, and the failure never names which criteria are outstanding
evidence: src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:60 — `closure_statement: { type: 'string' }` — optional in the schema
src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:56 — `required: ['thread_id', 'to_status']` only
src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:52 — description: 'Move a thread through the lifecycle FSM (DoD-gated for done); manage the active-thread pointer.' — 'DoD' is never expanded
src/model/dod.mjs:8-10 — 'every un-struck completion_criteria entry must be done:true for done' — no list of which ones
src/model/dod.mjs:11-14 — 'closure_statement must be non-empty for done'
src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:35-38 — the DoD check runs only after the FSM check, so the two failures surface one at a time
survivors.mechanism: canTransition passes, then blocked/abandoned guards are skipped, then checkDefinitionOfDone runs on the candidate (transition-thread.mjs:36). dod.mjs returns the first failure only. Verified against the live registry: a well-formed `transition_thread(to:'done')` on a thread with two open criteria returns 'every un-struck completion_criteria entry must be done:true for done'; after toggling both done, the same call returns 'closure_statement must be non-empty for done'. Two sequential failures, neither predictable from tools/list, and the first names no criterion id.
survivors.model_impact: A competent caller cannot construct a valid done transition from the tool surface alone — closure_statement looks optional. The model discovers the rule by failing twice. The criteria failure is worse: it does not say which criteria are outstanding, and there is no read tool to find out (see no-tool-returns-a-thread-or-roster), so unless the model still holds a prior echo of the thread it must guess criterion ids and toggle blindly through update_thread.
survivors.failure_scenario: Debrief step 6 transitions to done. Call 1 fails on criteria. The model has no thread record in context, calls update_thread with `[{id:'c1',done:true},{id:'c2',done:true}]` guessed from the criterion-id pattern, gets 'unknown completion_criteria id "c2"' because c2 was struck, and loops.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced. src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:56 requires only thread_id and to_status; :60 declares closure_statement as an optional plain string; the description at :52 is 95 characters (measured via listTools) and never expands 'DoD'. src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:35-38 runs checkDefinitionOfDone only after the FSM check, and src/model/dod.mjs returns the first failure only. My probe on a two-criterion thread: transition_thread(to_status:'done') returned 'every un-struck completion_criteria entry must be done:true for done' (src/model/dod.mjs:9) naming no criterion; after toggling both done, the same call returned 'closure_statement must be non-empty for done' (src/model/dod.mjs:13). Minor addition the finder omitted: there is a third reason at src/model/dod.mjs:5-7 when every criterion has been struck.

survivors.title: archive_thread and reopen fully duplicate transition_thread paths while disagreeing with it on validation: a whitespace-only reason is accepted by one and refused by the other
evidence: src/tools/archive-thread.mjs:42 — `reason: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` — ajv minLength does not trim
src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:6-8 — `nonEmpty` uses `value.trim().length > 0`
src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:23-25 — 'abandoned_reason is required to enter abandoned'
src/tools/archive-thread.mjs:12-28 vs src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:17-45 — same FSM check, same status write, same session event, same pointer clear

src/tools/reopen.mjs:18-31 vs src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:17-45 — reopen to 'active' does the same work; transition-thread.mjs:30 already sets `blocked_by: null` for any non-blocked target, which is reopen's only extra behavior (reopen.mjs:25)
src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:94 — `abandoned_reason: { type: ['string','null'] }` — no minLength at the write layer either
survivors.mechanism: Three tools cover overlapping regions of the same five-state FSM. Verified against the live registry: `archive_thread(reason:'   ')` succeeded and wrote a whitespace-only abandoned_reason plus the session event 'Archived (active -> abandoned):    '; `transition_thread(to:'abandoned', abandoned_reason:'   ')` was refused. The field is the same field on the same record; only the entry point differs, and thread.schema.mjs:94 does not backstop it.
survivors.model_impact: Three overlapping tools force a routing decision the descriptions do not resolve (archive_thread's 94-char description does not say it is transition_thread with a different parameter name). A model that picks the laxer door writes an empty abandonment reason, which is exactly the fact a future session needs to know why the thread died. Worse, a model that learns 'a blank reason is fine' from archive_thread will be refused by transition_thread for the same value and cannot tell why the same input is now invalid.
survivors.failure_scenario: A model abandons a thread through archive_thread with reason ' ' (a stray space from string assembly). The write succeeds; the ledger records an abandonment with no explanation and no error was ever raised.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced. src/tools/archive-thread.mjs:42 declares `reason: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` — ajv minLength counts characters, it does not trim — while src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:6-8 uses `value.trim().length > 0` and :23-25 refuses a blank abandoned_reason. src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:94 declares `abandoned_reason: { type: ['string','null'] }` with no minimum, so nothing backstops it at write. My probe: archive_thread(reason:'   ') was ACCEPTED and stored abandoned_reason "   "; transition_thread(to_status:'abandoned', abandoned_reason:'   ') was REFUSED. Redundancy also holds: archive-thread.mjs:12-28 duplicates the FSM check, status write, pointer clear and session event of transition-thread.mjs:17-45, and reopen.mjs:18-31 duplicates the to-'active' path whose only distinctive act (blocked_by: null, reopen.mjs:25) transition-thread.mjs:30 already performs for every non-blocked target.

survivors.title: record_decision accepts empty context, empty outcome and empty option strings, writing a structurally valid but content-free MADR record
evidence: src/tools/record-decision.mjs:92 — `context: { type: 'string' }` — no minLength
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:99 — `outcome: { type: 'string' }` — no minLength
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:95 — `{ type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }` — array option items have no minLength
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:8-14 — normalizeOptions filters empty lines only on the STRING branch (`.filter((line) => line.length > 0)`); the array branch at :9 returns the array untouched
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:45-47 — the only content check is `options.length === 0`, which an array of empty strings passes
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:16-40 — renderDecision interpolates the values with no further checks
survivors.mechanism: The union at record-decision.mjs:93-98 means the two branches get different treatment in the handler: a string is split, trimmed, de-bulleted and emptied-filtered (:10-13), while an array short-circuits at :9 and is emitted verbatim by :17. Verified: `record_decision(context:'', options:['',''], outcome:'')` succeeded and wrote a file whose Context and Outcome sections are empty and whose Options section is two bare '- ' bullets. title and slug are the only fields with real minimums.
survivors.model_impact: The union makes the SAME input semantically different depending on shape — `options: '\n\n'` is refused, `options: ['','']` is accepted — which is undiscoverable and re-runs the exact confusion of the known record_decision incident from the opposite direction. A model assembling a decision from a template with an unfilled slot writes a permanent, numbered, immutable-by-convention record containing nothing. Nothing downstream repairs it: the ref is linked into the spine (record-decision.mjs:70) and rendered in every briefing (briefing.mjs:125), so a future session sees a decision number, follows it via read_decision, and gets a blank page.
survivors.failure_scenario: A model records four straggler decisions in debrief; for the last one it has a title but its context variable resolved to ''. Decision 0004 is written with empty Context and Outcome, indexed into the spine, and surfaces in every future briefing as a real decision.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced. src/tools/record-decision.mjs:92 (`context: { type: 'string' }`) and :99 (`outcome: { type: 'string' }`) carry no minLength; :95 allows an array of strings with no per-item minLength. src/tools/record-decision.mjs:8-14: the array branch returns at :9 untouched, while only the string branch is split, trimmed, de-bulleted and emptied-filtered at :10-13. The only content guard is `options.length === 0` at :45-47, which an array of empty strings passes. src/tools/record-decision.mjs:16-40 interpolates the raw values, so Context and Outcome render as empty sections and Options renders as bare '- ' bullets. My probe: record_decision(context:'', options:['',''], outcome:'') was ACCEPTED and produced decision 0003; the semantically identical string form record_decision(options:'\n\n') was REFUSED with 'options must contain at least one option' — the same-input-different-shape asymmetry the finding names.

survivors.title: record_decision returns number and path but not ref, the only form every downstream tool accepts
evidence: src/tools/record-decision.mjs:67 — `const ref = `${nnnn}-${args.slug}`;` — computed in the handler
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:78 — `return { number: nnnn, path, recovery_degraded };` — ref is not returned
src/tools/schemas.mjs:70 and src/schema/patterns.mjs:8 — decision_ref must match `^[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9-]+$`
src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:90 and :101 — rewrite and strike require `decision_ref` in that form
src/tools/spine-input.mjs:76-79 — update_thread's key_decisions ref must be a member of knownDecisionRefs, which shared.mjs:12 builds as `${d.nnnn}-${d.slug}`
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:25 — instructs passing 'the `decision_ref` of the record' immediately after record_decision
survivors.mechanism: record_decision computes the canonical ref at line 67 and uses it at line 68-70 to link the spine, then discards it from the return at line 78. The caller receives `{number:'0001', path:'/abs/path/0001-slug.md', recovery_degraded:false}` (verified) and must reconstruct `0001-slug` by concatenating `number` with the slug it originally sent — or parse it out of the absolute path. Neither reconstruction is described anywhere.
survivors.model_impact: The debrief flow calls record_decision and then immediately needs decision_ref for amend_criteria (SKILL.md:25). A model that passes the returned `number` alone gets `must match pattern "^[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9-]+$"`, and a model that passes the returned `path` gets the same. Both are round trips spent rediscovering a value the server already computed. The `path` field, meanwhile, is an absolute filesystem path the MCP caller cannot act on — it is the one field returned that has no use.
survivors.failure_scenario: A model records a decision, receives `{number:'0003', path:'/Users/x/.../0003-plan-was-wrong.md'}`, calls `amend_criteria(operations:[{op:'strike', id:'c3', decision_ref:'0003'}])`, and is refused by the pattern; it then guesses `decision_ref: path` and is refused again.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced. src/tools/record-decision.mjs:67 computes `const ref = `${nnnn}-${args.slug}`;` and uses it at :68-70 to link the spine, but :78 returns `{ number: nnnn, path, recovery_degraded }`. My probe's actual return value was {"number":"0001","path":"/var/.../decisions/0001-long-title.md","recovery_degraded":false} — no ref. Every downstream consumer wants the ref form: src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:90 and :101 require decision_ref matching src/schema/patterns.mjs:8 '^[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9-]+$'; src/tools/spine-input.mjs:76 requires membership in the set built by src/tools/shared.mjs:12 as `${d.nnnn}-${d.slug}`. skills/debrief/SKILL.md:25 instructs passing that decision_ref immediately after recording. The absolute `path` is likewise unusable by an MCP client.

survivors.title: spine.key_decisions[].title is free text never checked against the decision file it references, so the briefing can attribute wording to a decision that does not contain it
evidence: src/tools/spine-input.mjs:74-83 — normalizeDecisions verifies only `knownRefs.has(decision.ref)`; the title is passed through at :82 `return { ref: decision.ref, title: decision.title, scope };`
src/tools/shared.mjs:10-13 — knownDecisionRefs returns a Set of ref strings only; the file's real title is never read
src/render/briefing.mjs:125 — the briefing renders the SPINE's title next to the decision number, not the file's
src/tools/schemas.mjs:29 — decisionInputItem `title: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }`
survivors.mechanism: update_thread's decision path resolves existence by ref (spine-input.mjs:76) and then trusts the caller's title verbatim. The decision file's actual `# {nnnn}. {title}` heading (record-decision.mjs:23) is never consulted. Verified: after record_decision wrote decision 0001 titled 'Use event sourcing for billing', an update_thread submitting the same ref with title 'Completely unrelated wording' was accepted, and both titles are now stored against ref 0001.
survivors.model_impact: The briefing's DECIDED ON THIS STEP block is the model's index into the decision corpus. If its labels can drift from the records they point at, a future session reads a title, decides the decision is irrelevant, and never calls read_decision — or reads a title, believes it, and states something the record contradicts. This is the same failure the audit itself was commissioned over: a plausible label believed instead of the source.
survivors.failure_scenario: A model re-scopes a decision and paraphrases its title from memory. The briefing now shows '0007 — use Postgres advisory locks'; the actual record says the team rejected advisory locks in favour of a queue. The next session reads the briefing line and implements advisory locks.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced. src/tools/spine-input.mjs:74-83 checks only `knownRefs.has(decision.ref)` and returns `{ ref, title: decision.title, scope }` at :82 — the caller's title is passed through. src/tools/shared.mjs:10-13 builds knownRefs from filenames only (`${d.nnnn}-${d.slug}`); the decision file's actual `# {nnnn}. {title}` heading (src/tools/record-decision.mjs:25) is never read. src/render/briefing.mjs:125 renders the spine's title beside the number. My probe: after record_decision wrote 0002 titled 'Use event sourcing for billing', update_thread submitting ref 0002-event-sourcing with title 'Completely unrelated wording' was ACCEPTED, leaving both wordings stored against the same ref.

survivors.title: Every write tool double-writes on retry after an ambiguous failure, and no description says so
evidence: src/tools/record-decision.mjs:56 — `const nnnn = await driver.nextDecisionNumber();` — src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:189-199 returns max+1 from the directory listing, so a retry mints a new number
src/model/binding.mjs:17 — `id: typeof options.id === 'string' ? options.id : newUlid()` — bind_branch (src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:12) never checks for an existing binding on the same repo/branch
src/model/thread.mjs:63 — same newUlid for open_thread and create_successor
src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:34-36 — `if (thread.slug && !(thread.slug in bySlug))` — first thread wins, so a duplicate-slug thread is unreachable through by-slug
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:244-249 — append_session_event's filename is derived from the millisecond timestamp, so a retry lands on a new path
src/tools/append-session-event.mjs:17, src/tools/open-thread.mjs:26, src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:21, src/tools/record-decision.mjs:83 — none of the four descriptions mentions retry safety
survivors.mechanism: Verified against the live registry: two identical record_decision calls produced 0009-retry-me and 0010-retry-me, both linked into the spine; two identical bind_branch calls produced two distinct binding ids, and rebuild_index's by-branch entry for 'r feat/x' listed both; two identical open_thread calls produced two threads with slug 'same-title', and by-slug resolves only the first, leaving the second reachable by ULID alone; two identical append_session_event calls produced two distinct session files.
survivors.model_impact: MCP calls can fail ambiguously — transport error, timeout, a malformed emission like the one that started this audit. The model's default recovery is to retry. For eight of the fourteen tools that silently creates a second record. Duplicate decisions are the most damaging: they occupy consecutive numbers, both appear in the spine, and both render in briefings, so a future session sees two decisions where one was made. Duplicate threads are the most confusing: the second is invisible to slug lookup, so it never appears in the roster path the skills use.
survivors.failure_scenario: record_decision returns a transport error after writing the file. The model retries. Decisions 0009 and 0010 are now identical records, both in spine.key_decisions, both rendered, and no tool can delete either.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced for all four demonstrated tools. src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:189-199 returns max+1 from the directory listing, so my two identical record_decision calls minted 0001 and 0002 and the thread spine ended up holding both refs. src/model/binding.mjs:17 mints a fresh ULID per call and src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:6-17 never looks for an existing repo/branch binding — my two identical bind_branch calls produced distinct ids and rebuild_index counted bindings:2 under one by_branch key (src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:58-62 pushes into an array). src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:244-249 derives the session filename from the millisecond timestamp — my two identical append_session_event calls returned distinct paths. src/model/thread.mjs:63 mints a fresh ULID for open_thread — my two identical open_thread calls produced two threads with slug 'same-title', and src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:34-36 ('first wins') mapped by-slug to the first only. None of the four descriptions mentions retry behavior. One caveat: the MODEL IMPACT's 'eight of the fourteen tools' is not derivable from the code — I count six non-idempotent write tools (the four above plus create_successor and amend_criteria's insert, src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:60-70), with get_resume_brief non-idempotent in the separate sense of the first finding.

survivors.title: recovery_degraded rides on every write return with no documented meaning, and it is how an uncommitted write reports success
evidence: src/tools/shared.mjs:15-17 — `isRecoveryDegraded` returns `commitResult.degraded === true`
src/tools/shared.mjs:19-23 — commitAndReindex attaches it to every write tool's return
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:298-300 — `} catch { return degradedCommit(); }` — a failed git commit is swallowed and reported as `{committed:false, sha:null, empty:false, degraded:true}`
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:51-53 — degradedCommit's shape
src/tools/registry.mjs:19-34 — not one of the 14 descriptions mentions recovery_degraded
survivors.mechanism: Each mutating handler returns `recovery_degraded` (e.g. update-thread.mjs:125, open-thread.mjs:21, record-decision.mjs:78). Its true value means the record reached disk via atomicWrite but the recovery repository did not commit it — local-driver.mjs:286-297 threw and line 299 converted the throw into a degraded result rather than an error. The tool still reports success.
survivors.model_impact: The model receives a boolean on every write whose semantics appear in no description and no schema. It cannot tell whether to warn the user, retry, or ignore it — and retrying is the wrong answer, since the write itself succeeded and a retry double-writes (see write-side-not-idempotent-undocumented). Meanwhile the one condition it flags, 'your data is not committed and will not survive', is exactly the condition the model would want to surface. It costs tokens on every call and conveys nothing actionable.
survivors.failure_scenario: A permission problem breaks the recovery repo. Every debrief write returns success with recovery_degraded:true. The model reports a clean handoff; nothing was committed, and the next session's git-backed reads find an empty ledger.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived. src/tools/shared.mjs:15-17 defines isRecoveryDegraded as `commitResult.degraded === true`; :19-23 attaches it to every commitAndReindex return, and I confirmed the field appears in the return of 12 tools by reading each return statement (update-thread.mjs:125, open-thread.mjs:21, record-decision.mjs:78, bind-branch.mjs:16, append-session-event.mjs:12, transition-thread.mjs:47, amend-criteria.mjs:117, archive-thread.mjs:30, reopen.mjs:32, create-successor.mjs:24, reconcile.mjs:9). src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:298-300 swallows a failed git commit into degradedCommit(), whose shape is at :51-53. No description in src/tools/registry.mjs:19-34 mentions the field — I dumped all 14 descriptions via listTools and none contains the string. One nuance the finder missed: degraded is also returned when no recovery repo exists at all (src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:280-282), so the flag conflates 'commit failed' with 'this ledger has no recovery repo', which makes it even less actionable.

survivors.title: The decision number's digit arity disagrees across three layers; at decision 10000 record_decision writes an orphan file and then fails permanently
evidence: src/schema/patterns.mjs:8 — `DECISION_REF_PATTERN = '^[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9-]+$'` — exactly four digits
src/tools/read-decision.mjs:25 — `nnnn: { type: 'string', pattern: '^[0-9]{4,}$' }` — four or more
src/render/briefing.mjs:7 — `DECISION_NUMBER = /^([0-9]{4,})-/` — four or more
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:199 — `return String(max + 1).padStart(4, '0');` — pads to four but does not cap
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:66 — `await driver.writeDecision(nnnn, args.slug, markdown)` runs BEFORE the thread write at :76
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:203-205 — writeDecision accepts any `^[0-9]+$`
survivors.mechanism: nextDecisionNumber returns a zero-padded string with no upper bound, so at 10000 it returns '10000'. record-decision.mjs:66 writes the file, then :67 forms ref '10000-slug', then :70 puts it in the spine, then :76 calls writeThread, where local-driver.mjs:148 assertValidThread rejects it against thread.schema.mjs:28. Verified by stubbing nextDecisionNumber: the call failed with `/spine/key_decisions/0/ref must match pattern "^[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9-]+$"` and the file `10000-ten-thousand.md` was left on disk. Since nextDecisionNumber counts files, that orphan raises the next number too, so every subsequent record_decision fails identically while leaving another orphan.
survivors.model_impact: Unreachable in practice at 10k decisions, but it demonstrates the reachable ordering flaw: record_decision commits the file to storage before validating the record it must also update, so any writeThread rejection leaves an orphan decision file that no tool can remove and that permanently advances the counter. The error text names a schema path the model has no way to act on, and retrying makes it strictly worse.
survivors.failure_scenario: Any future change that widens a decision slug or ref beyond the write-layer pattern reproduces this immediately: file written, thread write refused, orphan left, counter advanced, and the model's natural retry produces a second orphan.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced by stubbing the driver. src/schema/patterns.mjs:8 fixes exactly four digits; src/tools/read-decision.mjs:25 accepts '^[0-9]{4,}$'; src/render/briefing.mjs:7 accepts '^([0-9]{4,})-'; src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:199 returns `String(max + 1).padStart(4, '0')` with no upper bound; src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:203-205 accepts any '^[0-9]+$'. Ordering: src/tools/record-decision.mjs:66 writes the file before the thread write at :76. My probe with nextDecisionNumber stubbed to '10000': the call failed with `SchemaValidationError: Thread failed schema validation: /spine/key_decisions/2/ref must match pattern "^[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9-]+$"`, the file 10000-ten-thousand.md was left on disk, and the next nextDecisionNumber() returned '10001' — the counter permanently advanced by the orphan, exactly as claimed.

survivors.title: criterion `kind` is optional with a silent default in open_thread/create_successor but required in amend_criteria's insert branch
evidence: src/tools/schemas.mjs:48-56 — criteriaCreateItem `required: ['text']`; `kind` optional
src/model/thread.mjs:31 — `kind: item.kind ?? DEFAULT_CRITERION_KIND` — silently defaults to 'planned'
src/tools/schemas.mjs:79 — the insert branch of criteriaAmendOperation: `required: ['op', 'text', 'kind']`
src/tools/open-thread.mjs:36 and src/tools/create-successor.mjs:37 use criteriaCreateItem; src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:129 uses criteriaAmendOperation
survivors.mechanism: The same conceptual field carries two different requiredness rules depending on which tool creates the criterion. open_thread applies a default in the model layer (thread.mjs:31); amend_criteria's insert has no default and makes it required at the schema layer. Nothing in either description mentions the difference.
survivors.model_impact: A model that has successfully created threads without specifying `kind` will omit it on its first amend_criteria insert, and that omission lands it in the oneOf error wall (see amend-criteria-oneof-nonconvergent), where the message demands `id` and `decision_ref` rather than `kind`. The two defects compound: an easy mistake produces the least diagnosable error in the system.
survivors.failure_scenario: Verified: `amend_criteria(operations:[{op:'insert', text:'do the thing'}])` — missing only `kind` — returns a 484-char, 9-clause message whose second through eighth clauses point at fields that do not belong on an insert.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived. src/tools/schemas.mjs:48-56 (criteriaCreateItem) requires only ['text'] and leaves kind optional; src/model/thread.mjs:31 silently applies `kind: item.kind ?? DEFAULT_CRITERION_KIND` where DEFAULT_CRITERION_KIND is 'planned' (thread.mjs:8). src/tools/schemas.mjs:79 makes the insert branch `required: ['op', 'text', 'kind']` with no default. src/tools/open-thread.mjs:36 and src/tools/create-successor.mjs:37 use criteriaCreateItem; src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:129 uses criteriaAmendOperation. My probe confirmed the default: open_thread with three criteria and no kind produced c1/planned,c2/planned,c3/planned. The compounding claim also holds — my omitted-kind insert produced the 484-char oneOf wall whose second and third clauses demand 'id' and 'decision_ref'.

survivors.title: create_successor silently drops the slug, vcs_ref and external_refs that open_thread accepts, with no way to set them afterwards
evidence: src/tools/open-thread.mjs:31-39 — accepts title, slug, parent_id, predecessor_id, completion_criteria, vcs_ref, external_refs
src/tools/create-successor.mjs:34-38 — accepts only predecessor_id, title, completion_criteria, with `additionalProperties: false` at :32
src/tools/create-successor.mjs:15-20 — the newThread call passes only title, completion_criteria, predecessor_id, parent_id

src/tools/registry.mjs:19-34 — no tool updates slug, vcs_ref or external_refs after creation; update_thread's schema (update-thread.mjs:135-151) covers only thread_id, spine, replace_scopes, completion_criteria
survivors.mechanism: create_successor's schema forbids the extra fields via additionalProperties:false, and newThread then derives the slug from the title (thread.mjs:53-57) and sets vcs_ref null / external_refs [] (thread.mjs:70-71). No later tool can change any of the three.
survivors.model_impact: A model that used external_refs (ticket links) when opening the original thread and reaches for the same on the successor gets `must NOT have additional properties` — a message that, as elsewhere, does not name the rejected property. Having discovered the restriction, it has no remedy: the successor is permanently without its ticket link, and the model may work around it by calling open_thread instead, losing the predecessor linkage the tool exists to create.
survivors.failure_scenario: A model opens a successor and passes `external_refs:[{system:'linear', id:'ENG-412', url:'...'}]`. The call is refused with an unnamed additional-property error; the model drops the field, and the successor thread has no link back to the ticket.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived. src/tools/open-thread.mjs:31-39 accepts title, slug, parent_id, predecessor_id, completion_criteria, vcs_ref and external_refs. src/tools/create-successor.mjs:30-38 sets additionalProperties:false at :32 and declares only predecessor_id, title and completion_criteria; :15-20 passes only title, completion_criteria, predecessor_id and parent_id into newThread, which then derives the slug from the title (src/model/thread.mjs:53-56) and sets vcs_ref null / external_refs [] (src/model/thread.mjs:70-71). I read all 14 tool schemas: none of them can update slug, vcs_ref or external_refs after creation — update_thread's schema (src/tools/update-thread.mjs:135-151) covers only thread_id, spine, replace_scopes and completion_criteria.

survivors.title: replace_scopes naming a scope that holds nothing is silently accepted as a no-op, so a failed retirement reports success
evidence: src/tools/spine-input.mjs:26-34 — normalizeScopeList validates each scope against the regex only; no existence check against stored items or against the thread's criteria
src/tools/update-thread.mjs:18-27 — replaceScopedItems filters `existing` by the replaced set; if nothing matches, `carried` equals `existing` and the result is unchanged
src/tools/update-thread.mjs:29-34 — assertNamesAScope guards only the inverse case (an empty submitted array backed by no replace_scopes entry)
src/tools/update-thread.mjs:130 — description promises 'every named scope is replaced by whatever this call submits for it, down to nothing'
survivors.mechanism: replace_scopes is the only mechanism for retiring items, and it is keyed on a scope string that is never checked for existence. Verified: `update_thread(replace_scopes:{open_risks:['c42']})` on a thread whose only risk is scoped c99 was accepted and left the risk in place; the return reported success with one risk still stored.
survivors.model_impact: Retirement is the operation with no error path. A model that mistypes a scope, or names the scope it believes a risk lives under rather than the one it actually lives under, is told the call succeeded and reasonably concludes the risk is retired. The stale risk keeps appearing in future briefings, and the model that already 'retired' it will not try again. Combined with scope-accepts-nonexistent-criterion, a risk can be filed under an unreachable scope and then be un-retirable by any scope the model would guess.
survivors.failure_scenario: A model retires a resolved risk by naming scope 'c3' in replace_scopes, but the risk was filed under 'thread'. The call succeeds, the risk survives, and every later briefing repeats a constraint that no longer holds.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced. src/tools/spine-input.mjs:26-34 validates each scope against the regex only, with no check against stored items or the thread's criteria. src/tools/update-thread.mjs:18-27: when nothing in `existing` matches the replaced set, `carried` equals `existing` and the result is unchanged. src/tools/update-thread.mjs:29-34 (assertNamesAScope) guards only the inverse case — an empty submitted array with no backing replace_scopes entry. The description at :130 promises 'every named scope is replaced by whatever this call submits for it, down to nothing'. My probe: `update_thread(replace_scopes:{open_risks:['c42']})` on a thread whose risks were scoped c99 and thread was ACCEPTED and left both risks in place.

survivors.title: The 14 descriptions spend their budget unevenly: update_thread's 831 chars omit two rules that guarantee failure, while transition_thread's 95 chars omit a required field
evidence: Measured via listTools() on the live registry: description chars per tool — open_thread 111, bind_branch 77, append_session_event 87, record_decision 143, transition_thread 95, update_thread 831, amend_criteria 471, archive_thread 94, create_successor 86, reopen 99, reconcile 94, rebuild_index 87, get_resume_brief 168, read_decision 110; total 2,553 chars. Full tools/list payload 9,405 chars (~2.4k tokens per session).
src/tools/update-thread.mjs:130 — 831 chars, entirely about scope-replacement semantics and a bare assertion that 'Caps are enforced on the fields this call submits'
src/model/caps.mjs:1-12 — the caps it declines to name: active_goal 200, next_step 500, last_session 300, risk text 300, risk refs 8 x 200, decision title 120, out_of_scope 20 x 300
src/tools/schemas.mjs:141-146 (via update-thread.mjs:137-148) — none of those fields carries maxLength in the input schema either
src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:52 — 95 chars, does not mention closure_statement or the criteria precondition
survivors.mechanism: The total description budget (~640 tokens across 14 tools) is not the problem; its allocation is. update_thread's description devotes ~700 of its 831 chars to scope replacement while omitting the risk em-dash shape (spine-input.mjs:5), the out_of_scope replace-all asymmetry (update-thread.mjs:58), the out_of_scope-vs-decision-title dedup rule (spine-input.mjs:99-113), and every numeric cap. None of those caps appears as maxLength in the input schema either, so the model cannot recover them from the schema.
survivors.model_impact: Every cap in caps.mjs is discoverable only by exceeding it — a full failed round trip, with a full mega-payload resubmission, per cap. A 400-character next_step (well within a natural summary length) is refused with 'spine.next_step exceeds 500 chars' only after the model has already written the whole spine patch. Adding maxLength to the input schema would let a schema-aware caller truncate before sending, at zero description cost.
survivors.failure_scenario: A model writes a 260-char active_goal (the cap is 200) alongside six risks, twelve out_of_scope entries and four criteria toggles. The call is refused for the goal alone; the model must reassemble and resend the entire ~4KB payload.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and independently measured. My own listTools() dump reproduced every number exactly: open_thread 111, bind_branch 77, append_session_event 87, record_decision 143, transition_thread 95, update_thread 831, amend_criteria 471, archive_thread 94, create_successor 86, reopen 99, reconcile 94, rebuild_index 87, get_resume_brief 168, read_decision 110; total 2,553 chars; full tools/list payload 9,405 chars. src/model/caps.mjs:1-12 declares the numeric caps that no description names. The omissions are real: src/tools/spine-input.mjs:5 (risk em dash), src/tools/update-thread.mjs:58 (out_of_scope replace-all), src/tools/spine-input.mjs:99-113 (the restated-decision dedup rule). One citation slip that does not change the substance: the finder cites 'src/tools/schemas.mjs:141-146' for the absent maxLengths, but schemas.mjs is only 122 lines — the correct location is src/tools/update-thread.mjs:141-146 (active_goal/next_step/last_session/open_risks/key_decisions/out_of_scope, none with maxLength), plus src/tools/schemas.mjs:17 and :29 for risk text and decision title. Note that criterion text IS capped in the input schema (src/tools/schemas.mjs:53), which shows the omission is an inconsistency rather than a house style.

survivors.title: record_decision writes the decision file to disk before validating the thread record, so every failed call leaves an orphan numbered decision the model believes was never created, and each retry mints a new number
evidence: src/tools/record-decision.mjs:66 — `const path = await driver.writeDecision(nnnn, args.slug, markdown);` (file hits disk here)
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:76 — `await driver.writeThread(updated);` (first validation of the thread record happens here, ten lines later)
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:148 — `assertValidThread(thread);` inside writeThread, the throw site
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:189-199 — nextDecisionNumber scans the decisions directory and returns `String(max + 1).padStart(4, '0')`, so an orphan file permanently advances the counter
src/tools/shared.mjs:10-13 — `knownDecisionRefs` builds its Set from `driver.listDecisions()`, i.e. from files on disk, with no cross-check against any thread spine
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:286 — `args(['add', '-A'])` in commit, so a later successful tool sweeps the orphans into a commit under an unrelated message
survivors.mechanism: record_decision has no transaction boundary. It computes `nnnn` (local-driver.mjs:189), writes `decisions/<nnnn>-<slug>.md` via `driver.writeDecision` (record-decision.mjs:66), and only afterwards calls `driver.writeThread` (record-decision.mjs:76), which is the first and only point where `assertValidThread` (local-driver.mjs:148) runs. Any throw at or after line 76 aborts the handler and surfaces an error to the model, but the markdown file is already committed to the filesystem and there is no compensating unlink anywhere in the module. Because `nextDecisionNumber` derives the next number by scanning the directory (local-driver.mjs:190-199), the orphan raises the counter, so an identical retry produces a *different* number rather than overwriting. I reproduced this against a real LocalDriver: a thread whose stored record fails schema validation caused three identical record_decision retries to leave `0001-same-decision.md`, `0002-same-decision.md`, `0003-same-decision.md` on disk while the model received three errors. `knownDecisionRefs` (shared.mjs:10-13) reads the directory, so all three phantom refs subsequently validate as real `decision_ref` values in amend_criteria and resolve in read_decision. The next successful tool call runs `commitAndReindex`, whose LocalDriver commit stages with `git add -A` (local-driver.mjs:286), committing the orphans permanently under e.g. `chore(ledger): update <slug>`.
survivors.model_impact: The model is told the decision was not recorded and retries — the single most natural response to a tool error, and exactly what happened in the known incident. Each retry silently creates another permanent, numbered, committed decision record. The ledger then contains N duplicate MADR records that no thread spine references, the decision numbering has permanent gaps the model cannot explain, and a later session's `read_decision 0002` returns a record the model has no memory of authoring. The model will also confidently report 'no decisions were recorded this session' in its hand-off summary while three exist on disk. This is silent creation of false persistent data with no signal available to the caller.
survivors.failure_scenario: Thread record is a v1 or partial-spine record (readable, unwritable — see stored-record-readable-but-unwritable). Model calls record_decision(slug:'same-decision'); handler writes decisions/0001-same-decision.md, then writeThread throws SchemaValidationError; model sees an error, retries the identical call twice more. End state: three committed decision files 0001/0002/0003, zero spine links, model believes zero decisions exist.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived by reading and then reproduced live. Ordering: `const nnnn = await driver.nextDecisionNumber()` at src/tools/record-decision.mjs:56, `const path = await driver.writeDecision(nnnn, args.slug, markdown)` at src/tools/record-decision.mjs:66, `await driver.writeThread(updated)` at src/tools/record-decision.mjs:76. The only validation of the thread record is `assertValidThread(thread)` at src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:148, inside writeThread. There is no try/catch and no unlink anywhere in src/tools/record-decision.mjs. src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:189-199 derives the next number by scanning the decisions directory (`String(max + 1).padStart(4, '0')`, line 199), so an orphan permanently advances the counter. I checked for a guard upstream and found none: the only pre-write checks are the empty-options check (src/tools/record-decision.mjs:44-47), the thread-exists check (:48-51) and assertWritableScope (:52-55) — all of which run BEFORE line 66, so a failure there leaves nothing behind. Live reproduction against a real LocalDriver with a v1 stored record: three identical record_decision calls each returned `SchemaValidationError: Thread failed schema validation: /spine must have required property 'active_goal'; /spine must have required property 'next_step'` while the decisions directory ended up holding `0001-same-decision.md`, `0002-same-decision.md`, `0003-same-decision.md`. Downstream claims also hold on my own reading: `knownDecisionRefs` builds its Set purely from `driver.listDecisions()` (src/tools/shared.mjs:10-13), and listDecisions reads directory entries (src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:226-235), so the orphans become valid `decision_ref` values for amend_criteria's requireDecision (src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:7-13) and resolvable by read_decision (src/tools/read-decision.mjs:5-14); the LocalDriver commit stages with `args(['add', '-A'])` at src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:286, so a later successful tool's commitAndReindex sweeps them in. One precision note: the TITLE's phrase 'every failed call' is looser than the code supports — only a failure at or after src/tools/record-decision.mjs:66 orphans a file — but the finding's own MECHANISM states this correctly ('Any throw at or after line 76'), so the finding holds as written. Severity stays critical: silent creation of permanent, numbered, git-committed false records with zero signal available to the caller.

survivors.title: readThread upcasts without validating while writeThread validates, so a stored record that fails threadSchema reads and briefs fine but hard-blocks transition_thread, amend_criteria and record_decision with an error naming a field none of those tools accept
evidence: src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:143-145 — `async readThread(id) { return upcastThread(await readJsonOrNull(...)); }` — no assertValidThread on the read path
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:147-148 — `async writeThread(thread) { assertValidThread(thread);` — validation only on write

src/schema/upcast.mjs:67-74 — upcastSpine spreads `...rest` and only backfills `last_session`, `open_risks`, `key_decisions`, `out_of_scope`; `active_goal` and `next_step` are passed through untouched and are NOT defaulted
src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:99 — spine `required: ['active_goal', 'next_step', 'last_session', 'open_risks', 'key_decisions', 'out_of_scope']`

src/schema/validators.mjs:16 — `super(`${recordKind} failed schema validation: ${formatValidationErrors(errors)}`)` — message carries the record kind but no tool name and no statement that the offending record is the stored one
src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:53-63 — inputSchema has no spine property, so no argument can repair the record
src/model/thread.mjs:37-46 — emptySpine() proves newThread always writes both fields, so only upcast or hand-edited records reach this state
survivors.mechanism: `readThread` (local-driver.mjs:143-145) runs `upcastThread` but never validates. `upcastSpine` (upcast.mjs:67-74) backfills four spine fields and passes `active_goal`/`next_step` through via `...rest`, so a v1 record that lacks them yields an upcast object that violates `threadSchema`'s spine `required` list (thread.schema.mjs:99). Every read-only path succeeds: I confirmed `get_resume_brief` renders normally, because briefing.mjs reads spine fields defensively. But every write path calls `driver.writeThread`, which calls `assertValidThread` (local-driver.mjs:148), throwing `SchemaValidationError: Thread failed schema validation: /spine must have required property 'active_goal'; /spine must have required property 'next_step'`. I confirmed this error from update_thread, amend_criteria, transition_thread and record_decision on the same record. The message (validators.mjs:16) is built from `formatValidationErrors`, which emits only `instancePath + message`, so it names `/spine` — a path that looks exactly like a caller-supplied argument. It carries no tool name (unlike ToolValidationError at registry.mjs:46), no statement that the failing document is the stored record rather than the call arguments, and no hint that only update_thread has a `spine` parameter capable of repairing it. transition_thread's schema (transition-thread.mjs:53-63) has no spine field at all, so no retry of that call can ever succeed. I verified the repair path: `update_thread` supplying BOTH active_goal and next_step fixes the record, after which transition_thread succeeds.
survivors.model_impact: The model reads `/spine must have required property 'active_goal'` from a transition_thread call whose schema has no spine parameter. Its options are all wrong: retry unchanged (never succeeds), add a spine argument (rejected by additionalProperties:false), or conclude the thread_id is bad. There is nothing in the message pointing at the actual fix — a separate update_thread call supplying two specific fields.
