This is an unrecoverable retry loop for three of the four write tools, and it is the direct upstream cause of the orphan-decision-file defect above.
survivors.failure_scenario: A ledger written by schema v1 (or restored/hand-edited) has spine {open_risks:[],key_decisions:[],out_of_scope:[]}. Session start: get_resume_brief renders a clean briefing. Debrief: transition_thread(to_status:'paused') -> SchemaValidationError naming /spine/active_goal. Model retries, then tries record_decision, then amend_criteria — all fail identically, and record_decision leaves orphan files each time.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced. src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:143-145 is `async readThread(id) { return upcastThread(await readJsonOrNull(...)); }` — no validation. src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:147-148 is `async writeThread(thread) { assertValidThread(thread);` — validation only on write. src/schema/upcast.mjs:61-75 (upcastSpine) spreads `...rest` and explicitly backfills only last_session (:70), open_risks (:71), key_decisions (:72), out_of_scope (:73); active_goal and next_step are never defaulted. src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:99 requires all six. src/model/thread.mjs:37-46 (emptySpine) supplies both, so newly created threads are safe — the exposure is upcast or hand-edited records, exactly as claimed. Live reproduction on a v1 record whose spine had no active_goal/next_step: get_resume_brief rendered normally ('# PREFLIGHT BRIEFING — T / active · 0 of 1 done · ...'), while transition_thread, update_thread and record_decision each returned `SchemaValidationError: Thread failed schema validation: /spine must have required property 'active_goal'; /spine must have required property 'next_step'`. I verified the message construction myself at src/schema/validators.mjs:16 and the projection at :10 — instancePath + message only, no tool name, no statement that the offending document is the stored record; contrast ToolValidationError at src/tools/registry.mjs:46 which does prefix the tool name. I verified transition_thread's inputSchema (src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:53-63) has no spine property and `additionalProperties: false`, so no argument to that tool can repair the record. I verified the repair path the finder claims: `update_thread({spine:{active_goal:'g',next_step:'n'}})` succeeded, and transition_thread then succeeded on the same thread. Every element of the finding survives.

survivors.title: A legacy-scoped key_decision produced by the v1 upcast can never be retired: naming 'legacy' in replace_scopes is rejected by a bare regex message, and naming any other scope returns success while silently leaving the entry in place
evidence: src/schema/upcast.mjs:53-59 — upcastDecision returns `{ ref, title, scope: LEGACY_SCOPE }`, so every v1 key_decision lands with scope 'legacy'
src/schema/patterns.mjs:22 — `SCOPE_PATTERN = '^(c[1-9][0-9]*|thread|legacy)$'` (storage allows legacy)
src/schema/patterns.mjs:24 — `WRITABLE_SCOPE_PATTERN = '^(c[1-9][0-9]*|thread)$'` (every input schema forbids it)
src/tools/schemas.mjs:34-46 — replaceScopesInput's scopeList items use WRITABLE_SCOPE_PATTERN, so ajv rejects 'legacy' at registry.mjs:63 before any handler runs

src/tools/spine-input.mjs:12-19 — assertWritableScope carries the only human-readable explanation ('scope "legacy" is set only by the v1 upcast and is refused on every write path') and is unreachable for every caller-supplied scope
src/tools/update-thread.mjs:18-27 — replaceScopedItems filters `existing` by `replaced.has(item.scope)`; a legacy-scoped item is never in `replaced`, so it is always carried
src/tools/update-thread.mjs:125 — `return { thread: updated, recovery_degraded };` — a normal success result
survivors.mechanism: upcastDecision (upcast.mjs:53-59) stamps every v1 key_decision with scope 'legacy'. Storage permits it (SCOPE_PATTERN, patterns.mjs:22) but every input schema forbids it (WRITABLE_SCOPE_PATTERN, patterns.mjs:24, used by schemas.mjs:34-46). Retirement is only possible through `replace_scopes`, whose items are pattern-checked by ajv at registry.mjs:63. I verified all three attempts: `replace_scopes:{key_decisions:['legacy']}` -> `ToolValidationError: /replace_scopes/key_decisions/0 must match pattern "^(c[1-9][0-9]*|thread)$"`, a message that never explains that 'legacy' exists, is real, is in the record, and is deliberately unwritable. `replace_scopes:{key_decisions:['thread']}` and `['c1']` both returned SUCCESS with the legacy entry still present in the returned thread, because replaceScopedItems (update-thread.mjs:18-27) only drops carried items whose scope is in the `replaced` set. The explanatory ToolError in assertWritableScope (spine-input.mjs:12-19) is dead code for caller-supplied scopes: ajv rejects first in every case, and the only other caller passes `resolveWriteScope(thread)`, which returns a criterion id or 'thread' (selection.mjs:20-23) and never 'legacy'.
survivors.model_impact: The model, following debrief step 5 ('name every scope whose risks or decisions you are restating in full, including one whose last item you are retiring'), tries 'legacy', gets an opaque regex, then tries 'thread' and receives a success response. It then writes 'retired the legacy decision entries' into its hand-off summary — a false claim. The entry persists forever and is counted in the briefing's NOT SHOWN block on every future session. The one error message that would have taught the model the truth is structurally unreachable.
survivors.failure_scenario: A ledger upcast from v1 has spine.key_decisions = [{ref:'0001-old-call', title:'Old call', scope:'legacy'}]. Model calls update_thread with replace_scopes {key_decisions:['legacy']} -> pattern error; falls back to ['thread'] -> HTTP-level success, entry unchanged; model reports the retirement as done.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced all three branches. src/schema/upcast.mjs:47-59 returns `{ ref, title, scope: LEGACY_SCOPE }` for every v1 key_decision; src/schema/patterns.mjs:22 permits it in storage (`SCOPE_PATTERN = '^(c[1-9][0-9]*|thread|legacy)$'`), src/schema/patterns.mjs:24 forbids it in input (`WRITABLE_SCOPE_PATTERN = '^(c[1-9][0-9]*|thread)$'`), and I confirmed WRITABLE_SCOPE_PATTERN is what every caller-facing scope field uses: scopeList items at src/tools/schemas.mjs:34-37 (used by replaceScopesInput :39-46), riskInputItem.scope :18, decisionInputItem.scope :30, and record_decision's scope at src/tools/record-decision.mjs:100. Live: `update_thread({replace_scopes:{key_decisions:['legacy']}})` returned `ToolValidationError: update_thread: invalid input: /replace_scopes/key_decisions/0 must match pattern "^(c[1-9][0-9]*|thread)$"` — no mention of legacy at all. `replace_scopes:{key_decisions:['thread']}` and `['c1']` BOTH returned success with `key_decisions` still `[{"ref":"0007-old-choice","title":"Old choice","scope":"legacy"}]`, exactly as claimed, because src/tools/update-thread.mjs:22-25 filters carried items by `replaced.has(item.scope)` and 'legacy' is never in `replaced`. I checked the dead-code claim independently: the explanatory throw at src/tools/spine-input.mjs:12-19 is reached from normalizeScopeList:27, normalizeRisks:65 and normalizeDecisions:81 — all gated behind ajv (src/tools/registry.mjs:63) for caller-supplied values, and the non-caller defaults come from `resolveWriteScope(thread)`, which returns a criterion id or THREAD_SCOPE and never 'legacy' (src/model/selection.mjs:20-23). The one message that would teach the model the truth is unreachable. Confirmed.

survivors.title: record_decision mutates a done or abandoned thread's spine and updated_at, while update_thread and amend_criteria both refuse terminal threads
evidence: src/tools/update-thread.mjs:109-111 — `if (isTerminal(thread.status)) { throw new ToolError('update_thread: cannot mutate a terminal (...) thread'); }`
src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:106-108 — identical terminal guard
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:48-51 — reads the thread and checks only existence; no isTerminal call anywhere in the module
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:68-76 — appends to `thread.spine.key_decisions` and writes `{...thread, spine:{...}, updated_at: now()}`
src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:8-14 — also no terminal guard before writing a binding and the active-thread pointer
src/tools/append-session-event.mjs:6-10 — also no terminal guard
src/render/briefing.mjs:43-46 — the briefing header prints `last worked ${day}` from `thread.updated_at`
survivors.mechanism: Two of the four spine-mutating tools enforce a terminal guard (update-thread.mjs:109-111, amend-criteria.mjs:106-108) and advertise it in their descriptions ('Terminal-refused'). record_decision performs the same class of mutation — it appends to `spine.key_decisions` and rewrites `updated_at` (record-decision.mjs:68-76) — with no such check; its only precondition is that the thread exists (record-decision.mjs:48-51). I confirmed end to end: after transitioning a thread to `done` via the DoD gate, record_decision succeeded, wrote decisions/0001-post-mortem.md, appended a key_decisions entry, and left the status at `done` with a fresh updated_at. bind_branch (bind-branch.mjs:8-14) additionally re-points the active-thread pointer at a terminal thread. The FSM itself is airtight (fsm.mjs:15-16 gives done/abandoned no outgoing transitions) — the hole is entirely in which handlers consult it.
survivors.model_impact: A closed thread's record is no longer immutable. The briefing header (briefing.mjs:43-46) reports a false 'last worked' date for a thread that was closed weeks earlier, and its DoD-gated closure snapshot silently gains content recorded after closure. Because two sibling tools refuse the same operation, a model that learned 'terminal threads are frozen' from an update_thread refusal now holds a belief the server contradicts — it cannot predict which writes are gated. bind_branch pointing the active-thread pointer at a done thread additionally poisons the next session's preflight.
survivors.failure_scenario: Thread closed via transition_thread(done). Later in the same session the model promotes a straggler decision per debrief step 3 (which is ordered BEFORE the transition in the skill, but a model that reorders or a post-hoc capture hits this). record_decision succeeds, mutating the closed record and its updated_at.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced. I grepped every isTerminal call site myself: src/tools/update-thread.mjs:109, src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:106, src/tools/reopen.mjs:12, src/tools/create-successor.mjs:12, src/drift/reattach.mjs:74, src/drift/disposition.mjs:21 — and none in src/tools/record-decision.mjs, src/tools/bind-branch.mjs or src/tools/append-session-event.mjs. record_decision's only precondition is the existence check at src/tools/record-decision.mjs:48-51, and it mutates `thread.spine.key_decisions` and `updated_at` at :68-75. Live: after closing a thread through the DoD gate (status 'done'), record_decision returned `{"number":"0004","path":".../0004-post-mortem.md","recovery_degraded":false}` and the re-read record showed `status done`, a fresh `updated_at`, and `key_decisions [{"ref":"0004-post-mortem","title":"PM","scope":"c1"}]`. bind_branch and append_session_event also both succeeded on the same done thread. The FSM itself is airtight as claimed — src/model/fsm.mjs:15-16 gives done and abandoned empty transition lists — so the hole is purely in which handlers consult isTerminal. The briefing's 'last worked' line is a blind slice of updated_at (src/render/briefing.mjs:43), so the false-date consequence holds.

survivors.title: None of the ten SPINE_CAPS exist in threadSchema, and assertSpineCaps runs only in update_thread and only against the submitted patch — so over-cap values entering via record_decision or the v1 upcast persist through every later write and are silently ellipsized in the briefing
evidence: src/model/caps.mjs:1-12 — SPINE_CAPS defines activeGoalMaxChars 200, nextStepMaxChars 500, lastSessionMaxChars 300, riskTextMaxChars 300, riskRefsMaxItems 8, riskRefMaxChars 200, decisionTitleMaxChars 120, openRisksMaxPerScope 20, outOfScopeMaxItems 20, outOfScopeItemMaxChars 300
src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:100-107 — spine properties are `{type:'string'}` and `{type:'array'}` with no maxLength and no maxItems anywhere
src/tools/update-thread.mjs:77 — `assertSpineCaps(submitted);` — the ONLY call site in any handler; `submitted` is the patch, not the merged spine
src/tools/update-thread.mjs:56-69 — the merged `spine` (which is what gets written) is never passed to assertSpineCaps
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:148 — the write path's only check is assertValidThread, which compiles threadSchema
src/render/briefing.mjs:9-12 — `truncate` slices to `max - 1` and appends '…' with no other signal
src/render/briefing.mjs:51 — `truncate(spine.active_goal, SPINE_CAPS.activeGoalMaxChars)`
src/render/briefing.mjs:89 — `truncate(spine.next_step, SPINE_CAPS.nextStepMaxChars)`
survivors.mechanism: Caps live in exactly one place a caller can hit — `assertSpineCaps` at update-thread.mjs:77 — and it inspects `submitted`, the fields this call supplied, not the merged spine that is written at update-thread.mjs:123. The persistence layer knows nothing about caps: threadSchema's spine properties (thread.schema.mjs:100-107) carry no maxLength or maxItems, so assertValidThread (local-driver.mjs:148) accepts any length. I verified: a v1 record with a 900-character active_goal upcasts cleanly, and a subsequent `update_thread({spine:{next_step:'go'}})` re-wrote the whole record with the 900 characters intact and no rejection, because active_goal was not in `submitted`. The read side then silently truncates it: briefing.mjs:51 and :89 pass the stored value through `truncate` (briefing.mjs:9-12), which appends an ellipsis and nothing else. The briefing is the only artifact the next session sees — skills/preflight/SKILL.md:24 instructs the model to print it VERBATIM as the whole state transfer.
survivors.model_impact: For active_goal, next_step, last_session and out_of_scope there is no second copy anywhere: what the briefing shows IS the state. Over-cap content silently loses its tail at exactly the moment it matters, marked only by a '…' that reads as stylistic. A next session inherits a truncated goal or a truncated next action and proceeds on it. Meanwhile the caps are enforced inconsistently enough that a model cannot form a stable model of them: the identical value is rejected when submitted and accepted when carried.
survivors.failure_scenario: Ledger upcast from v1 (or a spine written before the caps existed) holds a 900-char active_goal. Model calls update_thread patching only next_step -> success. get_resume_brief renders '## WHY' with the first 199 chars plus '…'. Next session reads a goal whose second half is gone and never learns it was cut.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced. src/model/caps.mjs:1-12 defines all ten caps; I read src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:100-107 and confirmed every spine property is a bare `{type:'string'}` or `{type:'array'}` with no maxLength and no maxItems, so assertValidThread (src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:148) cannot enforce any of them. I grepped assertSpineCaps and found exactly one handler call site, `assertSpineCaps(submitted)` at src/tools/update-thread.mjs:77; the merged object built at :56-69 and written at :123 is never passed to it. Live: I wrote a 900-character active_goal through the driver, then called `update_thread({spine:{next_step:'go'}})` — it succeeded and the returned record's active_goal was still 900 characters. The read side then silently ellipsizes: src/render/briefing.mjs:9-12 slices to `max - 1` and appends '…', consumed at :51 (active_goal) and :89 (next_step). And skills/preflight/SKILL.md:24 does instruct the model to print the briefing VERBATIM as the whole state transfer, so the truncated string is what the next session inherits. The title's 'None of the ten SPINE_CAPS exist in threadSchema' is literally accurate.

survivors.title: amend_criteria's three-branch oneOf emits nine-to-eleven mutually contradictory required-property clauses that never name which op branch failed, and 'must be equal to constant' omits the constant
evidence: src/tools/schemas.mjs:72-109 — criteriaAmendOperation: `required:['op']` plus a three-member `oneOf` whose branches are discriminated only by `op: {const: 'insert'|'rewrite'|'strike'}`

src/schema/validators.mjs:10 — `errors.map((e) => `${e.instancePath || '(root)'} ${e.message}`.trim()).join('; ')` — drops e.schemaPath and e.params, which is where ajv puts the branch identity and the allowed constant
src/tools/registry.mjs:36 — `new Ajv({ allErrors: true })` — guarantees every branch's failures are collected, not just the first
src/tools/registry.mjs:46 — the ToolValidationError message is the concatenation of all of them
survivors.mechanism: criteriaAmendOperation (schemas.mjs:72-109) is a `oneOf` over three object schemas whose only discriminator is a `const` on `op`. With `allErrors: true` (registry.mjs:36), ajv evaluates all three branches and reports every failure from each. formatValidationErrors (validators.mjs:10) then flattens them using only `instancePath` and `message`, discarding `schemaPath` (the only field that says WHICH oneOf branch produced the clause) and `params` (which holds `allowedValue` for const and `allowedValues` for enum). I reproduced the exact strings a model receives. For `{op:'strike', id:'c1'}` — a single missing decision_ref: `amend_criteria: invalid input: /operations/0 must have required property 'text'; /operations/0 must have required property 'kind'; /operations/0 must NOT have additional properties; /operations/0/op must be equal to constant; /operations/0 must have required property 'text'; /operations/0 must have required property 'decision_ref'; /operations/0/op must be equal to constant; /operations/0 must have required property 'decision_ref'; /operations/0 must match exactly one schema in oneOf`. Nine clauses, three of them demanding fields ('text', 'kind') that a strike op must NOT have, two 'must be equal to constant' clauses that never say which constant, and no occurrence of the word 'strike' anywhere.
survivors.model_impact: This is the calibration incident's failure mode with a wider blast radius. The model cannot determine which field it actually got wrong: the message simultaneously demands 'text', 'kind' and 'decision_ref' for one operation. The attractive repair — adding 'text' and 'kind' because two clauses ask for them — pushes the payload further from the strike branch and produces a differently-shaped but equally opaque error, since additionalProperties:false now fires too. There is no signal distinguishing 'you chose the right op and omitted one field' from 'your op value is unrecognized'. Every retry burns a full round trip plus a re-read of the tool schema, and the correct fix (add decision_ref, change nothing else) is one of nine equally-weighted hypotheses.
survivors.failure_scenario: Model follows debrief step 4 and emits {op:'strike', id:'c1'} having recorded the decision but omitting decision_ref. It receives nine contradictory clauses, adds text and kind, receives a longer error, and either abandons the amendment or falls back to update_thread, losing the strike.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced byte-for-byte through the real callTool. `amend_criteria({thread_id: <valid ULID>, operations:[{op:'strike', id:'c1'}]})` returned exactly: `amend_criteria: invalid input: /operations/0 must have required property 'text'; /operations/0 must have required property 'kind'; /operations/0 must NOT have additional properties; /operations/0/op must be equal to constant; /operations/0 must have required property 'text'; /operations/0 must have required property 'decision_ref'; /operations/0/op must be equal to constant; /operations/0 must have required property 'decision_ref'; /operations/0 must match exactly one schema in oneOf`. Nine clauses, three demanding fields a strike op must not have, two constants never named, and the word 'strike' absent. Mechanism verified in source: src/tools/schemas.mjs:72-109 is a three-branch oneOf discriminated only by `op: {const: ...}` (branches at :81, :92, :103 — the finder's :77/:89/:102 are off by a few lines but name the right constructs); src/tools/registry.mjs:36 constructs `new Ajv({ allErrors: true })`; src/schema/validators.mjs:10 projects each error to `${e.instancePath || '(root)'} ${e.message}`, discarding e.schemaPath and e.params; src/tools/registry.mjs:46 concatenates the lot. I also confirmed the escalation claim: adding the demanded fields makes it worse — my second probe with an extra property produced ELEVEN clauses, six of them `must NOT have additional properties`.

survivors.title: normalizeOptions normalizes only the string branch; the array branch the skill instructs the model to use is written into the permanent decision record raw, producing '- - keep it', empty bullets and untrimmed text, while a comma-separated string silently collapses to one option
evidence: src/tools/record-decision.mjs:8-14 — `function normalizeOptions(options) { if (Array.isArray(options)) return options; return options.split('\n').map(...).filter(...); }` — the array branch returns immediately with zero processing
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:17 — `const optionLines = options.map((o) => `- ${o}`).join('\n');` — every element is prefixed with a bullet unconditionally
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:93-98 — `options: { anyOf: [ {type:'array', items:{type:'string'}}, {type:'string'} ] }` — array items have no minLength, so '' validates
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:44-47 — the only post-normalization check is `options.length === 0`
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:33 — instructs the model to pass 'the `options` you weighed (a plain list of strings)', i.e. the unnormalized branch
survivors.mechanism: normalizeOptions (record-decision.mjs:8-14) has two branches with completely different contracts. The string branch splits on newline, trims, strips a leading bullet marker and filters empties. The array branch returns the input untouched — no trim, no bullet stripping, no empty filtering — and renderDecision (record-decision.mjs:17) then prefixes every element with '- '. I verified against a real driver: `options: ['- keep it', '', '  spaced  ']` renders the Options section as `- - keep it`, `- ` (a bare bullet), `-   spaced  `. Separately, `options: 'keep it, drop it, defer it'` — a natural way to express three options in one string — renders as a single bullet `- keep it, drop it, defer it`, because the string branch splits only on '\n'. The only guard is `options.length === 0` (record-decision.mjs:44-47), which neither case trips. The output is a write-once MADR record: nothing in the codebase can edit a decision file after writeDecision.
survivors.model_impact: Silent corruption of permanent data with no error and no signal in the return value (the handler returns only `{number, path, recovery_degraded}` — never the rendered options). The array form is the one skills/debrief/SKILL.md:33 tells the model to use, so the unnormalized path is the default path. A model that helpfully pre-formats its options as markdown bullets gets double bullets forever; a model that passes a comma list silently records three deliberated alternatives as one. A later session reading that decision via read_decision inherits a malformed or collapsed rationale and cannot tell it was ever different.
survivors.failure_scenario: record_decision(options: ['- adopt orphan-branch backend', '- adopt custom-ref backend']) -> decisions/0001-x.md permanently contains '- - adopt orphan-branch backend' / '- - adopt custom-ref backend'. Or record_decision(options: 'orphan-branch, custom-ref, no ledger') -> one option recorded, two alternatives lost.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced against a real driver. src/tools/record-decision.mjs:8-14: `if (Array.isArray(options)) return options;` returns the array with zero processing, while the string branch splits on '\n', trims, strips BULLET_MARKER (:6) and filters empties. src/tools/record-decision.mjs:17 then prefixes every element with '- ' unconditionally. Live, `options: ['- keep it', '', '  spaced  ']` produced this Options section verbatim in decisions/0001-opts.md: `- - keep it` / `- ` / `-   spaced  `. And `options: 'keep it, drop it, defer it'` produced a single bullet `- keep it, drop it, defer it`. The only post-normalization guard is `options.length === 0` at :44-47, which neither case trips; the array items carry no minLength (:95), so '' validates. The handler returns only `{number, path, recovery_degraded}` (:78), so nothing in the response exposes the rendered options, and I found no code path in src/tools/ or src/drivers/ that edits a decision file after writeDecision. One citation correction: the skill instruction 'the `options` you weighed (a plain list of strings)' is at skills/debrief/SKILL.md:21, not :33 — the substance (the skill steers the model onto the unnormalized array branch) is correct.

survivors.title: record_decision writes an uncapped title into spine.key_decisions, bypassing the 120-char decisionTitleMaxChars that update_thread enforces, and the briefing then silently truncates it
evidence: src/tools/record-decision.mjs:91 — `title: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` — no maxLength

src/tools/record-decision.mjs:68-70 — `[...thread.spine.key_decisions, { ref, title: args.title, scope }]` — writes straight into the capped structure with no assertSpineCaps call anywhere in the module
src/model/caps.mjs:9 — `decisionTitleMaxChars: 120`
src/model/caps.mjs:79-86 — decisionViolations enforces it, reachable only from update-thread.mjs:77
src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:29 — decisionItem `title: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` — no maxLength at the write path either
src/render/briefing.mjs:125 — `truncate(d.title, SPINE_CAPS.decisionTitleMaxChars)`
survivors.mechanism: decisionTitleMaxChars (caps.mjs:9) is enforced by decisionViolations (caps.mjs:79-86), which only runs via assertSpineCaps at update-thread.mjs:77. record_decision writes the same field through a different door: its input schema caps nothing (record-decision.mjs:91) and its handler appends `{ref, title: args.title, scope}` to spine.key_decisions (record-decision.mjs:68-70) without calling assertSpineCaps. The write path cannot catch it either — decisionItem in threadSchema (thread.schema.mjs:29) has no maxLength. I verified: a 400-character title passed to record_decision is stored verbatim in spine.key_decisions, and a subsequent update_thread call succeeds without complaint. The briefing then silently cuts it to 119 chars plus an ellipsis (briefing.mjs:125).
survivors.model_impact: The same constraint is enforced or not depending on which tool the value travels through, so the model cannot learn it. More concretely: a model that writes a descriptive decision title sees it accepted by record_decision, then sees update_thread reject the identical string if it ever restates it, and finally sees a truncated version in the briefing. Unlike the spine scalars, the full title survives in the decision file, so this is recoverable via read_decision — but nothing tells the model that truncation occurred.
survivors.failure_scenario: record_decision(title: <180 chars>) succeeds. Briefing '## DECIDED ON THIS STEP' shows the first 119 chars plus '…'. Model later calls update_thread restating that key_decision with the same title -> CapViolationError 'spine.key_decisions item title exceeds 120 chars' for a value the server itself wrote.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced. src/tools/record-decision.mjs:91 is `title: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` — no maxLength, as claimed. :68-70 appends `{ ref, title: args.title, scope }` straight into spine.key_decisions with no assertSpineCaps call anywhere in the module (my grep found the only handler call site is src/tools/update-thread.mjs:77). src/model/caps.mjs:9 sets decisionTitleMaxChars 120 and :79-86 (decisionViolations) is the only enforcer. The write path cannot catch it: src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:29 is `title: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` with no maxLength. Live: a 400-character title passed to record_decision was stored verbatim (`stored title len: 400`), and a subsequent `update_thread({spine:{last_session:'ok'}})` succeeded without complaint. src/render/briefing.mjs:125 truncates it for display. The finder's recoverability caveat is also right — the full title survives in the decision file, readable via read_decision.

survivors.title: Every error is flattened to {error: <JS class name>, message} in an isError tool result, discarding CapViolationError.fields, ToolValidationError.errors and SchemaValidationError.errors, and giving bootstrap failures the same shape as input-validation failures
evidence: bin/ledger-server.mjs:57 — `text: JSON.stringify({ error: error.name, message: error.message })` — the only serialization of any error
bin/ledger-server.mjs:56-59 — returned as `{content:[...], isError:true}`, i.e. a tool result, never an MCP protocol error
bin/ledger-server.mjs:52 — `const ctx = await resolveContext();` sits inside the same try block, so context-build failures are reported identically
src/model/caps.mjs:24-25 — `this.fields = Object.freeze(...); this.field = this.fields[0];` — structured detail that never leaves the process
src/tools/registry.mjs:49 — `this.errors = errors;` — the full ajv error objects, likewise dropped
src/schema/validators.mjs:19 — `this.errors = errors;` — likewise dropped

src/drivers/select.mjs:29 — `throw new Error('selectDriver: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA is not set');` — an environment fault that reaches the model as `{"error":"Error", ...}` attributed to whichever tool was called
survivors.mechanism: The CallTool handler (ledger-server.mjs:49-61) wraps everything — including `resolveContext()` at line 52 — in one try, and serializes any throw to `{error: error.name, message: error.message}` (line 57). Three error classes deliberately carry structured detail: CapViolationError.fields (caps.mjs:24-25), ToolValidationError.errors (registry.mjs:49) and SchemaValidationError.errors (validators.mjs:19). None of it is serialized. I verified the wire format through the real server: a two-cap violation arrives as `{"error":"CapViolationError","message":"spine.active_goal exceeds 200 chars; spine.next_step exceeds 500 chars"}` — the `.fields` array `['active_goal','next_step']` is gone. The only discriminator the model gets is a JavaScript class name, which is not a stable API and does not map to layers: ToolError covers every handler rejection from a nonexistent thread_id to a malformed risk sentence, and plain `Error` covers driver faults, environment faults (select.mjs:29) and slug-derivation faults alike. There is no `code` field, no field path array, no retryable flag.
survivors.model_impact: A model cannot programmatically branch on the failure. It must parse English prose to decide whether to fix an argument, call a different tool, or tell the user the environment is broken — and the four categories are indistinguishable at the `error` key. Worst case: `selectDriver: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA is not set` returned from open_thread looks like an argument problem, so the model retries open_thread with different arguments indefinitely. Because these are isError tool results rather than protocol errors, they also do not surface as transport failures the harness could special-case.
survivors.failure_scenario: Non-git project with CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA unset. Model calls open_thread -> {"error":"Error","message":"selectDriver: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA is not set"} with isError:true, indistinguishable in shape from a bad-title rejection. Model retries open_thread with a different title.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived from source; every cited line says what is claimed. bin/ledger-server.mjs:49-61 wraps `const ctx = await resolveContext();` (:52) and `await call(...)` (:53) in one try, and :57 serializes any throw as `JSON.stringify({ error: error.name, message: error.message })`, returned with `isError: true` (:58) as a tool result rather than an MCP protocol error. The discarded detail is real: `this.fields = Object.freeze(...)` at src/model/caps.mjs:24, `this.errors = errors` at src/tools/registry.mjs:49, `this.errors = errors` at src/schema/validators.mjs:19 — none of the three is referenced anywhere in bin/. The message-only content of a multi-cap violation is confirmed by src/model/caps.mjs:120-121, which joins violation details with '; ' and passes the field list only into the discarded `.fields`. The environment-fault collision is real: src/drivers/select.mjs:29 throws a plain `Error('selectDriver: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA is not set')` from ledgerDataRoot, reached via buildContext (src/tools/context.mjs:9) inside the same try; I observed the analogous plain-Error class in my own runs, where `activeThreadPath: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA is not set for a non-git project` (src/util/active-thread.mjs:27) surfaced as a bare `Error` attributed to open_thread. There is no `code` field, no field-path array and no retryable flag anywhere in the serialization. Medium is the right severity: it degrades recovery quality rather than corrupting data.

survivors.title: formatValidationErrors discards ajv's params, so every enum rejection reads 'must be equal to one of the allowed values' and every const rejection reads 'must be equal to constant' with the permitted values never stated
evidence: src/schema/validators.mjs:10 — `${e.instancePath || '(root)'} ${e.message}` — e.params (allowedValues / allowedValue) is never read
src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:59 — `to_status: { type: 'string', enum: ['active','paused','blocked','done','abandoned'] }`
src/tools/schemas.mjs:54 — `kind: { type: 'string', enum: [...CRITERION_KINDS] }`
src/tools/schemas.mjs:77 — `op: { const: 'insert' }` (and :89, :102 for rewrite/strike)
src/tools/registry.mjs:46 — ToolValidationError composes its message from formatValidationErrors
survivors.mechanism: formatValidationErrors (validators.mjs:10) projects each ajv error to `instancePath + message` only. ajv places the permitted values in `e.params.allowedValues` for `enum` and `e.params.allowedValue` for `const`, and neither is read. I reproduced the resulting strings: `transition_thread({to_status:'closed'})` yields `transition_thread: invalid input: /to_status must be equal to one of the allowed values` — the five legal statuses never appear. The const case is worse because it also appears inside the amend_criteria oneOf, where `/operations/0/op must be equal to constant` gives the model neither the constant nor the branch. By contrast `pattern` rejections do carry the regex inline (I confirmed `/slug must match pattern "^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$"`), so the layer is inconsistent about self-description even within itself.
survivors.model_impact: Grading the four attribution questions for an enum rejection: (i) which layer — inferable from the 'invalid input' prefix, OK; (ii) which field — yes, instancePath names it; (iii) what an accepted value looks like — NO, entirely absent; (iv) can the same payload ever succeed — implicitly no, but the model must guess a replacement value blind. It must re-fetch the tool schema (a full ListTools round trip) or guess. Pattern errors answer (iii); enum and const errors do not. The fix is one line reading e.params, so the cost is pure waste.
survivors.failure_scenario: Model emits transition_thread(to_status:'closed') or amend_criteria op:'remove'. It receives no list of legal values and either guesses ('close','completed','finished') across several round trips or re-reads the full tool list.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced all three strings myself. src/schema/validators.mjs:10 projects to `${e.instancePath || '(root)'} ${e.message}` and never reads e.params, which is where ajv stores allowedValues (enum) and allowedValue (const). Live: `transition_thread({to_status:'closed'})` returned `transition_thread: invalid input: /to_status must be equal to one of the allowed values` — the five statuses declared at src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:59 never appear. The const case reproduced inside the oneOf as `/operations/0/op must be equal to constant` with no constant named. The inconsistency claim also holds: `record_decision({slug:'Bad Slug', ...})` returned `/slug must match pattern "^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$"`, and the replace_scopes probe returned `/replace_scopes/key_decisions/0 must match pattern "^(c[1-9][0-9]*|thread)$"` — pattern errors self-describe, enum and const errors do not, within the same formatter. Minor citation drift: the const declarations are at src/tools/schemas.mjs:81, :92 and :103, not :77/:89/:102.

survivors.title: open_risks[].text must match a spaced em-dash two-clause regex enforced only in a handler; neither the input schema nor the tool description mentions it, so any caller not driven by the debrief skill fails on first use
evidence: src/tools/spine-input.mjs:5 — `const RISK_SENTENCE = /^[^\n]+ — [^\n]+$/;` — requires a literal U+2014 with a space on each side
src/tools/spine-input.mjs:60-63 — the throw site, reached for every risk on every update_thread call
src/tools/schemas.mjs:12-21 — riskInputItem declares `text: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` with no pattern and no description
src/tools/update-thread.mjs:130 — the tool description covers scoping and replace_scopes at length but never mentions the risk text shape
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:30 — the ONLY place the shape is stated: 'Shape each one as `<specific constraint or action> — <why, in plain words>`'
survivors.mechanism: The constraint lives entirely at the handler layer (spine-input.mjs:5, enforced at :60-63). The MCP contract the model actually reads — riskInputItem (schemas.mjs:12-21) plus the update_thread description (update-thread.mjs:130) — advertises only `minLength: 1`. I confirmed the runtime behavior through the server: `open_risks:[{text:'watch the cache'}]` returns `ToolError: update_thread: spine.open_risks: risk text "watch the cache" does not match the required shape "<specific constraint or action> — <why, in plain words>": two non-empty clauses on one line, joined by a spaced em dash`. The error message itself is excellent — it names the tool, the field, the offending value, and the accepted shape. The defect is purely that the constraint is undiscoverable before failing, and that the required character is U+2014 specifically: a hyphen, an en dash, or an unspaced em dash all fail.
survivors.model_impact: Guaranteed one wasted round trip on first use for any caller whose context does not include skills/debrief/SKILL.md — a subagent, a different skill, or a model invoking the tool directly. The MCP tool schema is supposed to be the self-contained contract; here it under-specifies, and the gap is closed only by a document that is not part of the server. Recovery is fast because the error is well-written, so the cost is bounded at roughly one round trip per risk-writing context.
survivors.failure_scenario: A subagent with only the ledger MCP tools loaded calls update_thread with open_risks:[{text:'cache invalidation is fragile'}]. Rejected. It cannot learn the requirement from listTools output; it learns it only from the rejection.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced. src/tools/spine-input.mjs:5 is `const RISK_SENTENCE = /^[^\n]+ — [^\n]+$/;` — a literal U+2014 with a mandatory space on each side, so a hyphen, an en dash or an unspaced em dash all fail. The throw is at :60-63 inside normalizeRisks, reached from src/tools/update-thread.mjs:41-47 for every submitted risk. The advertised contract does not mention it: riskInputItem at src/tools/schemas.mjs:12-21 declares only `text: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` with no pattern and no description, and the update_thread description at src/tools/update-thread.mjs:130 covers scoping and replace_scopes at length while never mentioning risk text shape. I confirmed skills/debrief/SKILL.md:30 is the only statement of the shape. Live: `update_thread({spine:{open_risks:[{text:'watch the cache'}]}})` returned `update_thread: spine.open_risks: risk text "watch the cache" does not match the required shape "<specific constraint or action> — <why, in plain words>": two non-empty clauses on one line, joined by a spaced em dash`. The finder's own assessment — excellent message, undiscoverable constraint, cost bounded at roughly one round trip — is accurate, and medium is the right severity.

survivors.title: archive_thread stores a whitespace-only abandoned_reason that transition_thread refuses for the identical field, and transition_thread reports a supplied-but-blank value as 'required'
evidence: src/tools/archive-thread.mjs:42 — `reason: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` — ajv-only, no trim
src/tools/archive-thread.mjs:21 — `abandoned_reason: args.reason` — written with no further check
src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:6-8 — `function nonEmpty(value) { return typeof value === 'string' && value.trim().length > 0; }`
src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:23-25 — `if (to === 'abandoned' && !nonEmpty(args.abandoned_reason)) throw new ToolError('transition_thread: abandoned_reason is required to enter abandoned');`
src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:94 — `abandoned_reason: { type: ['string','null'] }` — the write path enforces neither emptiness rule
survivors.mechanism: Two tools set the same stored field under two different emptiness definitions. archive_thread relies on ajv's `minLength: 1` (archive-thread.mjs:42), which counts whitespace, and writes the value straight through (archive-thread.mjs:21). transition_thread applies `nonEmpty`, which trims (transition-thread.mjs:6-8, :23-25). threadSchema (thread.schema.mjs:94) enforces neither, so the write path cannot arbitrate. I verified both: `archive_thread({reason:'   '})` succeeded and stored `abandoned_reason: '   '`; `transition_thread({to_status:'abandoned', abandoned_reason:'   '})` was refused. Separately, the refusal wording is wrong: the value WAS supplied, so 'abandoned_reason is required to enter abandoned' misattributes a content failure as an omission. The same wording defect applies to blocked_by (transition-thread.mjs:20-22), which I also confirmed returns 'blocked_by is required to enter blocked' for `blocked_by: '  '`.
survivors.model_impact: A model that hits the transition_thread refusal reads 'is required' and concludes it omitted the parameter — the wrong hypothesis, exactly the shape of the calibration incident. It may re-emit the same blank value believing the first call did not parse. And if it routes to archive_thread instead, the blank reason is accepted, permanently closing a thread with an empty rationale that the briefing and future sessions cannot interpret.
survivors.failure_scenario: Model builds abandoned_reason from an empty template variable, yielding '   '. transition_thread refuses with 'is required'; model retries identically; then falls back to archive_thread(reason:'   '), which succeeds and stores the blank reason forever.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced both halves. src/tools/archive-thread.mjs:42 is `reason: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` (ajv counts whitespace) and :21 writes `abandoned_reason: args.reason` with no further check; src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:6-8 defines nonEmpty with `.trim()` and :23-25 applies it. src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:94 is `abandoned_reason: { type: ['string', 'null'] }` — no minLength, no pattern, so the write path arbitrates nothing. Live: `archive_thread({reason:'   '})` succeeded and stored `"   "`; `transition_thread({to_status:'abandoned', abandoned_reason:'   '})` returned `transition_thread: abandoned_reason is required to enter abandoned` and `transition_thread({to_status:'blocked', blocked_by:'  '})` returned `transition_thread: blocked_by is required to enter blocked`. The misattribution claim is fair — the value was supplied, and 'is required' points the model at omission rather than content. Worth adding that the codebase already has the correct wording one file away: src/model/dod.mjs:13 says `closure_statement must be non-empty for done` for exactly this class of failure.

survivors.title: archive_thread appends a fixed 'a blocked thread must first go blocked -> paused' hint to every illegal-transition refusal, so archiving an already-terminal thread instructs the model to perform an unrelated and itself-illegal transition
evidence: src/tools/archive-thread.mjs:12-16 — the message is unconditional: `throw new ToolError(`archive_thread: illegal transition ${thread.status} -> abandoned (a blocked thread must first go blocked -> paused)`)`
src/model/fsm.mjs:15-16 — `done: Object.freeze([]), abandoned: Object.freeze([])` — terminal states have no outgoing transitions, so the suggested repair is impossible
src/tools/reopen.mjs:12-14 — the sibling tool DOES distinguish terminal and points at the right remedy: 'cannot reopen a terminal (...) thread; use create_successor'
survivors.mechanism: canTransition returns false for three distinct reasons — the thread is blocked, done, or already abandoned (fsm.mjs:11-17) — and archive-thread.mjs:12-16 emits one message for all of them with a parenthetical that is only true for the blocked case. I confirmed the wrong-hint output on a done thread: `archive_thread: illegal transition done -> abandoned (a blocked thread must first go blocked -> paused)`. For a done thread the suggested repair is doubly wrong: the thread is not blocked, and ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.done is empty (fsm.mjs:15) so no transition out of done exists at all. reopen.mjs:12-14 shows the codebase knows how to do this correctly — it separates the terminal case and names create_successor as the remedy.
survivors.model_impact: The model is handed an explicit, authoritative-sounding repair instruction that cannot work. It will call transition_thread(to_status:'paused') on the done thread, receive 'illegal transition done -> paused' from a different tool with different wording, and now hold two contradictory refusals about the same thread with no statement anywhere that terminal threads simply cannot be archived. Two guaranteed-failing round trips before it can reason its way out.
survivors.failure_scenario: Model tries to archive a thread already closed as done (e.g. it lost track of an earlier transition). It gets the blocked-thread hint, calls transition_thread(done -> paused), gets a second refusal, and is left without the correct answer (the thread is already terminal; nothing further is needed).

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and reproduced. src/tools/archive-thread.mjs:12-16 emits one unconditional message for every canTransition-false case, including the parenthetical '(a blocked thread must first go blocked -> paused)'. src/model/fsm.mjs:11-17 shows canTransition(x,'abandoned') is false for three distinct states — blocked (:14 allows only active and paused), done (:15 empty) and abandoned (:16 empty) — so the hint is true for only one of the three. Live on a thread I closed through the DoD gate: `archive_thread: illegal transition done -> abandoned (a blocked thread must first go blocked -> paused)`. The suggested repair is impossible: ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.done is `Object.freeze([])` at src/model/fsm.mjs:15, so no transition out of done exists. The contrast is real — src/tools/reopen.mjs:12-14 separates the terminal case and names create_successor as the remedy, so the codebase already knows how to word this.

survivors.title: Thread slugs are neither unique nor pattern-checked at any layer: an explicit slug is stored verbatim while a derived slug is normalized, and duplicate slugs are silently collapsed by the by-slug index so branch reattach resolves the wrong thread
evidence: src/tools/open-thread.mjs:33 — `slug: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` — no pattern
src/model/thread.mjs:53-56 — `const slug = typeof rawSlug === 'string' && rawSlug.trim().length > 0 ? rawSlug : toSlug(title);` — an explicit slug skips toSlug entirely
src/model/thread.mjs:10-15 — toSlug lowercases and collapses `[^a-z0-9]+` to '-', so derived slugs are always `[a-z0-9-]+`
src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:59 — `slug: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` — the write path adds no pattern either
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:206-208 — decision slugs ARE pattern-checked at the driver: `if (typeof slug !== 'string' || !SLUG_PATTERN.test(slug)) throw ...`
src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:34-35 — `if (thread.slug && !(thread.slug in bySlug)) { bySlug[thread.slug] = thread.id; }` — first writer wins, silently
src/drift/reattach.mjs:43-44 — `const bySlug = await driver.readIndexFile('by-slug'); const candidate = bySlug ? bySlug[branchSlug(branch)] : undefined;`
survivors.mechanism: No layer constrains a thread slug beyond `minLength: 1` (open-thread.mjs:33, thread.schema.mjs:59). I verified both halves. Shape: `open_thread({title:'x', slug:'Not A Slug/../etc'})` stored the slug verbatim, because thread.mjs:53-56 uses an explicit slug as-is and only falls back to toSlug (thread.mjs:10-15) when absent — so the two creation paths produce structurally different slugs. The driver proves the codebase knows to check this: decision slugs are pattern-validated at local-driver.mjs:206-208, thread slugs are not. Uniqueness: two open_thread calls with the same title both produced slug 'ship-the-cache' with distinct ULIDs, and the rebuilt by-slug index contained exactly one entry pointing at the FIRST thread (rebuild-index.mjs:34-35 keeps the first writer). The returned counts report `by_slug: 1` against `threads: 2` but never name a collision. drift/reattach.mjs:43-44 resolves a renamed branch through that index, so it will attach to the older same-slug thread.
survivors.model_impact: Two silent wrongs. First, the second thread is unreachable by slug forever, and branch reattachment (reattach.mjs:43-44) binds work to the wrong thread — a wrong-thread binding means session state is written into someone else's continuity record. Second, a model that supplies an explicit slug gets a different validity contract than one that lets it be derived, so it cannot predict what is legal; a slug containing path separators or spaces is accepted without comment even though the sibling decision-slug path rejects exactly that.
survivors.failure_scenario: Two threads opened in the same project with the title 'Ship the cache' (a natural repeat across sessions). Both get slug 'ship-the-cache'. A branch named ship-the-cache is later reattached via reconcile -> reattach resolves by-slug to the FIRST, now-stale thread and binds the branch there.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced both halves. Shape: src/tools/open-thread.mjs:33 is `slug: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` with no pattern, src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:59 is the same at the write path, and src/model/thread.mjs:53-56 uses an explicit slug verbatim, falling back to toSlug (:10-15, which collapses `[^a-z0-9]+` to '-') only when absent. Live: `open_thread({title:'x', slug:'Not A Slug/../etc'})` stored `"Not A Slug/../etc"` unchanged. The sibling contrast is real — src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:206-208 rejects a decision slug that fails SLUG_PATTERN (:15). Uniqueness: two open_thread calls with title 'Ship the cache' both produced slug 'ship-the-cache' with distinct ULIDs, and rebuild_index returned `{"threads":2,...,"by_slug":1,...}` with by-slug containing exactly one entry pointing at the FIRST thread — matching src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:34-35 (`if (thread.slug && !(thread.slug in bySlug))`), first writer wins, silently, with no collision named in the returned counts. src/drift/reattach.mjs:42-47 resolves a renamed branch through that index, so the wrong-thread binding follows; note this arm requires driver.isGit() (reattach.mjs:53), i.e. it applies to git projects, which is the normal deployment.

survivors.title: toSlug strips every non-ASCII character, so any fully non-Latin thread title fails open_thread with a bare Error and a constraint stated nowhere in the schema or description
evidence: src/model/thread.mjs:10-15 — `.replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')` after lowercasing, which erases CJK, Cyrillic, Greek, Hebrew, Arabic and emoji alike
src/model/thread.mjs:57-59 — `if (slug.length === 0) { throw new Error('newThread: could not derive a slug from title; pass an explicit slug'); }`
src/tools/open-thread.mjs:32 — `title: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` — no charset constraint
src/tools/open-thread.mjs:26 — the description mentions neither slugs nor the charset requirement
bin/ledger-server.mjs:57 — serializes `error.name`, which here is the generic 'Error'
survivors.mechanism: toSlug (thread.mjs:10-15) lowercases and replaces every run of non-`[a-z0-9]` with a hyphen, then strips leading/trailing hyphens. A title composed entirely of non-ASCII letters reduces to the empty string, and thread.mjs:57-59 throws. I confirmed: `open_thread({title:'キャッシュ改善', completion_criteria:[{text:'a'}]})` -> `Error: newThread: could not derive a slug from title; pass an explicit slug`. Nothing in the input schema (open-thread.mjs:32) or the description (open-thread.mjs:26) signals that the title's character set is load-bearing, and the error class is the generic `Error`, so the wire payload is `{"error":"Error", ...}` with no tool attribution.
survivors.model_impact: Guaranteed first-call failure for any non-Latin-script project, discoverable only by failing. The message does name the remedy ('pass an explicit slug'), so recovery is one round trip — but the model must then invent a slug whose own validity is unconstrained (see thread-slug-uniqueness-and-shape-unenforced), and it has no way to know what a good one looks like. create_successor (create-successor.mjs:15-20) shares the defect and is worse: its input schema exposes no slug parameter at all, so the suggested remedy is unavailable and the failure is unrecoverable.
survivors.failure_scenario: Model opens a thread titled '缓存改进' -> Error. It retries via create_successor or with a slug guess. Through create_successor there is no slug parameter, so the call can never succeed with that title.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced. src/model/thread.mjs:10-15 lowercases and replaces every run of `[^a-z0-9]+` with '-', then strips leading/trailing hyphens, so a fully non-ASCII title reduces to ''; :57-59 then throws a generic `Error`. Live: `open_thread({title:'キャッシュ改善', completion_criteria:[{text:'a'}]})` returned `Error | newThread: could not derive a slug from title; pass an explicit slug`. Nothing signals the charset dependency: src/tools/open-thread.mjs:32 is `title: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` and the description at :26 mentions neither slugs nor charset. The error class is the generic Error, so bin/ledger-server.mjs:57 serializes `"error":"Error"` with no tool attribution. I verified the create_successor aggravation independently: its inputSchema (src/tools/create-successor.mjs:30-39) exposes no slug property, and its newThread call (:15-20) passes only title, completion_criteria, predecessor_id and parent_id — so the suggested remedy genuinely is unavailable there.

survivors.title: Decision refs are pinned to exactly four digits in the thread schema and every input schema but read_decision accepts four-or-more and nextDecisionNumber grows past four, so a ledger past 9999 decisions writes the file then fails the thread write
evidence: src/schema/patterns.mjs:8 — `DECISION_REF_PATTERN = '^[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9-]+$'` — exactly four
src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:28 — decisionItem `ref: { type: 'string', pattern: DECISION_REF_PATTERN }` — enforced at the write path
src/tools/schemas.mjs:70 — `const decisionRef = { type: 'string', pattern: DECISION_REF_PATTERN };` used by amend_criteria rewrite/strike
src/tools/read-decision.mjs:25 — `nnnn: { type: 'string', pattern: '^[0-9]{4,}$' }` — four or more
src/render/briefing.mjs:7 — `const DECISION_NUMBER = /^([0-9]{4,})-/;` — four or more
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:199 — `return String(max + 1).padStart(4, '0');` — pads to four but does not cap at four
survivors.mechanism: Three components disagree on decision-number width. nextDecisionNumber (local-driver.mjs:199) pads to four but returns five digits once max reaches 9999. read_decision (read-decision.mjs:25) and the briefing renderer (briefing.mjs:7) both accept four-or-more. But DECISION_REF_PATTERN (patterns.mjs:8) is exactly four, and it gates both the stored thread record (thread.schema.mjs:28) and amend_criteria's decision_ref input (schemas.mjs:70). At decision 10000, record_decision would write the file at record-decision.mjs:66, build ref '10000-slug', and then fail assertValidThread at local-driver.mjs:148 — feeding directly into the orphan-decision-file defect, and permanently, since every retry produces a wider number.
survivors.model_impact: Practically unreachable (10000 decisions in one project ledger), so the direct impact is nil. It matters as a coherence signal: the same value has three different validity definitions across read, render and write layers, and the strictest one sits at the write path where a failure produces an uncleaned side effect. The narrower live consequence is that a model reading briefing output (which tolerates 4+) cannot rely on that string being a legal amend_criteria decision_ref.
survivors.failure_scenario: Ledger accumulates 10000 decisions. record_decision writes decisions/10000-x.md then throws SchemaValidationError on /spine/key_decisions/N/ref, leaving an orphan file; every retry widens the number and repeats.

verdict.reasoning: Confidence upgraded from the finder's 'likely' to certain — I tested the regexes directly rather than reasoning about them. src/schema/patterns.mjs:8 is `'^[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9-]+$'`; `new RegExp(that).test('10000-slug')` returns false, so a five-digit ref is rejected. It gates the stored record at src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:28 and amend_criteria's decision_ref at src/tools/schemas.mjs:70. src/tools/read-decision.mjs:25 accepts `'^[0-9]{4,}$'` and src/render/briefing.mjs:7 accepts `/^([0-9]{4,})-/`. src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:199 is `String(max + 1).padStart(4, '0')`, which returns '10000' for max 9999, and DECISION_FILE at :16 (`/^([0-9]+)-(.+)\.md$/`) matches '10000-slug.md' so listDecisions keeps counting. The failure chain into the orphan defect is therefore real: writeDecision at src/tools/record-decision.mjs:66 lands the file, then assertValidThread rejects the ref. Practically unreachable at 10000 decisions, so low is correct; it stands as a coherence signal — three definitions of one value across read, render and write.

survivors.title: ISO_TIMESTAMP_PATTERN has no trailing anchor, so created_at and updated_at accept any trailing garbage and any impossible date component
evidence: src/schema/patterns.mjs:3-4 — `ISO_TIMESTAMP_PATTERN = '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}'` — starts with ^, ends with no $
src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:109-110 — created_at and updated_at both use it
src/schema/binding.schema.mjs:25 — created_at uses it
src/render/briefing.mjs:43 — `thread.updated_at.slice(0, 10)` — the briefing's 'last worked' date is a blind slice of that string
src/tools/context.mjs:8 — the server's clock is `() => new Date().toISOString()`, so in normal operation the value is well-formed
survivors.mechanism: The pattern (patterns.mjs:3-4) is anchored only at the start, so '2026-99-99T99:99:99 anything at all' validates against threadSchema (thread.schema.mjs:109-110) and bindingSchema (binding.schema.mjs:25). It also validates digit shape rather than date validity — month 99 and hour 99 pass. In server operation the values come from `now()` (context.mjs:8), which is `new Date().toISOString()`, so a caller cannot inject a bad timestamp through any tool input schema; the exposure is to hand-edited, restored, or externally-written ledger records, which are then trusted by briefing.mjs:43 and by the created_at sort in rebuild-index.mjs:5-15.
survivors.model_impact: No direct model-caller impact, since no tool accepts a timestamp argument. It matters only as a validation-coverage hole: the write path's timestamp check does not actually establish that stored timestamps are meaningful, so a corrupted ledger passes assertValidThread and produces a nonsense 'last worked' line in the briefing and an arbitrary thread ordering, with the schema layer having certified the record as valid.
survivors.failure_scenario: A ledger record restored from a partial merge or hand-edited carries updated_at '2026-13-45T00:00:00Z'. assertValidThread accepts it; the briefing header renders 'last worked 2026-13-45'; rebuild-index sorts it after every real thread.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading and by direct regex test. src/schema/patterns.mjs:3-4 is `'^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}'` — leading ^ with no trailing $; `new RegExp(that).test('2026-99-99T99:99:99 anything at all')` returns true, so both trailing garbage and impossible components pass. It gates created_at and updated_at at src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:109-110 and binding created_at at src/schema/binding.schema.mjs:25. The finder's scoping is honest and I re-checked it: I grepped every file in src/tools/ for created_at/updated_at and found only handler-side assignments (transition-thread.mjs:33, archive-thread.mjs:22, record-decision.mjs:74, update-thread.mjs:122, amend-criteria.mjs:114, reopen.mjs:26) — no input schema accepts a timestamp, and the clock is `() => new Date().toISOString()` at src/tools/context.mjs:8. So there is no model-caller path to inject a bad timestamp; the exposure is corrupt or hand-edited storage that assertValidThread would certify, feeding src/render/briefing.mjs:43 and the created_at sort at src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:5-15. Low is right.

survivors.title: debrief's only source of thread_id is a SessionStart text injection that no tool can re-fetch, so a compacted or long session cannot address any write tool
evidence: skills/debrief/SKILL.md:11 — "Its `thread_id` is the active thread the SessionStart context surfaced ... Pass that `thread_id` to every write below."
hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:100-101 — roster is fetched via `invokeCliJson(['roster'])` and returned as `additionalContext` text, once, at session start
hooks/lib/roster.mjs:33 — the injected line is `- [status] slug (d of t): title -- next: ... (id <ULID>)`; the ULID exists only inside that prose
src/tools/registry.mjs:19-34 — TOOLS lists all 14 tools; none lists or searches threads
src/tools/rebuild-index.mjs:4-7 — handler returns `{ counts }` only, never the roster

hooks/lib/user-prompt-submit.mjs:3 — RESUME_INTENT regex; verified empirically that 'session handoff', 'wrap up', 'hand off', 'handoff summary' all return false, so the roster is NOT re-injected on any debrief trigger phrase
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:3 — those same phrases are debrief's declared triggers
hooks/lib/pre-compact.mjs:12-19 — the PreCompact checkpoint records event/session_id/transcript_path/trigger/custom_instructions/recorded_at and no thread id
survivors.mechanism: The ULID the entire write side depends on reaches the model exactly once, as free text in a SessionStart `additionalContext` block (hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:101, hooks/lib/roster.mjs:33). Every debrief tool requires it as a ULID-patterned argument (e.g. src/tools/append-session-event.mjs:23, src/tools/update-thread.mjs:136). No registered tool returns a thread list (src/tools/registry.mjs:19-34), and rebuild_index — the one tool debrief calls that touches the roster — returns only counts (src/tools/rebuild-index.mjs:6). The UserPromptSubmit re-injection is gated on a resume-intent regex (hooks/lib/user-prompt-submit.mjs:3,11-13) that, verified by running it, matches none of debrief's own trigger phrases (skills/debrief/SKILL.md:3). PreCompact writes a checkpoint that does not carry the id (hooks/lib/pre-compact.mjs:12-19). So once the injected text falls out of context — the exact condition debrief runs under — the id is unrecoverable through the server.
survivors.model_impact: At wrap-up the model either fabricates a ULID (rejected by the ajv pattern, or worse, accepted if it happens to name another thread), or guesses from memory, or silently skips the ledger write and prints only the chat summary. The session's entire continuity payload is lost with no error anywhere, and the next preflight presents the previous session's spine as current.
survivors.failure_scenario: Long session, context compacted at 70% (hooks/lib/post-tool-use.mjs:49 nudges but does not preserve the id). User types 'wrap up'. UserPromptSubmit does not re-inject the roster. The model has no tool that returns a thread_id and no id in context; it writes nothing and reports a hand-off it did not perform.

verdict.correction: Accurate narrower claim: no MCP tool in the registry can re-fetch a thread_id, and debrief's only stated source is the one-time SessionStart injection. But the id is not 'unrecoverable' — two paths exist that the finding does not account for, so 'critical / a compacted session cannot address any write tool' is not supported by the code.
verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED parts, my own citations: hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:100-101 fetches the roster via invokeCliJson(['roster']) and returns formatRoster(roster) as SessionStart additionalContext; hooks/lib/roster.mjs:33 is the only place the ULID appears, embedded in prose as `(id ${id})`. src/tools/registry.mjs:19-34 lists all 14 tools and none returns a thread list — I read every handler; the closest, src/tools/rebuild-index.mjs:4-7, returns `{ counts }` and src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:63-73 confirms those counts are integers only. hooks/lib/user-prompt-submit.mjs:3 RESUME_INTENT is /\b(resume|resuming|pick up where|catch me up|where (?:did|were) we|last session|continue where we|carry on where we)\b/i — none of debrief's declared triggers at skills/debrief/SKILL.md:3 ('session handoff', 'wrap up', 'hand off', 'handoff summary') contain any alternative. hooks/lib/pre-compact.mjs:12-19 records event/session_id/transcript_path/trigger/custom_instructions/recorded_at and no thread id. OVERSTATED because: (1) hooks/hooks.json:3 registers SessionStart with NO source matcher, so every SessionStart the harness emits re-injects the roster; whether the harness emits one after compaction is external to this repo, so the finding's central 'compacted session' premise is not settleable from code and it asserts it as certain. (2) bin/ledger-cli.mjs:22-26 exposes `roster` on the CLI, and hooks/lib/pre-tool-use.mjs:11 + :89-91 + :100-104 classify a Bash command as `ask`/`deny` only when it contains '_ledger', 'refs/ledger/', 'CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA' or a resolved root spelling — a plain `node <plugin>/bin/ledger-cli.mjs roster` matches none, so it returns null (unclassified, no prompt). The roster is therefore recoverable outside MCP. (3) hooks/lib/stop.mjs:8 prints the ULID back to the model on the block path. The real, code-provable defect is narrower: the MCP surface has no read-side thread enumeration at all.

survivors.title: The Stop hook is the only mechanism forcing a debrief, and it fires only on the active-thread pointer, which nothing in the documented preflight flow ever sets
evidence: hooks/lib/stop.mjs:101-104 — blocks only when `ledger-cli active-thread` returns a string thread_id
src/util/active-thread.mjs:32-39 — writeActiveThread is the only writer of that file

src/tools/open-thread.mjs:19, src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:14, src/tools/reopen.mjs:29, src/tools/create-successor.mjs:22, src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:40-41 — the complete set of callers of writeActiveThread
skills/preflight/SKILL.md:4 — allowed-tools is reconcile, rebuild_index, get_resume_brief, read_decision only
test/unit/skills/preflight.test.mjs:44-49 — asserts preflight must NOT allow transition_thread, update_thread, record_decision or append_session_event
src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:42-44 — the pointer is cleared only when the STORED status was 'active'
src/render/briefing.mjs:88-90 — NEXT STEP is rendered from spine.next_step unconditionally
survivors.mechanism: handleStop blocks the turn only when the active-thread file is non-empty (hooks/lib/stop.mjs:101-104). That file is written by exactly five handlers (src/tools/open-thread.mjs:19, bind-branch.mjs:14, reopen.mjs:29, create-successor.mjs:22, transition-thread.mjs:40-41). Preflight calls none of them — its allowed-tools are four read tools (skills/preflight/SKILL.md:4) and test/unit/skills/preflight.test.mjs:44-49 asserts that as an invariant. A session that resumes an existing paused thread therefore ends with the pointer absent, the Stop hook silent, and the thread's spine exactly as the previous session left it. src/render/briefing.mjs:88-90 then prints that stale next_step at the top of the next briefing with no marker that it is a session old.
survivors.model_impact: The guardrail the system relies on to force a hand-off is inert for the normal resume flow. A model that forgets debrief — the likeliest outcome given finding 'debrief-payload-scheduling-mismatch' — gets no signal, and the next session is briefed with stale forward-looking text presented as current instruction.
survivors.failure_scenario: Session 2 resumes thread X via preflight (X stays 'paused'), work happens, the user closes the session without saying 'wrap up'. Stop hook sees no pointer, does not block, runs `sync` and exits 0 (hooks/lib/stop.mjs:106-107). Session 3's briefing prints session 1's NEXT STEP as the next action.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived. hooks/lib/stop.mjs:101-104: handleStop reads `active-thread` via the CLI and returns exitCode 2 only when `active.thread_id` is a string. bin/ledger-cli.mjs:28-31 shows that value comes from readActiveThread, and src/util/active-thread.mjs:41-53 returns null on ENOENT. I grepped writeActiveThread across src/, bin/, hooks/: the complete writer set is src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:14, src/tools/reopen.mjs:29, src/tools/create-successor.mjs:22, src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:41, src/tools/open-thread.mjs:19 — no others. skills/preflight/SKILL.md:4 allows only reconcile, rebuild_index, get_resume_brief, read_decision (both spellings), and test/unit/skills/preflight.test.mjs:44-49 asserts the write tools are excluded. src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:40-41 arms the pointer only for `to_status === 'active'`, which no skill calls. So a session that resumes a paused thread ends with the pointer absent and the Stop hook silent. I also checked the only other pointer-clearing path: src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:42-44 gates the clear on the STORED status being 'active'. And src/render/briefing.mjs:88-90 renders spine.next_step unconditionally with no freshness marker, so the next briefing repeats last session's text. The finding's 'only forcing mechanism' wording holds — hooks/lib/post-tool-use.mjs:49-50 emits only advisory additionalContext, not a block.

survivors.title: The user-global continuity rule points the model at <repo>/.claude/ledger/ markdown files, which is not a guarded path and not a path any tool reads
evidence: /Users/satanshumishra/Documents/DevLabs/.windful-ocean/.claude/rules/common/continuity-ledger.md:7 — "Git projects: `<repo>/.claude/ledger/`, committed."

/Users/satanshumishra/Documents/DevLabs/.windful-ocean/.claude/rules/common/continuity-ledger.md:8 — `PROJECT.md`, `threads/<slug>.md`, `decisions/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`, `sessions/YYYY-MM-DD-NN-<thread-slug>.md`
hooks/lib/ledger-roots.mjs:6-21 — resolveLedgerRoots returns only `<CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA>/<projectKey>` and `<git-common-dir>/ledger`
hooks/lib/pre-tool-use.mjs:127-133 — Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit are denied only when the target `isUnderRoot(path, roots, baseDir)`
src/util/active-thread.mjs:18-29 — the real store is `<git-common-dir>/ledger` or `<CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA>/<projectKey>`
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:212 — decisions are written as `decisions/<nnnn>-<slug>.md`
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:246-249 — session events are written as `sessions/<threadId>/<iso>--<actor>.md`
survivors.mechanism: The always-loaded global rule names a file layout (continuity-ledger.md:7-8) that this server does not use: the server stores threads under `<git-common-dir>/ledger` or `<CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA>/<projectKey>` (src/util/active-thread.mjs:18-29) with entirely different filenames (src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:212, :246-249). The PreToolUse guard denies direct writes only under the roots it resolves (hooks/lib/ledger-roots.mjs:6-21, hooks/lib/pre-tool-use.mjs:127-133), and `<repo>/.claude/ledger/` is not among them. So a model obeying the global rule writes `PROJECT.md`, `threads/*.md` and `decisions/YYYY-MM-DD-*.md` into the repo, unimpeded and uncommented-on.
survivors.model_impact: The model believes it has recorded continuity, and it has — into a directory the MCP server never reads and the roster never indexes. The next session's SessionStart roster shows nothing from it. The user gets a plausible-looking committed ledger that is pure fiction relative to the actual store.
survivors.failure_scenario: Model recalls the global rule at wrap-up, writes `.claude/ledger/threads/auth-refactor.md` with the spine. No hook fires. Next session, the SessionStart roster is empty or stale, and the briefing contains none of it.

verdict.correction: The path mismatch is real, but 'not a path any tool reads' is false in this environment, and the artifact is outside the audited repo, so 'critical' overstates it. Accurate claim: the user-global continuity rule names <repo>/.claude/ledger/, which is outside every root the PreToolUse guard resolves and outside every path this MCP server reads or indexes.
verdict.reasoning: Verified path facts myself. hooks/lib/ledger-roots.mjs:6-21 resolveLedgerRoots returns at most `<CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA>/<projectKey>` and `join(gitCommonDir, 'ledger')`; I ran `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` in this repo and it returns `.git`, so the guarded root is `<repo>/.git/ledger`, not `<repo>/.claude/ledger`. hooks/lib/pre-tool-use.mjs:127-133 denies Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit only when isUnderRoot(path, roots, baseDir) — `<repo>/.claude/ledger/PROJECT.md` is not under those roots, so it is not denied. src/util/active-thread.mjs:18-29 and src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:212 (`decisions/<nnnn>-<slug>.md`) and :246-249 (`sessions/<threadId>/<iso>--<actor>.md`) confirm the real store's location and filename grammar differ. The quoted rule line is real: /Users/satanshumishra/Documents/DevLabs/.windful-ocean/.claude/rules/common/continuity-ledger.md:7-8. REASONS FOR DOWNGRADE: (a) the file is user-global config, not a file in the repo under audit, so no change to logbook can fix it; (b) 'not a path any tool reads' is contradicted by this environment's own skill roster, which contains `resume-project` ('Reads the ARCHIVED v1 file ledger under .claude/ledger/') and `session-handoff` ('Writes the legacy v1 markdown file ledger under .claude/ledger/') — that directory is the designated v1 archive, read by those skills, so writes there are not orphaned in the way the finding claims. I also confirmed `<repo>/.claude/` currently contains only settings.local.json and reports/, i.e. no ledger has actually been written there.

survivors.title: debrief step 5's replace_scopes instruction, followed literally without also submitting key_decisions, deletes the spine links to the decisions step 3 just created
evidence: skills/debrief/SKILL.md:32 — "`replace_scopes`: name every scope whose risks or decisions you are restating in full, including one whose last item you are retiring."
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:27-31 — the enumerated fields to write are active_goal, next_step, last_session, open_risks, out_of_scope; key_decisions is never listed
