survivors.model_impact: The model executes the skill exactly as written and destroys its own step-3 output, with a 200-OK-shaped result. The loss is invisible until a future session's briefing is missing the decisions, and by then no error exists to trace.
survivors.failure_scenario: Debrief records decision 0007 under scope c3 (step 3), then calls update_thread with `replace_scopes: {key_decisions: ['c3'], open_risks: ['c3']}` and a spine patch containing only active_goal/next_step/last_session/open_risks. spine.key_decisions loses 0007. Next preflight: DECIDED ON THIS STEP is omitted entirely (src/render/briefing.mjs:122) and NOT SHOWN reports 0.

verdict.reasoning: I traced the deletion myself. src/tools/update-thread.mjs:116-121: replaceScopes is normalized, spinePatch is null when `spine` is absent, and `clearsAScope` (line 118) is true when any scoped field's replace list is non-empty, so patchSpine runs with `spinePatch ?? {}`. src/tools/update-thread.mjs:18-27 replaceScopedItems: with `submitted` undefined and `authoritative = ['c3']`, the early return at line 20 does not fire (authoritative.length is 1), `incoming = []`, `replaced = new Set(['c3'])`, and `carried` filters out every stored item whose scope is 'c3' — the return is `[]`. Line 64-68 passes key_decisions through that same function with replaceScopes.key_decisions. src/tools/record-decision.mjs:66-70 is what put those entries there. src/render/briefing.mjs:119-127 renders the DECIDED block only from spine.key_decisions, so the links are gone from the briefing; src/render/briefing.mjs:147-158 would not even count them. The skill side checks out too: skills/debrief/SKILL.md:27-32 enumerates active_goal, next_step, last_session, open_risks, out_of_scope and replace_scopes — key_decisions is absent — while line 32 tells the model to name every scope whose 'risks or decisions' it is restating, without ever revealing that replace_scopes is keyed per field. A model restating only risks for c3 can plausibly emit replace_scopes.key_decisions:['c3'] and silently drop the decision links, and src/tools/update-thread.mjs:123-125 returns success.

survivors.title: debrief step 4 instructs promoting work to a child thread, but no tool that creates a thread is in the skill's allowed-tools or prose, and the detour-nesting refusal that forces the choice is unstated
evidence: skills/debrief/SKILL.md:24 — "Work that needs its own criteria, or that will outlive this session, is a child thread instead, not a detour."
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:4 — allowed-tools lists only append_session_event, record_decision, amend_criteria, update_thread, transition_thread, rebuild_index (both spellings)
src/tools/open-thread.mjs:33-34 — open_thread is the only handler accepting `parent_id`
src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:50-56 — a detour insert is refused while any live detour has done !== true: "detours do not nest; open a child thread for work that needs its own criteria"
grep over README.md, skills/, .claude-plugin/ — `open_thread`, `reopen`, `bind_branch`, `create_successor`, `archive_thread` appear in none of them
survivors.mechanism: The only way to create a child thread is open_thread with parent_id (src/tools/open-thread.mjs:33-34). open_thread is absent from debrief's allowed-tools (skills/debrief/SKILL.md:4) and from every line of prose in both skills and the README (verified by grep). The server's own refusal message for a nested detour repeats the same advice (src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:53-55), so the model is told twice to do something it has no permitted tool for. The skill also never states the nesting refusal itself, so the model learns it only by having a valid-looking amend_criteria call rejected.
survivors.model_impact: Second detour in a session: the call is refused, the error tells the model to open a child thread, the skill tells it the same, and the tool is not available. The model either abandons the record (losing the unplanned work from the ledger entirely) or breaks out of the skill's tool contract.
survivors.failure_scenario: Session hits two unplanned issues. First `amend_criteria` insert detour succeeds. Second returns 'criterion "c7" is an open detour and detours do not nest; open a child thread'. Neither debrief nor its allowed-tools offers open_thread.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived. src/tools/open-thread.mjs:34 is the only inputSchema in src/tools/ that accepts `parent_id`; I checked src/tools/create-successor.mjs:33-38, whose schema has no parent_id (it inherits predecessor.parent_id internally at :19). skills/debrief/SKILL.md:4 allows exactly append_session_event, record_decision, amend_criteria, update_thread, transition_thread, rebuild_index under both spellings — open_thread is not among them, and test/unit/skills/debrief.test.mjs:34-35 asserts that list is EXACT. I ran `grep -rn 'open_thread' README.md skills/` and it exits 1 (no match); the same for reopen/bind_branch/create_successor/archive_thread across README.md, skills/ and .claude-plugin/. src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:50-56 confirms the refusal text: a second detour while `liveCriteria(thread).find(c => c.kind === 'detour' && c.done !== true)` is truthy throws '...detours do not nest; open a child thread for work that needs its own criteria'. So both the skill (SKILL.md:24) and the server's own error direct the model to a tool the skill's allowed-tools withholds, and the nesting rule itself is never stated in the skill.

survivors.title: A malformed amend_criteria operation returns an ajv oneOf error listing required properties from all three branches, actively directing the model to add fields the operation it intends must not have
evidence: src/tools/schemas.mjs:72-109 — criteriaAmendOperation is `{required:['op'], oneOf:[insert, rewrite, strike]}`, each branch `additionalProperties:false`
src/tools/registry.mjs:36 — `new Ajv({ allErrors: true })`

src/schema/validators.mjs:9-11 — formatValidationErrors emits only `instancePath` + `message`, discarding `e.params`, so 'must be equal to constant' never names the constant and 'must NOT have additional properties' never names the property
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:24 — tells the model to insert with `kind` `detour` but never states that `text` AND `kind` are both required
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:25 — tells the model to `rewrite` with a `decision_ref` but never states that `text` is also required
survivors.mechanism: Verified by running callTool against the live registry. `{op:'insert', text:'do the thing'}` (missing kind) returns: "must have required property 'kind'; must have required property 'id'; must have required property 'decision_ref'; /operations/0/op must be equal to constant; must have required property 'id'; must have required property 'decision_ref'; must NOT have additional properties; /operations/0/op must be equal to constant; must match exactly one schema in oneOf". Six of the nine clauses come from the rewrite and strike branches and are wrong for an insert. `{op:'rewrite', id, decision_ref}` (missing text) similarly reports 'must have required property kind' and two unattributed 'must NOT have additional properties'. Because formatValidationErrors drops params (src/schema/validators.mjs:10), the model cannot tell which branch or which property each clause refers to.
survivors.model_impact: This is the known record_decision incident's exact failure mode with a larger blast radius: the error's most prominent suggestions (add `id`, add `decision_ref`) are impossible for the operation the skill told the model to write, so the model retries a wrong hypothesis. amend_criteria is also atomic (src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:110-113), so one bad operation discards the whole batch.
survivors.failure_scenario: Debrief step 4, model emits `{op:'insert', text:'fixed the flaky test'}`. Error says to add `id` and `decision_ref`. Model adds them. Now the insert branch fails on additionalProperties and the strike branch on the op constant. Loop.

verdict.reasoning: I reproduced both errors against the live registry rather than trusting the quote. `callTool('amend_criteria', {thread_id:<ulid>, operations:[{op:'insert', text:'do the thing'}]})` returns exactly: "/operations/0 must have required property 'kind'; /operations/0 must have required property 'id'; /operations/0 must have required property 'decision_ref'; /operations/0/op must be equal to constant; /operations/0 must have required property 'id'; /operations/0 must have required property 'decision_ref'; /operations/0 must NOT have additional properties; /operations/0/op must be equal to constant; /operations/0 must match exactly one schema in oneOf" — six of nine clauses come from the rewrite/strike branches. `{op:'rewrite', id:'c1', decision_ref:'0001-x'}` returns "...must have required property 'text'; ...must have required property 'kind'; ...must NOT have additional properties; ...must NOT have additional properties; ...op must be equal to constant; ...must have required property 'text'; ...op must be equal to constant; ...must match exactly one schema in oneOf". Schema confirmed at src/tools/schemas.mjs:72-109 (required:['op'] plus a three-branch oneOf, each additionalProperties:false); src/tools/registry.mjs:36 is `new Ajv({ allErrors: true })`; src/schema/validators.mjs:9-11 maps errors to `instancePath + message` only, discarding e.params, so 'must be equal to constant' never names the constant and 'must NOT have additional properties' never names the property. One narrowing worth stating: the full inputSchema IS published to the model (src/tools/registry.mjs:53-55 listTools returns inputSchema), so the model can in principle read the branches; the defect is that the ERROR actively points at the wrong branch, which is the known-incident failure mode. Atomicity confirmed at src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:110-115 (single reduce, single writeThread).

survivors.title: bind_branch writes the active-thread pointer regardless of thread status, but transition_thread and archive_thread clear it only when the stored status is 'active', so a bound paused thread leaves a pointer that debrief cannot clear
evidence: src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:8-14 — reads the thread, does not check its status, calls writeActiveThread unconditionally
src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:42-44 — `else if (thread.status === 'active' && (await readActiveThread(ctx)) === candidate.id)` is the only clear path
src/tools/archive-thread.mjs:25-27 — same `thread.status === 'active'` guard
src/model/fsm.mjs:13 — `paused: ['active','done','abandoned']`, so paused -> paused is refused
src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:18 — `illegal transition ${thread.status} -> ${to}`
hooks/lib/stop.mjs:101-104 and hooks/lib/stop.mjs:8 — blocks with "thread X is still active. Run the debrief skill to hand it off (which pauses the thread and clears the active-thread pointer)"
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:38 — "Parking the worked thread clears the active-thread pointer server-side."
hooks/commit-msg:44-52 — every commit reads `$common_dir/ledger/active-thread` and stamps a `Thread-Id:` trailer from it
survivors.mechanism: bind_branch writes the pointer for a thread of any status (src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:14). If the thread is paused, the Stop hook then blocks the turn with a message asserting the thread is 'active' and that debrief will clear the pointer (hooks/lib/stop.mjs:8,101-104). Debrief's step 6 parks at paused (skills/debrief/SKILL.md:35), which the FSM refuses from paused (src/model/fsm.mjs:13, src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:18). Even if the model instead closes the thread paused -> done, the clear branch is skipped because it tests the STORED status (src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:42), so the pointer survives on a terminal thread. The commit-msg hook then stamps every subsequent commit in the repo with that dead thread's id (hooks/commit-msg:44-52).
survivors.model_impact: The Stop hook's reason text and the skill's step-6 claim both describe a clearing that will not happen, so the model's correct-per-instructions response fails and it has no documented recovery (reopen is not in either skill). Meanwhile commits are mislabelled with a stale Thread-Id, corrupting the trailer-based reattachment in src/drift/reattach.mjs:20-22.
survivors.failure_scenario: Model calls bind_branch on paused thread X to associate the feature branch. Session ends. Stop blocks: 'thread X is still active'. Debrief runs transition_thread(paused) -> 'illegal transition paused -> paused'. Model closes it done instead; pointer remains. Every later commit in the repo gets `Thread-Id: X`.

verdict.reasoning: Mechanism verified line by line. src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:6-16: the handler reads the thread, never inspects thread.status, and calls writeActiveThread(ctx, thread.id) unconditionally at :14. src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:40-44: the pointer is cleared only in the `else if (thread.status === 'active' && (await readActiveThread(ctx)) === candidate.id)` branch — keyed on the STORED status. src/tools/archive-thread.mjs:25-27 has the identical guard. src/model/fsm.mjs:11-17 gives paused: ['active','done','abandoned'], so paused->paused is refused at src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:17-19, and a paused->done close skips the clear branch because thread.status is 'paused' — the pointer survives on a terminal thread, exactly as claimed. hooks/lib/stop.mjs:8 then asserts 'thread X is still active' and promises debrief 'pauses the thread and clears the active-thread pointer', which skills/debrief/SKILL.md:38 repeats. hooks/commit-msg:44-53 reads `$common_dir/ledger/active-thread`, validates 26 Crockford chars, and stamps `Thread-Id:` on every subsequent commit; src/drift/reattach.mjs:19-23 resolves that trailer first. DOWNGRADE to medium: bind_branch is the sole trigger and it appears in neither skill's allowed-tools (skills/preflight/SKILL.md:4, skills/debrief/SKILL.md:4) nor anywhere in README.md or skills/ (grep exits 1), so the stranding is unreachable through the documented flow. I checked every other pointer writer — open_thread, reopen, create_successor and transition_thread(to:'active') all leave the thread in status 'active', so none can strand it.

survivors.title: Calling get_resume_brief writes a pledge that makes the Stop hook block the turn until the exact briefing text appears in an assistant message, and the skill never says the call itself creates that obligation
evidence: src/tools/get-resume-brief.mjs:30-34 — every call writes `{thread_id, rendered, rendered_at}` to the BRIEFING_INDEX pledge file
hooks/lib/stop.mjs:83-93 — verbatimGate: if a pledge exists, assistant texts are non-empty, and none contains `pledge.rendered` verbatim, return exitCode 2 with the whole briefing on stderr
hooks/lib/stop.mjs:91 — the pledge is cleared only after a successful echo (or when the transcript yields no assistant text)
skills/preflight/SKILL.md:24 — instructs the verbatim print but says nothing about the pledge, the Stop-hook gate, or that the obligation is created by the call rather than by the decision to brief
survivors.mechanism: get_resume_brief unconditionally writes the pledge as a side effect of rendering (src/tools/get-resume-brief.mjs:30-34). handleStop reads it and blocks the turn end unless some assistant message contains the rendered string as an exact substring (hooks/lib/stop.mjs:83-93). The pledge is only cleared by a matching echo (hooks/lib/stop.mjs:91). The skill (skills/preflight/SKILL.md:24) presents the verbatim print as an instruction, not as a machine-enforced debt incurred at call time.
survivors.model_impact: Any turn in which the model calls get_resume_brief and then does not print the result — user interrupts, model summarizes instead, model briefs two threads and prints only the second — is blocked, and the entire briefing is re-emitted on stderr and must be printed. The model has no way to cancel the obligation through any tool, since no MCP tool clears the pledge (only `ledger-cli briefing-pledge --clear`, bin/ledger-cli.mjs:54-56, which the model cannot call without Bash into a guarded area).
survivors.failure_scenario: Model calls get_resume_brief for thread A, user immediately says 'no, the other one', model calls it for thread B and prints B. Pledge now holds B, echoed, fine. Reverse the order — model prints A then re-briefs B without printing — and the turn is blocked with B's full text forced onto the screen.

verdict.correction: Accurate claim: get_resume_brief writes the verbatim pledge as an unannounced side effect, and a turn that ends without echoing it is blocked ONCE. It is not an uncancellable obligation, and the 'briefs two threads, prints only the second' example is wrong.
verdict.reasoning: src/tools/get-resume-brief.mjs:30-34 does write {thread_id, rendered, rendered_at} to BRIEFING_INDEX on every call — that part is right, and skills/preflight/SKILL.md:24 does not mention it. But I read the gate in full, which the finder did not. hooks/lib/stop.mjs:83-93: the block at :88-89 requires `texts.length > 0 && !echoed && !stopHookActive`; on the very next Stop, `stop_hook_active` is true (hooks/lib/stop.mjs:96), so the condition is false and line 91 `await clearPledge(ctx)` runs and the gate returns null. The obligation therefore self-clears after a single block — the model is not held until it prints, and it does have a cancellation path (any second stop). The finding's claim that no MCP tool clears the pledge is technically true (bin/ledger-cli.mjs:51-58 owns --clear) but is moot given the self-clear. The two-thread example is refuted outright: src/tools/get-resume-brief.mjs:30 calls writeIndexFile(BRIEFING_INDEX, ...), which overwrites, so after briefing two threads only the SECOND rendering is pledged and printing it satisfies the gate. hooks/lib/stop.mjs:88 also passes the gate when the transcript yields no assistant text at all.

survivors.title: record_decision requires context and outcome but enforces no minLength, so an empty-string decision record is written, committed and linked into the spine as if complete
evidence: src/tools/record-decision.mjs:92 — `context: { type: 'string' }` with no minLength
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:99 — `outcome: { type: 'string' }` with no minLength
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:91 — `title: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` for contrast
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:16-40 — renderDecision interpolates context and outcome raw into `## Context` and `## Outcome` sections
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:66-77 — the file is written, appended to spine.key_decisions and committed
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:21 — "call `mcp__ledger__record_decision` with the `thread_id`, a kebab-case `slug`, a `title`, the `context`, the `options` you weighed ... and the `outcome`"
survivors.mechanism: options has a handler-level emptiness check that throws (src/tools/record-decision.mjs:44-47) and title has minLength 1 (src/tools/record-decision.mjs:91), but context and outcome have neither (src/tools/record-decision.mjs:92,99). An empty string for either passes ajv and the handler, renderDecision emits a heading followed by a blank line (src/tools/record-decision.mjs:16-40), the file is written and committed, and the ref is appended to spine.key_decisions (src/tools/record-decision.mjs:66-70).
survivors.model_impact: A model under context pressure that emits `"context": ""` to save tokens — or that mis-emits the field the way the known incident mis-emitted options — creates a permanent, numbered, append-only MADR record with no rationale, and the ledger reports success. Decisions are the one thing the design says is never compressed away; a hollow one is worse than a missing one because the spine and the briefing both count it as recorded.
survivors.failure_scenario: Debrief step 3 with an exhausted context: `record_decision(thread_id, slug:'use-git-refs', title:'Use git refs', context:'', options:['refs','files'], outcome:'')`. Returns `{number:'0009', path:...}`. The next session reads decision 0009 and finds two empty sections.

verdict.reasoning: Verified against the schema, not the name. src/tools/record-decision.mjs:87 requires ['thread_id','slug','title','context','options','outcome']; :92 is `context: { type: 'string' }` and :99 is `outcome: { type: 'string' }` — neither carries minLength, while :91 is `title: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` and :90 constrains slug by pattern. The only handler-level emptiness check is on options (:44-47, after normalizeOptions at :8-14). renderDecision at :16-40 interpolates context and outcome raw under '## Context' and '## Outcome'. Nothing downstream saves it: src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:202-213 writeDecision validates only the number, slug pattern and that markdown is a string; the decision file is never schema-validated, and :66-77 writes it, appends {ref,title,scope} to spine.key_decisions and commits. skills/debrief/SKILL.md:21 names all six fields without any content requirement. So an empty-string context or outcome produces a permanent numbered MADR record with a blank rationale and a success result.

survivors.title: preflight tells the model to call read_decision 'with that number', but the parameter is named nnnn and must be a string of at least four digits, so the natural JSON emission is rejected twice
evidence: skills/preflight/SKILL.md:26 — "The briefing names decisions by number. If the user asks about one, call `mcp__ledger__read_decision` with that number."
src/tools/read-decision.mjs:25 — `nnnn: { type: 'string', pattern: '^[0-9]{4,}$' }`
src/render/briefing.mjs:125 — decisions render as `- ${decisionNumber(d.ref)} — title`, i.e. the bare zero-padded digits
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:199 — numbers are produced as `String(max + 1).padStart(4, '0')`
survivors.mechanism: The briefing shows a decision as `- 0009 — title` (src/render/briefing.mjs:125). The skill says to call read_decision with 'that number' and names no parameter (skills/preflight/SKILL.md:26). The schema requires a string parameter called `nnnn` matching `^[0-9]{4,}$` (src/tools/read-decision.mjs:25). Verified against the live registry: `{nnnn: 12}` returns "/nnnn must be string" and `{nnnn: '12'}` returns "/nnnn must match pattern". JSON cannot express `0009` as a numeric literal at all, so the only correct emission is the quoted, zero-padded form — which the skill never states.
survivors.model_impact: Two guaranteed rejections on a read-only drill-down the user explicitly asked for, at the moment the model has just been told to STOP and hand control back. Each rejection costs a round trip and the second error ('must match pattern') gives no hint that zero-padding is what is missing.
survivors.failure_scenario: User: 'what was decision 9?'. Model emits `{nnnn: 9}` -> must be string. Model emits `{nnnn: '9'}` -> must match pattern ^[0-9]{4,}$. Model must infer zero-padding from a regex.

verdict.correction: Accurate claim: the preflight skill says 'that number' (skills/preflight/SKILL.md:26) while the parameter is a zero-padded string named nnnn. But the full inputSchema is published to the model, so 'two guaranteed rejections' is not supported by the code.
verdict.reasoning: I reproduced both rejections: callTool('read_decision', {nnnn: 12}) -> '/nnnn must be string'; {nnnn: '12'} -> '/nnnn must match pattern "^[0-9]{4,}$"'. Schema confirmed at src/tools/read-decision.mjs:25. Rendering confirmed at src/render/briefing.mjs:125 (`- ${decisionNumber(d.ref)} — ...`) with decisionNumber at :14-18 returning the leading 4+ digits, and src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:199 producing `String(max + 1).padStart(4, '0')`. WHY OVERSTATED: src/tools/registry.mjs:53-55 listTools returns each tool's full inputSchema to the client, so the model is shown `type: 'string'` and the pattern before it ever calls; src/tools/read-decision.mjs:19 additionally describes it as 'by its four-digit number'. The rejection is a plausible model error, not a code-guaranteed one, and the claim of certainty rests on model behavior the code cannot settle. The genuine, provable defect is only the skill-prose/parameter mismatch, and it costs at most a read-only retry.

verdict.reasoning: All three legs verified independently. src/model/selection.mjs:16-23 — resolveWriteScope returns the first not-done live criterion id, else the last, else 'thread'

skills/debrief/SKILL.md:21 — step 3 lists thread_id, slug, title, context, options, outcome; `scope` is never named
src/model/selection.mjs:39-42 — visibleScopes = {'thread', anchor.id}
src/render/briefing.mjs:119-127 — decisions are filtered by visibleScopes
src/render/briefing.mjs:147-158 — hidden decisions are reduced to a bare count in NOT SHOWN
survivors.mechanism: record_decision defaults scope to the anchor criterion (src/tools/record-decision.mjs:52-55, src/model/selection.mjs:16-23). Debrief step 3 runs before step 5's criterion toggles (skills/debrief/SKILL.md:21,27), so the decision is scoped to the criterion the session was closing. Once step 5 flips that criterion done, the next session's anchor is the following criterion (src/model/selection.mjs:16-18), visibleScopes no longer contains the decision's scope (src/model/selection.mjs:39-42), and the briefing renders it only as a number in NOT SHOWN (src/render/briefing.mjs:150-157). The skill never mentions that `scope: 'thread'` exists and is what makes a decision standing.
survivors.model_impact: Cross-cutting architectural decisions — the ones most worth carrying forward — are systematically demoted to a count on the very next resume, and the model has no documented way to prevent it. It cannot even fix it afterwards, because debrief step 5 never lists key_decisions as a writable spine field.
survivors.failure_scenario: Session closes criterion c3 and records 'adopt git-ref storage for all threads' with the default scope c3. Next session's briefing shows 'DECIDED ON THIS STEP' for c4 (empty, so omitted) and 'NOT SHOWN: 0 risk(s) and 1 decision(s) from other steps'.

verdict.reasoning: Mechanism re-derived. src/tools/record-decision.mjs:52-55: `scope = assertWritableScope(args.scope ?? resolveWriteScope(thread), ...)`. src/model/selection.mjs:20-23 resolveWriteScope returns anchorCriterion(liveCriteria(thread)).id, and :16-18 anchorCriterion is `live.find(c => c.done !== true) ?? live[live.length - 1] ?? null` — the first not-done criterion. Ordering: skills/debrief/SKILL.md:21 (step 3, record_decision) precedes SKILL.md:27 (step 5, criterion toggles), so the decision is scoped to the criterion the session is about to close. src/model/selection.mjs:39-42 builds visibleScopes as exactly {'thread', anchor.id}; src/render/briefing.mjs:119-127 filters key_decisions by that set and :147-158 reduces the rest to a bare count. So once the anchoring criterion flips done, the decision drops to a number in NOT SHOWN on the very next briefing. skills/debrief/SKILL.md:21 does not name `scope`. NARROWING I would attach: the finding's 'no documented way to prevent it' overreaches — src/tools/record-decision.mjs:100 publishes `scope` with pattern '^(c[1-9][0-9]*|thread)$' (src/schema/patterns.mjs:24) in the inputSchema the model receives, and src/tools/record-decision.mjs:83 states the default in the tool description; likewise src/tools/update-thread.mjs:145 does expose key_decisions as a writable spine field. The mechanism and the skill-side silence hold; the impossibility claim does not.

survivors.title: rebuild_index returns only counts and every mutating tool already reindexes, so both skills' explicit rebuild steps refresh a file the model cannot read and that was already current
evidence: skills/preflight/SKILL.md:15 — "Call `mcp__ledger__rebuild_index` so the resumable roster is current before you show anything."
skills/preflight/SKILL.md:17 — step 2 then shows the roster from the SessionStart context, not from step 1's result
src/tools/rebuild-index.mjs:4-7 — the handler returns `{ counts }`
src/tools/shared.mjs:19-23 — commitAndReindex calls rebuildIndex before every commit
src/tools/reconcile.mjs:8, src/tools/update-thread.mjs:124, src/tools/record-decision.mjs:77, src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:116, src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:46 — all route through commitAndReindex
bin/ledger-cli.mjs:22-26 — the SessionStart `roster` command itself calls rebuildIndex before reading the index
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:40 — "Rebuild the index. Call `mcp__ledger__rebuild_index` so the derived roster reflects this hand-off."
survivors.mechanism: The SessionStart roster CLI rebuilds the index before reading it (bin/ledger-cli.mjs:23-25), so the injected roster is already current when the model sees it. Preflight step 1 rebuilds again and receives only counts (src/tools/rebuild-index.mjs:6); the roster the model then presents in step 2 is the same injected text, so the refresh cannot affect what is shown. On the write side, transition_thread already reindexes through commitAndReindex (src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:46, src/tools/shared.mjs:19-23), so debrief step 7 rebuilds an index that step 6 just rebuilt.
survivors.model_impact: Two mandatory tool round-trips per session whose results the model cannot use and whose effects were already guaranteed. On the preflight side it also creates a false belief that the roster about to be presented is fresh, when it is whatever text SessionStart injected — possibly many turns and several thread mutations ago.
survivors.failure_scenario: A thread is opened mid-session. Later, preflight is invoked. Step 1's rebuild_index correctly indexes it and returns counts; step 2 presents the SessionStart roster, which predates the thread and omits it. The user cannot choose a thread that exists.

verdict.reasoning: Verified. bin/ledger-cli.mjs:22-26 runRoster calls rebuildIndex(ctx.driver) before readIndexFile('resumable'), and hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:98-101 runs sync, then reconcile, then that roster — so the injected roster is built from a freshly rebuilt index. src/tools/rebuild-index.mjs:4-7 returns `{ counts }` and src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:63-73 shows those are six integers, no roster payload. skills/preflight/SKILL.md:15 mandates the rebuild and :17 then presents 'the SessionStart context surfaces this roster', so the rebuild cannot change what is shown. On the write side src/tools/shared.mjs:19-23 commitAndReindex calls rebuildIndex before every commit, and I confirmed every mutating tool routes through it (src/tools/reconcile.mjs:8, update-thread.mjs:124, record-decision.mjs:77, amend-criteria.mjs:116, transition-thread.mjs:46), so skills/debrief/SKILL.md:40's step 7 rebuilds an index step 6 just rebuilt. I also checked that nothing between SessionStart and preflight step 1 can stale the index without reindexing — the only non-reindexing writer is append_session_event (src/tools/append-session-event.mjs:10-12), which touches no indexed field. Downgraded to low: the cost is two idempotent round-trips, and the false-freshness belief is a consequence of the skill's own step-2 wording rather than of the tool.

survivors.title: preflight step 3 mandates reconcile, but no skill ever creates a binding and SessionStart already reconciled, so the call reliably observes nothing while paying a commit and a full reindex
evidence: skills/preflight/SKILL.md:22 — "Call `mcp__ledger__reconcile`, which takes no arguments and runs across the whole ledger, before you brief on anything."
src/drift/reconcile.mjs:29-31 — the drift loop iterates `await driver.listBindings()`
src/drift/reconcile.mjs:50-51 — the reattach loop derives its repo set from those same bindings

src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:20-21 — bind_branch is the only tool that writes a binding; it appears in neither skill's allowed-tools (skills/preflight/SKILL.md:4, skills/debrief/SKILL.md:4) nor in any prose
hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:99 — SessionStart already runs `invokeCli(['reconcile'])`
docs/specs/2026-08-02-preflight-briefing-redesign.md:345-349 — "Reconcile runs twice in the normal resume flow ... so the second run observes nothing"
src/tools/reconcile.mjs:8 — the handler still calls commitAndReindex('chore(ledger): reconcile')
survivors.mechanism: runReconcile's entire work set is the binding list (src/drift/reconcile.mjs:29-31) and the repos derived from it (src/drift/reconcile.mjs:50-51). Bindings are created only by bind_branch (src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:20-21), which neither skill names. With zero bindings both loops are empty and `{drift: [], dispositions: []}` is returned — yet reconcile still commits and reindexes (src/tools/reconcile.mjs:8). Even in a project that does have bindings, the spec itself records that SessionStart's run (hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:99) already closed them, so the second run observes nothing (docs/specs/2026-08-02-preflight-briefing-redesign.md:345-349).
survivors.model_impact: A mandated step whose documented purpose ('fold drift') cannot occur under the documented tool set, costing a tool round-trip plus a git commit and a full index rebuild on every resume. The briefing's SINCE YOU LEFT block (src/render/briefing.mjs:54-69) is correspondingly dead in the documented flow, so the model is briefed as if nothing changed on any branch, whether or not that is true.
survivors.failure_scenario: Every preflight run: reconcile returns `{drift:[],dispositions:[],recovery_degraded:false}` and writes a `chore(ledger): reconcile` commit. The model reads it as confirmation that no drift exists, when in fact nothing was ever observable.

verdict.correction: Accurate claim: with zero bindings runReconcile does no work, and no skill can create a binding. But it does not cost a commit — index/ is gitignored, so a no-change reconcile produces no commit object — and the 'SINCE YOU LEFT block is dead' consequence is wrong, because the drift snapshot merges rather than overwrites.
verdict.reasoning: src/drift/reconcile.mjs:29-31 iterates `await driver.listBindings()`; :50-51 derives boundKeys and repos from that same list, so with zero bindings both loops are empty and :66 returns {drift: [], dispositions: []}. src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:13 is the only TOOL that writes a binding (the other writeBinding calls are internal: src/drift/reattach.mjs:94 and src/drift/reconcile.mjs:45, both reachable only from runReconcile itself), and bind_branch is in neither skill (skills/preflight/SKILL.md:4, skills/debrief/SKILL.md:4; grep over README.md and skills/ exits 1). WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG: (a) src/tools/reconcile.mjs:8 does call commitAndReindex, but src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:19 sets RECOVERY_GITIGNORE = 'index/\n' and src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:31 sets GITIGNORE = 'index/\n', and src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:284-287 returns `{committed:false, empty:true}` when `git diff --cached --quiet` exits 0 — a reconcile that changed nothing writes only index files and creates no commit. (b) The SINCE YOU LEFT block is not dead by this mechanism: src/drift/snapshot.mjs writeDriftSnapshot calls mergeDriftSnapshot(await readIndexFile('drift'), drift), which merges per thread and preserves prior entries, and takeDriftSnapshot only clears the briefed thread's slice — so preflight's second reconcile does not erase SessionStart's drift, contradicting the finding's implied consequence. The block is empty only because there are no bindings in the first place (src/render/briefing.mjs:54-69 returns null on an empty list).

survivors.title: Only the terminal-refusal in update_thread/amend_criteria enforces any of debrief's ordering; a run that dies after the session log and decisions leaves a committed session with a stale spine and no incompleteness marker
evidence: skills/debrief/SKILL.md:27 — "Refresh the spine — MANDATORY, and BEFORE any transition."
src/tools/update-thread.mjs:103-126 — the handler performs no ordering or precondition check beyond thread existence and terminality
src/tools/update-thread.mjs:109-111 and src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:106-108 — the only ordering the server enforces: a terminal thread is refused
src/model/fsm.mjs:11-17 — paused is non-terminal, so update_thread after a paused transition is fully legal
src/tools/append-session-event.mjs:10-12 — the session log is written and committed on its own, independently
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:66-77 — each decision is written and committed on its own
src/render/briefing.mjs:88-90 — the next briefing prints spine.next_step with no freshness marker
docs/specs/2026-08-02-preflight-briefing-redesign.md:152 — "A refusal costs no work because the debrief writes the session log before it refreshes the spine."
survivors.mechanism: Each debrief step commits independently (src/tools/append-session-event.mjs:10-12, src/tools/record-decision.mjs:66-77). The server enforces only one of the skill's six ordering claims — update_thread and amend_criteria refuse a terminal thread (src/tools/update-thread.mjs:109-111, src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:106-108) — and paused is not terminal (src/model/fsm.mjs:11-17), so the 'spine BEFORE transition' rule (skills/debrief/SKILL.md:27) is pure convention for the normal hand-off. A run that stops after steps 2-3 leaves a committed session log and committed decisions attached to a thread whose spine still holds the previous session's active_goal/next_step/last_session, and nothing anywhere records that the hand-off was partial.
survivors.model_impact: After a mid-debrief failure — a cap refusal, a paused->paused refusal, a context exhaustion — the ledger is in a state that reads as complete: the session log says what happened, the decisions exist, and the briefing confidently prints a next step from the session before. The next model is briefed with false forward-looking instruction and has no way to detect it.
survivors.failure_scenario: Step 5's update_thread is refused for a cap violation, the model retries once, runs out of context, and the session ends. Thread has a new session log dated today and a next_step from yesterday. Next preflight prints yesterday's next step under '## NEXT STEP'.

verdict.reasoning: Verified. Independent commits: src/tools/append-session-event.mjs:10-12 appends and calls driver.commit directly; src/tools/record-decision.mjs:66-77 writes the file, patches the spine and calls commitAndReindex — each step lands on its own. Enforcement: I read src/tools/update-thread.mjs:103-126 end to end; the only preconditions are thread existence (:106-108) and terminality (:109-111), with no ordering or 'session log first' check; src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:102-108 is identical in shape. src/model/fsm.mjs:9 TERMINAL_STATUSES is ['done','abandoned'], so paused is non-terminal and src/tools/update-thread.mjs:109 does not refuse an update after a paused transition — the skill's 'BEFORE any transition' at skills/debrief/SKILL.md:27 is therefore convention for the normal hand-off, enforced by nothing but test/unit/skills/debrief.test.mjs:45-50, which only checks the ORDER OF THE PROSE. Consequence confirmed at src/render/briefing.mjs:88-90: nextStepBlock returns ['## NEXT STEP', truncate(spine.next_step, ...)] unconditionally, with no timestamp or staleness marker anywhere in renderBriefing (:161-185). So a run that dies after steps 2-3 leaves committed session logs and decisions against a spine still holding the prior session's next_step, indistinguishable from a complete hand-off.

survivors.title: The always-loaded continuity-ledger rule describes a different system: different skill names, file layout, cap units, decision format, auto-transition, criteria immutability, staleness scan and supersession workflow
evidence: continuity-ledger.md:3 — "Write side: the `ledgerize` skill. Read side: the `lift-off` skill." vs skills/debrief/SKILL.md:2 (`name: debrief`) and skills/preflight/SKILL.md:2 (`name: preflight`)

continuity-ledger.md:8 — "`PROJECT.md` (stable core, cap 80 lines) ... `decisions/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` (append-only, cap 20 lines)" vs src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:212 (`decisions/<nnnn>-<slug>.md`) and src/model/caps.mjs:1-12 (all caps in characters, none in lines); no PROJECT.md exists anywhere in src/
continuity-ledger.md:12 — "Hand-off auto-transitions the worked thread `active -> paused`" vs src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:10-47 (an explicit call, refused from paused per src/model/fsm.mjs:13)

continuity-ledger.md:29 — DoD requires "non-empty `completion_criteria` (defined at thread CREATION, never retroactively)" vs src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:49-71 (insert adds criteria at any time) and skills/debrief/SKILL.md:24 (which instructs exactly that)

continuity-ledger.md:37-41 — "A SessionStart scan flags threads" for staleness vs hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:94-102 (self-heal, sync, reconcile, roster — no age computation) and hooks/lib/roster.mjs:27-34 (no timestamp field emitted)
continuity-ledger.md:45 — "honor an explicit `/lift-off <slug>`" vs skills/preflight/SKILL.md:18 (`/preflight <slug>`)

continuity-ledger.md:51 — "after acceptance only the Status line may change (`accepted` -> `superseded-by: <filename>`)" vs src/tools/registry.mjs:19-34 (no tool edits a decision; record_decision hardcodes `Status: accepted` at src/tools/record-decision.mjs:18)

continuity-ledger.md:65 — "over-cap content is demoted to the session log with a pointer retained" vs src/model/caps.mjs:119-124 (throws) and docs/specs/2026-08-02-preflight-briefing-redesign.md:151 ("No demotion, no soft-warn")
survivors.mechanism: continuity-ledger.md is loaded into every session (it is in the CLAUDE.md include chain) and describes a v1 markdown file ledger. Eight of its load-bearing statements are false for this server: skill names (line 3), storage layout and filename grammar (lines 7-8), cap units (line 8 vs src/model/caps.mjs), automatic hand-off transition (line 12), criteria-fixed-at-creation (line 29 vs src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:49-71), the SessionStart staleness scan (lines 37-41 vs hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:94-102), the resume command name (line 45), decision supersession (line 51 vs the absence of any edit tool), and cap-violation demotion (line 65 vs src/model/caps.mjs:119-124).
survivors.model_impact: The model arrives at every debrief carrying a coherent, confident, wrong mental model that the thin skills do not correct — because the thinness invariant forbids them from restating server semantics. Concretely: it expects the transition to happen automatically (so may skip step 6), expects a cap overflow to be demoted (so may believe a refused write landed), believes criteria cannot be amended (so may refuse to use amend_criteria as step 4 instructs), and believes it can supersede a decision by editing a file the server has no tool to edit.
survivors.failure_scenario: Model is told by continuity-ledger.md:29 that criteria are 'defined at thread CREATION, never retroactively', reaches debrief step 4 which instructs an `insert` of a detour criterion, and resolves the conflict in favour of the global rule (which outranks skills per the user's own precedence rules), silently dropping the unplanned work from the ledger.

verdict.reasoning: I opened the rule file and checked each of the eight against the code. (1) continuity-ledger.md:3 names 'ledgerize' and 'lift-off'; the actual skills are skills/debrief/SKILL.md:2 `name: debrief` and skills/preflight/SKILL.md:2 `name: preflight`. (2) continuity-ledger.md:7-8 gives `<repo>/.claude/ledger/`, PROJECT.md and `decisions/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`; the server writes `decisions/<nnnn>-<slug>.md` (src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:212) and `sessions/<threadId>/<iso>--<actor>.md` (:246-249) under the roots at src/util/active-thread.mjs:18-29, and grep finds no PROJECT.md anywhere in src/. (3) Cap units: continuity-ledger.md:8 states line caps; src/model/caps.mjs:1-12 are all character or item counts. (4) continuity-ledger.md:12 'Hand-off auto-transitions the worked thread active -> paused'; src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:10-47 is an explicit tool call and src/model/fsm.mjs:13 refuses paused->paused. (5) continuity-ledger.md:29 'defined at thread CREATION, never retroactively'; src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:49-71 inserts criteria at any time and skills/debrief/SKILL.md:24 instructs exactly that. (6) continuity-ledger.md:37-41 promises a SessionStart staleness scan; hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:94-102 does self-heal, sync, reconcile, roster and computes no age, and hooks/lib/roster.mjs:27-34 emits no timestamp. (7) continuity-ledger.md:45 '/lift-off <slug>' vs skills/preflight/SKILL.md:18 '/preflight <slug>'. (8) continuity-ledger.md:51 decision supersession by editing the Status line; src/tools/record-decision.mjs:18 hardcodes 'Status: accepted' and no tool in src/tools/registry.mjs:19-34 edits a decision. Plus continuity-ledger.md:65 demotion vs src/model/caps.mjs:119-124 throw. All eight verified. SEVERITY DOWNGRADE and scope note: the contradicting artifact is a user-global rules file outside the audited repo (/Users/satanshumishra/Documents/DevLabs/.windful-ocean/.claude/rules/common/continuity-ledger.md), so no change to logbook can remove it; it is environment drift against this plugin, not a plugin defect.

survivors.title: A test forbids the string 'active -> paused' in either SKILL.md, structurally guaranteeing that the model can never be told the precondition its step-6 call requires
evidence: test/unit/skills/skill-invariants.mjs:8-14 — FORBIDDEN_SUBSTRINGS includes 'ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS' and 'active -> paused'
test/unit/skills/debrief.test.mjs:74-78 and test/unit/skills/preflight.test.mjs:80-84 — both assert the skill text contains none of them
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:38 — "The server decides which moves are legal ... do not pre-judge those rules here; surface the server's refusal to the user."
test/unit/skills/preflight.test.mjs:44-49 — preflight is asserted to expose no write tool, so it cannot transition a thread to active
src/model/fsm.mjs:13 — `paused: ['active','done','abandoned']`

docs/specs/2026-08-02-preflight-briefing-redesign.md:478-479 — "The invariant tests cannot catch this class of drift — they assert that a tool name is MENTIONED ... never that the described call matches its schema."
survivors.mechanism: The thinness invariant is enforced by a substring blacklist that specifically includes 'active -> paused' (test/unit/skills/skill-invariants.mjs:12) and is asserted for both skills (test/unit/skills/debrief.test.mjs:74-78, test/unit/skills/preflight.test.mjs:80-84). Combined with the preflight no-write-tools assertion (test/unit/skills/preflight.test.mjs:44-49), the test suite simultaneously guarantees that (a) preflight cannot make a thread active and (b) debrief cannot be told that 'paused' requires the thread to be active first. Neither the skills nor the tests contain any assertion that the described call sequence is executable against the FSM.
survivors.model_impact: The instruction layer is prevented by construction from carrying the one fact that would make the documented round-trip work, and the test suite reads green while the flow is broken. Any future fix that adds the precondition to the prose fails a test; any fix that adds a write tool to preflight fails a different test. The model's only teacher is the refusal.
survivors.failure_scenario: A maintainer adds 'the thread must be active before it can be parked' to skills/debrief/SKILL.md; test/unit/skills/debrief.test.mjs:74-78 fails on the forbidden substring, and the correction is reverted.

verdict.reasoning: Verified. test/unit/skills/skill-invariants.mjs:8-14 FORBIDDEN_SUBSTRINGS is exactly ['ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS','additionalProperties','80 lines','active -> paused','schema_version'] — I read the array, the string 'active -> paused' is literally there. test/unit/skills/debrief.test.mjs:74-78 and test/unit/skills/preflight.test.mjs:80-84 both assert `!text.includes(forbidden)` over the whole SKILL.md including frontmatter. test/unit/skills/preflight.test.mjs:44-49 asserts preflight allows none of append_session_event/record_decision/update_thread/transition_thread under either spelling, and :40-42 asserts the allowed list is EXACTLY the four read tools — so preflight is test-locked out of arming a thread. src/model/fsm.mjs:13 `paused: ['active','done','abandoned']` is the precondition that cannot be stated. skills/debrief/SKILL.md:38 explicitly defers to the server ('do not pre-judge those rules here'). I confirmed neither test file contains any assertion that a described call is executable against the FSM or matches a tool schema — debrief.test.mjs only checks prose ordering (:45-62) and token presence (:64-72). The spec acknowledges the class at docs/specs/2026-08-02-preflight-briefing-redesign.md in section 10.1: 'The invariant tests cannot catch this class of drift — they assert that a tool name is MENTIONED ... never that the described call matches its schema.'

survivors.title: WHY and NEXT STEP are rendered unconditionally, so a never-debriefed thread produces a briefing of empty headings that the Stop hook forces the model to print verbatim
evidence: src/render/briefing.mjs:50-52 — whyBlock always returns ['## WHY', truncate(spine.active_goal, ...)]
src/render/briefing.mjs:88-90 — nextStepBlock always returns ['## NEXT STEP', truncate(spine.next_step, ...)]
src/render/briefing.mjs:83-86 — lastSessionBlock returns null when empty, for contrast
docs/specs/2026-08-02-preflight-briefing-redesign.md:186-187 — "Sections marked CONDITIONAL are omitted entirely — never rendered as an empty heading — when their source is empty."
skills/preflight/SKILL.md:24 — print the briefing VERBATIM, adding nothing before or after
hooks/lib/stop.mjs:83-93 — the verbatim gate blocks the turn until that exact string is echoed
survivors.mechanism:
Verified by calling renderBriefing on a thread with an empty spine: the output is `# PREFLIGHT BRIEFING — T
paused · 0 of 1 done ...

## WHY


## PROGRESS
- [>] c1 — first

## NEXT STEP


## NOT SHOWN...`. WHY and NEXT STEP render as headings with an empty body (src/render/briefing.mjs:50-52, 88-90), unlike LAST SESSION which is omitted when empty (src/render/briefing.mjs:85). The skill forbids the model from adding any explanatory text (skills/preflight/SKILL.md:24), and the Stop hook enforces that verbatim print (hooks/lib/stop.mjs:83-93).
survivors.model_impact: The model is compelled to present a briefing that looks authoritative and says nothing, with no permitted way to tell the user that the spine was never written. It also cannot distinguish 'the previous session recorded no next step' from 'the previous session's debrief failed' — the two states render identically.
survivors.failure_scenario: Session 1 opens a thread and its debrief dies at step 5. Session 2's preflight prints '## WHY' and '## NEXT STEP' with blank bodies. The user reads a formatted briefing and concludes there is genuinely nothing pending.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced it rather than reasoning about it. Calling renderBriefing on newThread({title:'T', completion_criteria:[{text:'first'}]}) with status paused yields verbatim: '# PREFLIGHT BRIEFING — T
paused · 0 of 1 done · 0 detour(s) open · last worked 2026-08-04

## WHY


## PROGRESS
- [>] c1 — first

## NEXT STEP


## NOT SHOWN
0 risk(s) and 0 decision(s) from other steps; 0 legacy decision(s).
Ask for any decision by number: read_decision.' src/model/thread.mjs:37-46 emptySpine sets active_goal/next_step/last_session to ''. src/render/briefing.mjs:50-52 whyBlock and :88-90 nextStepBlock both return a two-element array unconditionally, while :83-86 lastSessionBlock returns null when empty and :129-135, :103-117, :119-127 all return null when empty — so WHY and NEXT STEP are the two that violate the spec's own rule at docs/specs/2026-08-02-preflight-briefing-redesign.md section 6 ('Sections marked CONDITIONAL are omitted entirely — never rendered as an empty heading — when their source is empty'). skills/preflight/SKILL.md:24 forbids adding anything before or after, and hooks/lib/stop.mjs:83-93 enforces the exact-substring echo. The two states the finding names ('no next step recorded' vs 'debrief failed') do render identically.

survivors.title: The largest, most deeply nested and most heavily validated call of the whole protocol is scheduled last, behind fourteen distinct refusal sites, at the point of maximum context pressure
evidence: skills/debrief/SKILL.md:27-32 — step 5 (update_thread) is the fifth of eight steps and asks for six spine fields plus replace_scopes plus criterion toggles in one call
src/tools/update-thread.mjs:131-152 — the input schema nests four levels deep: args -> spine -> open_risks[] -> refs[]

src/model/caps.mjs:1-12 — the maximum legal single payload is roughly 200 + 500 + 300 chars of scalars, 20 risks per scope at 300 chars each plus 8 refs of 200 chars each (1,900 chars per risk), and 20 out_of_scope entries at 300 chars: about 45,000 characters for one visible scope, ~83,000 across two
hooks/lib/post-tool-use.mjs:4-8,49-50 — the nudge to run debrief fires at 70% of a 1.2 MB transcript budget, i.e. deliberately near context exhaustion

refusal sites reachable from one update_thread call: src/tools/registry.mjs:63; src/tools/update-thread.mjs:107, :110, :84, :87, :31; src/tools/spine-input.mjs:14, :29, :44, :48, :61, :77, :107; src/model/caps.mjs:120; plus src/schema/validators.mjs:32 at write
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:19,21,23,34,40 — four further tool calls surround it, each with its own required-field set
survivors.mechanism: A complete debrief is five or more tool calls (skills/debrief/SKILL.md:19,21,23,27,34,40). The fourth of them, update_thread, is the deepest (four levels of nesting, src/tools/update-thread.mjs:137-151) and the most heavily gated: fourteen distinct throw sites are reachable from a single call (enumerated in the evidence), each with its own error vocabulary and none of which the skill documents except the risk sentence shape and the out_of_scope dedup rule. The PostToolUse nudge that prompts a debrief is triggered by transcript size crossing 70% of budget (hooks/lib/post-tool-use.mjs:10-20,49-50), so the protocol's peak-complexity call is scheduled precisely when the model has least room to reason about it, least access to the criterion ids and decision refs it must cite, and — per the thread_id finding — possibly no thread_id at all.
survivors.model_impact: Every degradation mode compounds at once: truncated risk prose hits the em-dash regex, dropped fields hit ajv, over-long next_step hits the cap, a stale criterion id hits the unknown-id refusal, and each refusal discards the entire call and costs a full re-emission of a payload that can legitimately run to tens of thousands of characters. Retrying an 83,000-character call under context pressure is not viable, so the realistic outcome is a partial or abandoned debrief.
survivors.failure_scenario: At 75% context the model composes update_thread with five risks, three refs each, four criterion toggles and replace_scopes. One risk uses a hyphen instead of the spaced em dash. The whole call is refused at src/tools/spine-input.mjs:61; the model must re-emit every field to retry.

verdict.reasoning: The component facts check out; I verified each rather than the aggregate framing. Nesting: src/tools/update-thread.mjs:137-151 is args -> spine -> open_risks[] -> refs[], four levels, the deepest schema in src/tools/. Refusal sites reachable from one call, each opened: src/tools/registry.mjs:63 (ajv), src/tools/update-thread.mjs:107, :110, :84, :87, :31; src/tools/spine-input.mjs:14, :29, :42-45, :47-50, :60-63, :76-79, :106-109; src/model/caps.mjs:119-124; and src/schema/validators.mjs:32 at write via src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:147 — that is 15, so 'fourteen' is if anything conservative. Payload size: src/model/caps.mjs:1-12 permits 20 risks per scope at 300 chars plus 8 refs of 200 chars (1,900 chars each = 38,000), 20 out_of_scope at 300 (6,000) and ~1,000 of scalars — ~45,000 chars per visible scope, and src/model/selection.mjs:39-42 makes two scopes visible, so ~83,000 across both. Nudge timing: hooks/lib/post-tool-use.mjs:4-5 DEFAULT_FRACTION 0.7 and DEFAULT_BUDGET 1,200,000, computed at :10-20 and compared at :48-50. Step count: skills/debrief/SKILL.md:19,21,23,27,34,40 is six tool-call steps with update_thread fourth. DOWNGRADE to low: every constituent fact is verified, but the finding is a design critique built from facts already reported individually (caps-unstated, thread_id, criterion ids); as a discrete defect it adds no new failing behavior, and its 'realistic outcome is a partial or abandoned debrief' conclusion is a prediction about model behavior the code cannot settle.

survivors.title: debrief step 5 must toggle criteria by id, but the id of a criterion step 4 inserted is assigned server-side, does not match its position, and the skill never says to read it from the amend response
evidence: src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:60-66 — the inserted entry's id is `nextCriterionId(criteria)` and done is hardcoded false
src/model/criteria.mjs:3-11 — nextCriterionId returns `c<highest+1>`, independent of insert position
src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:35-47 — a detour with no `before` is inserted immediately ahead of the current criterion, so array position and id number disagree
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:24 — instructs inserting a detour for "unplanned work that you closed"

skills/debrief/SKILL.md:27 — instructs flipping satisfied criteria done by "match a criterion by its id and supply its done flag"; the skill never says the id comes from amend_criteria's returned thread
src/tools/update-thread.mjs:83-85 — an unrecognised id is refused: 'unknown completion_criteria id'
src/model/dod.mjs:8 — every un-struck criterion, detours included, must be done:true before a thread can close
survivors.mechanism: An inserted detour receives id `c<highest+1>` (src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:61, src/model/criteria.mjs:3-11) while being placed ahead of the current criterion (src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:44-46), so a detour inserted between c2 and c3 in a five-criterion thread is named c6. It is created with done:false (src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:63). Step 5 must then toggle it by that id (skills/debrief/SKILL.md:27), which is available only in step 4's returned thread — something the skill never states. Guessing wrong hits src/tools/update-thread.mjs:84.
survivors.model_impact: The model either guesses an id (refused), skips the toggle (leaving a permanently open detour that blocks the DoD gate at src/model/dod.mjs:8 and inflates the 'detour(s) open' count in the briefing header at src/render/briefing.mjs:46), or must have retained the full amend_criteria response — at the point in the session where retention is worst.
survivors.failure_scenario: Five-criterion thread, detour inserted for work already finished. Model assumes the new id follows its position and sends `{id:'c3', done:true}`, silently marking a genuine planned criterion complete instead — a wrong toggle the server accepts, since c3 exists.

verdict.reasoning: Verified. src/model/criteria.mjs:3-11 nextCriterionId scans every existing id for the highest c<N> and returns `c${highest + 1}` — it never consults position. src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:59-66 uses that id while `at` comes from insertPosition (:35-47), which for a detour with no `before` returns the index of currentCriterion (:44-46), so a detour placed between c2 and c3 in a five-criterion thread is genuinely named c6; done is hardcoded false at :63. The id reaches the model only in the response: src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:117 returns `{ thread: updated, recovery_degraded }`, and skills/debrief/SKILL.md:24-27 never says to read the id back from that thread. hooks/lib/roster.mjs:2,18-21 — NEXT_STEP_MAX_CHARS = 120, truncated with '...'
src/render/briefing.mjs:88-90 — the full 500 chars are shown only inside the briefing, which requires a thread_id the model gets from that same truncated roster line
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:27 — "`active_goal` and `next_step`: where the work is going, and the single next action", with no length guidance
survivors.mechanism: A model writing a thorough next_step within the 500-character cap (src/model/caps.mjs:3) sees 76% of it discarded in the roster line the next session actually reads first (hooks/lib/roster.mjs:2,18-21). The full text appears only in the briefing (src/render/briefing.mjs:88-90), which is reached after the roster has already been used to choose a thread.
survivors.model_impact: Token spent on the roster's most decision-relevant field is wasted, and the roster — the surface used to pick which thread to resume — can present a next step truncated mid-clause, inverting its meaning.
survivors.failure_scenario: next_step = 'Do not merge the branch until the migration lands; the API route is written but ...' truncates at 120 chars to a line that reads as an instruction to merge.

verdict.reasoning: Verified both numbers directly. src/model/caps.mjs:3 `nextStepMaxChars: 500`, enforced at src/model/caps.mjs:14-18 SCALAR_CAPS via scalarViolations (:33-39). hooks/lib/roster.mjs:2 `NEXT_STEP_MAX_CHARS = 120`, applied at :18-21 through truncate (:5-8) which appends '...' — so a 500-char next_step is cut to 117 chars plus an ellipsis in the roster line. The full text is only in src/render/briefing.mjs:88-90, which truncates at SPINE_CAPS.nextStepMaxChars (500) — i.e. not at all — but is reachable only after a thread_id has been chosen from the truncated line. skills/debrief/SKILL.md:28 gives no length guidance.
