survivors.title: Automatic ledger sync merges the remote ledger with -X theirs and then force-pushes, so a teammate's ledger silently overwrites the local user's conflicting thread state with no report to the model or the user
evidence: src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:488-491 — `scopedExec(worktree, ['merge', '--no-verify', '--no-edit', '-X', 'theirs', '-m', MERGE_MESSAGE, this.mirrorRef], ...)`
src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:439 — `if (await this.#pushLease(remote, mergeSha, remoteSha))` — the -X theirs merge result is immediately pushed back
src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:437-441 — the diverged branch of sync() runs unconditionally, gated only by #assertSharedRoot
hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:98 — `await ctx.invokeCli(['sync']);` with the return value discarded
hooks/lib/stop.mjs:106 — `await ctx.invokeCli(['sync']);` with the return value discarded
bin/ledger-cli.mjs:65-68 — `runSync` just returns `ctx.driver.sync()`; the `{ merged: true }` flag never reaches the model
src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:28 — `const GITATTRIBUTES = 'sessions/**/*.md merge=union\n';` union merge covers only session logs, not threads/*.json
survivors.mechanism: sync() detects divergence between the local ledger ref and the fetched mirror and resolves it with `git merge -X theirs` (src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:490). `-X theirs` resolves every conflicting hunk in favour of the incoming remote side. threads/*.json are single-line-per-field JSON documents not covered by the union merge driver (only sessions/**/*.md is, line 28), so any concurrent edit to the same thread record resolves entirely to the remote copy. The merged sha is then pushed with --force-with-lease (line 439), making the loss authoritative for everyone. sync() runs automatically at SessionStart (hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:98) and at Stop (hooks/lib/stop.mjs:106) and both call sites throw the result away, so nothing surfaces `{ merged: true }` to the model or the user.
survivors.model_impact: The model completes a debrief, writes the spine, sees success, and the session ends. The Stop hook then syncs and the entire spine refresh is silently replaced by a teammate's version. The next session's briefing is confidently wrong and the model has no way to know a merge discarded its writes — it will re-derive state from a record that no longer reflects what it wrote.
survivors.failure_scenario: Two contributors touch the same thread in overlapping sessions -> B pushes first -> A's Stop hook syncs, merges with -X theirs, and A's just-written next_step/criteria toggles vanish -> A's next preflight briefing states a next step A never recorded.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived. src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:486-497 (`#mergeTheirs`) runs `merge --no-verify --no-edit -X theirs <mirrorRef>`; sync's diverged branch (lines 437-441) calls it and immediately pushes the merge sha with `--force-with-lease` (`#pushLease`, lines 463-472). The union merge driver is scoped to session logs only: `const GITATTRIBUTES = 'sessions/**/*.md merge=union\n'` (line 28), so threads/*.json is a plain text merge; records are pretty-printed one field per line (src/drivers/layout.mjs:2). I verified the git semantics directly: two branches editing the same JSON field, merged with `-X theirs`, exits 0, prints no conflict, and the local value is gone. Silence confirmed: `sync()` is reachable only through `bin/ledger-cli.mjs:65-68`, invoked at hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:98 and hooks/lib/stop.mjs:106 with the return value discarded, and `hooks/lib/cli.mjs:11-27` never even throws on failure; no MCP tool in src/tools/registry.mjs:19-34 exposes sync, so `{merged:true}` can reach neither model nor user. One narrowing: `-X theirs` resolves per conflicting hunk, not the whole record as the mechanism paragraph says — non-conflicting fields from both sides survive. That narrowing does not rescue the spine, whose scalar fields are adjacent lines and fall in one conflict region when both sides run a debrief.

survivors.title: readThread only upcasts and listThreads does not even do that, so every write-side cap and pattern is void for a ledger record authored elsewhere and pulled in via git
evidence: src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:143-145 — `async readThread(id) { return upcastThread(await readJsonOrNull(join(this.ledgerRoot, 'threads', `${id}.json`))); }` — no assertValidThread
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:155-164 — `listThreads()` calls `readJsonOrNull` directly with neither upcast nor validation
src/schema/upcast.mjs:82 — `if (record.schema_version !== LEGACY_SCHEMA_VERSION) return record;` — a v2 record is returned untouched
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:148 — `assertValidThread(thread)` exists only on the write path
src/tools/get-resume-brief.mjs:15 — the briefing is rendered from `await driver.readThread(args.thread_id)`, the unvalidated value
src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:59-60 — even the write schema caps nothing: `slug: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }`, `title: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }`
src/tools/open-thread.mjs:32-33 — the tool schema is equally open: `title: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }`, `slug: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }`
src/model/thread.mjs:53-56 — an explicitly supplied slug is stored raw (`? rawSlug`), never matched against SLUG_PATTERN
survivors.mechanism: All four validation layers named in the incident report sit on the write path. The read path (src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:143-145, 155-164) applies none of them: readThread upcasts v1 records and returns v2 records byte-for-byte, listThreads does not even upcast. renderBriefing accepts whatever comes back (src/render/briefing.mjs:161-169 only checks that thread and thread.spine are objects). Consequently every cap enforced by src/model/caps.mjs and the ajv tool schemas applies only to records this process wrote; a record written by a teammate, by a hand edit, or by an older plugin version reaches the renderer unchecked. Independently, thread.title and thread.slug have no maxLength at any layer (src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:59-60, src/tools/open-thread.mjs:32-33) and title has no render-side truncation (src/render/briefing.mjs:45), so title is unbounded even on the fully-validated write path.
survivors.model_impact: The model is told (tool descriptions, skill text) that the server enforces every rule and refuses anything illegal. For any ledger it did not itself author, that is false: caps, patterns and scope rules are all bypassed, and an unbounded title alone can blow the briefing to arbitrary size and cost. It also makes the injection findings above unfixable at the write layer.
survivors.failure_scenario: Pull a ledger whose threads/<id>.json has a 200 KB title and a spine with 500 out_of_scope entries -> get_resume_brief renders and returns all of it -> the model's context is consumed by data no validator ever saw.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived. src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:143-145 — `readThread` returns `upcastThread(await readJsonOrNull(...))` with no `assertValidThread`; src/schema/upcast.mjs:77-82 returns any record whose `schema_version !== 1` completely untouched. src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:155-164 — `listThreads` calls `readJsonOrNull` directly, neither upcasting nor validating. Validation exists only on the write path (src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:147-148, 170-171). src/render/briefing.mjs:161-169 type-checks only `brief` and `brief.thread`; every field-level guard downstream is a defensive `Array.isArray`/`typeof`, not a cap. src/tools/get-resume-brief.mjs:15,19 render from exactly those unvalidated values. The independent secondary claim also holds: no maxLength on title or slug at any layer (src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:59-60; src/tools/open-thread.mjs:32-33) and no render-side truncation of title (src/render/briefing.mjs:45); an explicitly supplied slug is stored raw at src/model/thread.mjs:53-56 and never tested against SLUG_PATTERN, which src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:15 uses only for decision filenames (line 206). Worth adding: because title/slug are unvalidated on the WRITE path too, the injection findings above do not even depend on a foreign ledger — my probe injected through an ordinary open_thread call.

survivors.title: readJsonOrNull calls JSON.parse outside its try block, so one malformed file anywhere in the ledger makes every reindexing tool throw a SyntaxError that names no file
evidence: src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:55-64 — the try/catch wraps only `readFile` and re-throws anything that is not ENOENT; `return JSON.parse(raw);` on line 63 is outside the try
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:160 — `const record = await readJsonOrNull(join(this.ledgerRoot, 'threads', name));` inside listThreads' loop, uncaught
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:183 — same pattern in listBindings
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:253 — same pattern in readIndexFile
src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:27-28 — `await driver.listThreads()` / `listBindings()` with no error handling
src/tools/shared.mjs:19-23 — `commitAndReindex` calls rebuildIndex first, so every mutating tool goes through listThreads
bin/ledger-server.mjs:55-59 — the failure is returned to the model as `{ error: error.name, message: error.message }`, i.e. `{"error":"SyntaxError", ...}` with no path
survivors.mechanism: JSON.parse sits outside readJsonOrNull's try (src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:63), so a truncated or conflict-marked file raises SyntaxError. listThreads (line 160) and listBindings (line 183) iterate the directory with no per-file guard, and rebuildIndex calls both with no guard (src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:27-28). commitAndReindex runs rebuildIndex before the commit (src/tools/shared.mjs:20), so open_thread, bind_branch, record_decision, update_thread, amend_criteria, archive_thread, create_successor, reopen, reconcile and rebuild_index all fail. get_resume_brief calls listThreads directly (src/tools/get-resume-brief.mjs:19). The server surfaces only error.name and error.message (bin/ledger-server.mjs:57), so the model receives `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ... in JSON at position N` with no indication of which of N files is bad or that the problem is a file at all.
survivors.model_impact: Guaranteed unrecoverable retry loop. Thirteen of fourteen tools fail identically with an error that looks like a bug in the server, not a data problem. The model cannot locate the offending file through any tool the server exposes and will burn turns retrying different tools, each producing the same opaque SyntaxError.
survivors.failure_scenario: A merge or an interrupted write leaves threads/01XXXX.json truncated -> every subsequent ledger tool call returns `{"error":"SyntaxError","message":"Unexpected end of JSON input"}` -> the model has no path to diagnosis.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and empirically reproduced. src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:55-64 — the try/catch wraps only `readFile` and re-throws non-ENOENT; `return JSON.parse(raw);` on line 63 sits outside it. listThreads (line 160), listBindings (line 183) and readIndexFile (line 253) call it with no per-file guard; src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:27-28 calls both unguarded; src/tools/shared.mjs:19-23 runs rebuildIndex before the commit. I dropped a file `threads/garbage.json` containing `{ not json` into a live git-backed ledger: `rebuild_index` and `get_resume_brief` both failed with `SyntaxError | Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 2` — no filename, no path, no hint that the cause is data. bin/ledger-server.mjs:55-59 returns exactly `{ error: error.name, message: error.message }` to the model. One correction to the impact line: it is 12 of 14 tools, not 13 — the ten commitAndReindex callers (amend-criteria:116, archive-thread:29, open-thread:20, bind-branch:15, create-successor:23, record-decision:77, reopen:31, reconcile:8, transition-thread:46, update-thread:124) plus rebuild_index plus get_resume_brief; `append_session_event` (src/tools/append-session-event.mjs:10-11, commit only) and `read_decision` survive.

survivors.title: bind_branch accepts any string as `repo` and reconcile uses it directly as a git process cwd with no per-binding error handling, so one stale or foreign path aborts the whole reconcile with the misleading message "spawn git ENOENT"
evidence: src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:28 — `repo: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` — no absolute-path, existence or project-scope check
src/model/binding.mjs:20 — `repo: fields.repo` stored verbatim; src/schema/binding.schema.mjs:22 repeats `minLength: 1`
src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:504-506 — `const base = await resolveIntegrationBase(repo); const scope = hostScope(repo); const headSha = await revParseOrNull(scope, ...)`
src/util/git-scope.mjs:35-43 — `hostScope(dir)` only asserts non-empty; the dir becomes scope.dir
src/util/git-exec.mjs:18 — `{ cwd: repoDir, env: mergedEnv, ... }` — the caller value is the process cwd
src/util/git-exec.mjs:20-22 — `if (error && typeof error.code !== 'number') { reject(error); return; }` — this fires before the `check: false` branch, so check:false does not suppress a spawn failure
src/drift/reconcile.mjs:35 — `const observation = await driver.observeBranch(binding);` inside the loop, no try/catch
src/drift/reconcile.mjs:54 — `const branches = await driver.listRepoBranches(repo);` likewise unguarded
src/tools/reconcile.mjs:6 — `const { drift, dispositions } = await runReconcile(ctx);` — no error handling in the tool either
skills/preflight/SKILL.md:22 — "Call `mcp__ledger__reconcile` ... before you brief on anything."
survivors.mechanism: binding.repo is an unvalidated free-form string that becomes the cwd of a spawned git process (src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:28 -> src/model/binding.mjs:20 -> src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:505 -> src/util/git-scope.mjs:35 -> src/util/git-exec.mjs:18). Bindings are stored in the ledger and therefore shared, but repo holds a machine-local absolute path, so on any other machine it usually does not exist. I ran gitExec against a nonexistent directory with `check: false` and confirmed it rejects with name=Error, code='ENOENT', message='spawn git ENOENT' — the `check: false` escape hatch at src/util/git-exec.mjs:26 is never reached because the spawn-failure branch at lines 20-22 returns first. runReconcile has no per-binding guard (src/drift/reconcile.mjs:35,54), so the first unreachable repo aborts the entire reconcile, which the preflight skill requires before briefing (skills/preflight/SKILL.md:22).
survivors.model_impact: The model calls reconcile as instructed and receives `{"error":"Error","message":"spawn git ENOENT"}`. That message states that the git binary is missing — a false diagnosis the model will act on (checking PATH, telling the user to install git) while the real cause is one binding row pointing at a directory that does not exist on this machine. Nothing in the error names the binding, the repo path, or reconcile's loop position. Secondarily, an injected instruction can call bind_branch with any path on the machine and reconcile will then run git enumeration inside that unrelated repository and write its branch/trailer data into the shared ledger.
survivors.failure_scenario: Alice binds a thread to repo=/Users/alice/work/app and pushes the ledger; Bob pulls and runs preflight -> reconcile -> observeBranch spawns git with cwd=/Users/alice/work/app -> reject 'spawn git ENOENT' -> reconcile fails for Bob permanently, and the model reports that git is not installed.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and empirically reproduced end to end. `repo` is accepted as any non-empty string (src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:28), stored verbatim (src/model/binding.mjs:20; schema repeats minLength 1 at src/schema/binding.schema.mjs:22), and becomes a spawn cwd: src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:504-506 -> src/util/git-scope.mjs:35-43 (hostScope only asserts non-empty) -> src/util/git-scope.mjs:98 -> src/util/git-exec.mjs:14-18 (`cwd: repoDir`). I confirmed Node's behaviour directly: execFile with a nonexistent cwd yields `code: 'ENOENT'` as a STRING, so src/util/git-exec.mjs:20-22 rejects before the `check: false` branch at line 26 can suppress it. src/drift/reconcile.mjs:31-48 and 53-54 have no per-binding try/catch and src/tools/reconcile.mjs:6 adds none. Live test: bind_branch with repo '/no/such/dir/anywhere', then reconcile -> `{ name: 'Error', message: 'spawn git ENOENT' }`, naming neither the binding, nor the path, nor the loop position. skills/preflight/SKILL.md:22 does require reconcile before briefing. One observed nuance: get_resume_brief survived the same bad binding in my probe (its drift snapshot path reads a cached index file, src/drift/snapshot.mjs takeDriftSnapshot, not observeBranch), so the blast radius is reconcile, not the brief.

survivors.title: nextDecisionNumber pads to four digits but never bounds the value, so a single decisions/ filename with a five-or-more-digit prefix permanently breaks record_decision after the decision file has already been written
evidence: src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:16 — `const DECISION_FILE = /^([0-9]+)-(.+)\.md$/;` — any number of leading digits matches
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:189-200 — nextDecisionNumber takes `Number(match[1])`, keeps the max and returns `String(max + 1).padStart(4, '0')` with no upper bound
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:203-205 — writeDecision only checks `/^[0-9]+$/.test(nnnn)`, which a value like "1e+21" fails
src/schema/patterns.mjs:8 — `DECISION_REF_PATTERN = '^[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9-]+$'` requires exactly four digits
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:66 — `const path = await driver.writeDecision(nnnn, args.slug, markdown);`
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:67-70 — `const ref = `${nnnn}-${args.slug}`` is appended to spine.key_decisions
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:76 — `await driver.writeThread(updated);` runs after the file is already on disk, and writeThread validates via src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:148
survivors.mechanism: A decisions/ entry named e.g. `12345-anything.md` matches DECISION_FILE (src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:16), so max becomes 12345 and nextDecisionNumber returns "12346" (padStart only pads, never truncates — line 199). record_decision writes the file first (src/tools/record-decision.mjs:66), then builds `ref = "12346-<slug>"` and calls writeThread (line 76), where assertValidThread rejects it because DECISION_REF_PATTERN demands exactly four digits (src/schema/patterns.mjs:8). I verified the regex rejects `12346-a`. The tool throws, but the markdown file has already been written and, under GitRefDriver, staged into the worktree — the next commit picks up an orphaned decision record the thread does not reference. At the extreme, a prefix of 1e21 or greater makes String(max+1) produce "1e+21", which I verified fails writeDecision's own `/^[0-9]+$/` check, so the failure moves one step earlier but is equally permanent.
survivors.model_impact: record_decision fails on every call with a schema error about a decision ref, while silently accumulating one orphaned decision file per attempt. The debrief skill (skills/debrief/SKILL.md:21) instructs the model to retry decision capture, so the model retries, littering the ledger further. amend_criteria's rewrite/strike operations then also fail, because they require a decision_ref that resolves (src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:7-12), so the whole plan-amendment path is dead too.
survivors.failure_scenario: Someone commits decisions/12345-legacy-import.md to the shared ledger -> next record_decision writes decisions/12346-<slug>.md then throws `Thread failed schema validation: /spine/key_decisions/N/ref must match pattern` -> retried, it writes 12347, 12348 ... each time failing identically.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and empirically reproduced. src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:16 — `DECISION_FILE = /^([0-9]+)-(.+)\.md$/` matches any digit count; lines 189-200 take Number(match[1]), keep the max, and return `String(max + 1).padStart(4, '0')` with no ceiling — padStart pads, never truncates. src/schema/patterns.mjs:8 demands exactly four digits. src/tools/record-decision.mjs:66 writes the markdown file BEFORE line 67 builds the ref and line 76 calls writeThread, which validates via src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:147-148. Live test: I dropped `decisions/12345-foreign.md` into a git-backed ledger, then called record_decision — nextDecisionNumber returned '12346', the call failed with `SchemaValidationError | Thread failed schema validation: /spine/key_decisions/0/ref must match pattern "^[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9-]+$"`, and `decisions/` afterwards contained BOTH `12345-foreign.md` and the newly orphaned `12346-my-choice.md`. Retrying litters one more file each time; skills/debrief/SKILL.md:21 and 25 do drive retries, and amend_criteria's rewrite/strike require a resolvable decision_ref (src/tools/schemas.mjs:90-106). Two calibration notes: the error name is SchemaValidationError (not the bare Error implied), and the defect needs the precondition of a foreign/hand-authored 5+-digit filename, which the same missing read-side validation (finding 4) makes reachable through any pulled ledger.

survivors.title: Every driver init recursively deletes the ledger worktree before re-adding it, and hook-spawned CLI processes do this concurrently with the long-lived MCP server whose writes are not covered by the worktree lock
evidence: src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:354-359 — `#provisionWorktree()` runs `await rm(this.worktreeDir, { recursive: true, force: true });` then `worktree prune` and `worktree add --detach`
src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:309-319 — `init()` calls `#ensureWorktree()` unconditionally on every construction
src/tools/context.mjs:10 — `await driver.init();` inside buildContext
bin/ledger-cli.mjs:23,53,61,66,75 — runRoster, runBriefingPledge, runReconcile, runSync and runRecordSha each call `buildContext({})`
hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:98-100 — SessionStart invokes the CLI three times (`sync`, `reconcile`, `roster`)
hooks/lib/stop.mjs:61,101,106 — Stop invokes `briefing-pledge`, `active-thread` and `sync`
hooks/lib/post-tool-use.mjs:45 — `await ctx.invokeCli(['record-sha', sha]);` after any git-commit-ish Bash command
src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:343-352 — `#ensureWorktree` takes the lock only around `#provisionWorktree`
src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:282-287 — `#writeInWorktree` guards with a per-instance `#uncommittedWrite` flag, which another process cannot see
survivors.mechanism: buildContext always calls driver.init() (src/tools/context.mjs:10), and for the git backend init always reaches #provisionWorktree, whose first action is `rm(this.worktreeDir, { recursive: true, force: true })` (src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:356). Every hook-spawned CLI command builds a fresh context (bin/ledger-cli.mjs:23,53,61,66,75), so the worktree is destroyed and re-created on SessionStart (three times), on Stop (three times), on every resume-intent prompt, and after every Bash command matching /git (commit|merge|rebase|...)/ (hooks/lib/post-tool-use.mjs:42-46). Meanwhile the MCP server holds one long-lived driver for the same directory (bin/ledger-server.mjs:34-45 caches the context). The worktree lock (src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:344-351) serialises provisioning against provisioning only; the server's writeThread/writeDecision/appendSessionEvent calls (lines 289-307) take no lock, and the #uncommittedWrite guard on line 283 is process-local.
survivors.model_impact: An uncommitted ledger write issued by the MCP server can be deleted mid-flight by a hook-spawned CLI, or fail with ENOENT after the model was told the write succeeded. The model then reports a successful debrief for data that no longer exists, and the next session's briefing silently omits it. This is a race, so it is intermittent and effectively undebuggable from the model's side.
survivors.failure_scenario: Model calls update_thread (writes threads/<id>.json into the worktree, commit pending) while the user runs a Bash `git commit` in another pane -> PostToolUse invokes `ledger-cli record-sha` -> buildContext -> init -> rm -rf of the worktree -> the pending write is gone or the subsequent commit stages nothing.

verdict.reasoning: Mechanism re-derived, and its deterministic consequence proved (the finder's stated consequence is the weaker, speculative half). src/tools/context.mjs:10 calls `driver.init()` on every context build; src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:309-319 always reaches `#ensureWorktree`; lines 354-359 begin with `await rm(this.worktreeDir, { recursive: true, force: true })`. Every CLI entry builds a context (bin/ledger-cli.mjs:23, 29, 53, 61, 66, 75), and the hooks invoke the CLI three times at SessionStart (hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:98-100), twice at Stop (hooks/lib/stop.mjs:61 via readPledge, 101, 106) and after any git-commit-ish Bash (hooks/lib/post-tool-use.mjs:42-45 with COMMITISH at line 6). The lock covers provisioning only (src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:343-352) while writeThread/writeDecision/appendSessionEvent/writeIndexFile take none (lines 289-307), and `#uncommittedWrite` (line 206, 282-287) is per-instance. The worktree path is shared across every process for a project (src/drivers/select.mjs:38-42, keyed only by projectKey), so cross-session concurrency is real. What I could NOT prove is the mid-flight race on a committed record — MCP handlers write and commit inside one call, and committed data lives in the ref so `worktree add` restores it. What I DID prove is that the uncommitted, gitignored `index/` tree is destroyed deterministically on every CLI call (see missed finding #1): index dir before a CLI call = [briefing, by-branch, by-slug, children, resumable]; after = [].

survivors.title: Ledger commits are made with --no-verify and pushed to origin automatically at session start and session end, so free-form model-authored text bypasses any repo secret-scanning hook and reaches the shared remote with no user gate
evidence: src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:390 — `await scopedExec(worktree, ['commit', '--no-verify', '-m', message], { env: ledgerCommitEnv() });`
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:291-295 — the recovery repo commits with `args(['commit', '--no-verify', '-m', message])` too
src/util/git-scope.mjs:77 — networkScope/isolatedScope set `core.hooksPath` to `join(gitDir, 'hooks-disabled')`, a second, independent hook bypass
src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:452-461 — `#pushCreate` runs `['push', this.remote, `${localSha}:${this.ledgerRef}`]`
hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:98 — `await ctx.invokeCli(['sync']);` runs at every session start
hooks/lib/stop.mjs:106 — `await ctx.invokeCli(['sync']);` runs at every session end
src/tools/append-session-event.mjs:25-26 — `actor: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }`, `body: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` — no maxLength, no content restriction
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:19 — instructs the model to record "what shipped AND what failed and why" in the body
skills/debrief/SKILL.md:17 — instructs that background work "belongs in the session-log body with its shell id and kill command"
src/tools/record-decision.mjs:96,99 — `context` and `outcome` are bare `{ type: 'string' }`, rendered straight into the committed markdown at src/tools/record-decision.mjs:29,37
survivors.mechanism: The debrief skill directs the model to paste failure narratives, commands and shell state into append_session_event bodies and record_decision context/outcome (skills/debrief/SKILL.md:17,19). Those strings are written to disk verbatim (src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:246-249; src/tools/record-decision.mjs:29,37,66) and committed with `--no-verify` (src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:390), which skips pre-commit and commit-msg hooks — the standard mounting point for gitleaks/detect-secrets in a team repo. scopedExec additionally points core.hooksPath at a nonexistent directory (src/util/git-scope.mjs:77), so even a global hooks path is neutralised. sync() then pushes to origin (src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:455) and is invoked automatically at SessionStart and Stop (hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:98, hooks/lib/stop.mjs:106) with no user confirmation and no output surfaced. There is no size cap and no redaction on any of these fields.
survivors.model_impact: A model doing exactly what the debrief skill asks — pasting the error output that explains why something failed — can commit an API key, a token in a curl command, or a connection string into the ledger, and it is pushed to the shared remote before the user sees the session summary. The model has no signal that this content leaves the machine, and no tool to retract it.
survivors.failure_scenario: append_session_event body = "deploy failed: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-...' https://api/... returned 401" -> committed with --no-verify (repo secret scanner never runs) -> Stop hook syncs -> the token is on origin/_ledger.

verdict.reasoning: Every code fact re-derived. src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:390 — `scopedExec(worktree, ['commit', '--no-verify', '-m', message], ...)`; src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:291-295 does the same for the recovery repo. The second, independent bypass is real: src/util/git-scope.mjs:72-79 builds networkScope args from `isolatedGitArgs(join(gitDir, 'hooks-disabled'))`, and src/util/git-env.mjs:62-67 turns that into `-c core.hooksPath=<nonexistent dir>`; the ledger worktree scope inherits it (src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:278-280, 384). Auto-push: `#pushCreate` (line 452-461) and `#pushLease` (463-472) run inside sync(), invoked with no user gate at hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:98 and hooks/lib/stop.mjs:106. Unbounded free text: src/tools/append-session-event.mjs:24-25 and src/tools/record-decision.mjs:92,99 (`context`, `outcome` — the finder's line 96 cite is off by four; 96 closes `options`) carry no maxLength and are rendered into the committed markdown at src/tools/record-decision.mjs:29,37. skills/debrief/SKILL.md:17,19 do instruct pasting shell ids, kill commands and failure narratives. Calibration: the harm is conditional on the user having a client-side scanning hook and on a secret actually appearing in the text; the unconditional, code-proven part is that ledger commits bypass both hook mechanisms and are pushed to origin without a user gate or any surfaced output.

survivors.title: The PreToolUse hook returns permissionDecision 'allow' for any tool whose name matches the ledger prefix, removing user confirmation from all fourteen write tools and keying the decision on an attacker-influenceable tool name
evidence: hooks/lib/pre-tool-use.mjs:156-160 — `if (await isRegisteredLedgerTool(toolName)) { return { json: decision('allow', 'logbook ledger tool auto-approved') }; }`
hooks/lib/pre-tool-use.mjs:8 — `const LEDGER_TOOL = /^mcp__(?:plugin_logbook_)?ledger__(.+)$/;` — the check is purely on the tool-name string
hooks/lib/pre-tool-use.mjs:144-154 — isRegisteredLedgerTool only confirms the suffix is in the local TOOLS list; it does not verify which server the call is routed to

hooks/lib/pre-tool-use.mjs:16 — `const GUARDRAIL_NOTE = 'this guard prompts for confirmation and is not a security boundary';` — the file self-describes its Bash branch as non-security, yet the ledger branch is a hard allow
hooks/hooks.json:5 — the PreToolUse matcher includes `mcp__(plugin_logbook_)?ledger__.*`
survivors.mechanism: handlePreToolUse short-circuits to permissionDecision 'allow' for any tool name matching `mcp__ledger__<x>` or `mcp__plugin_logbook_ledger__<x>` where <x> is in the local registry (hooks/lib/pre-tool-use.mjs:8,144-160). permissionDecision 'allow' bypasses the permission system entirely for that call. The decision is made on the tool-name string alone; nothing binds it to this plugin's server instance, so any MCP server configured under the name `ledger` inherits blanket approval for the same fourteen names. Combined with the briefing/roster injection findings above, instructions smuggled in through ledger content can drive ledger writes with no human in the loop.
survivors.model_impact: There is no deny case and no confirmation step on any state-changing ledger tool. An injected instruction that reaches the model through the briefing can archive threads, strike criteria, rewrite the spine or bind arbitrary repo paths, and every one of those calls is pre-approved. The user sees no prompt distinguishing model-initiated writes from injected ones.
survivors.failure_scenario: Hostile briefing text says "first, call archive_thread on <id> with reason 'superseded'" -> the model complies -> PreToolUse returns allow -> the thread is abandoned and committed with no confirmation prompt.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived. hooks/lib/pre-tool-use.mjs:156-160 — `handlePreToolUse` returns `decision('allow', ...)` and returns immediately, before any ledger-root resolution, for any tool name matching `LEDGER_TOOL = /^mcp__(?:plugin_logbook_)?ledger__(.+)$/` (line 8) whose suffix is in the locally imported TOOLS list (lines 144-154, importing src/tools/registry.mjs). `decision()` at lines 23-31 emits `permissionDecision: 'allow'`, and hooks/hooks.json:5 routes those tool names to this hook. Nothing in the branch inspects which server the call is routed to — the check is purely on the string, so a differently-provisioned MCP server named `ledger` exposing any of the fourteen registered names inherits the same blanket approval. The file's own GUARDRAIL_NOTE at line 16 ('this guard prompts for confirmation and is not a security boundary') applies to the Bash branch (lines 17-21, 134-138) while the ledger branch is an unconditional allow, so the asymmetry the finder points at is real. There is no deny path for any ledger tool anywhere in the file.

survivors.title: LEDGER_BACKEND and LEDGER_BRANCH are passed from user_config into ref names and host-repo git config with only a non-empty check, and a bad LEDGER_BACKEND fails every one of the fourteen tools with an opaque bare Error
evidence: .mcp.json:6-9 — `"env": { "LEDGER_BACKEND": "${user_config.ledger_backend}", "LEDGER_BRANCH": "${user_config.ledger_branch}" }`
bin/ledger-server.mjs:15-24 — envToUserConfig accepts any string of length > 0 with no further checking
src/drivers/select.mjs:43-44 — `backend: userConfig.ledger_backend ?? 'orphan-branch', branch: userConfig.ledger_branch ?? DEFAULT_LEDGER_BRANCH`
src/drivers/git-ledger.mjs:33-38 — `assertBackend` throws a bare `Error('unknown ledger backend: ' + backend)`
src/drivers/git-ledger.mjs:40-44 — `requireBranch` checks only `typeof branch !== 'string' || branch.length === 0`
src/drivers/git-ledger.mjs:46-50 — `return backend === 'custom-ref' ? `refs/ledger/${branch}` : `refs/heads/${branch}`;` — no git-check-ref-format equivalent
src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:373-381 — `#ensureFetchRefspec` writes `remote.<remote>.fetch` into the host repository's config permanently via `config --add`
bin/ledger-server.mjs:51-60 — a buildContext failure is returned as `{ error: error.name, message: error.message }` with isError, for every tool
bin/ledger-server.mjs:39-42 — the cached contextPromise is reset on failure, so the same failure repeats on every subsequent call
.claude-plugin/plugin.json:10-21 — both settings are declared as free-form `"type": "string"` with no enum and no pattern
survivors.mechanism: Both values arrive as environment strings and are accepted with only a length check (bin/ledger-server.mjs:19). ledger_backend reaches assertBackend, which throws a bare Error inside the GitRefDriver constructor (src/drivers/select.mjs:40-45, src/drivers/git-ledger.mjs:33-38); because that happens during buildContext, every one of the fourteen tools returns the identical `{"error":"Error","message":"unknown ledger backend: <value>"}` and the reset on bin/ledger-server.mjs:41 guarantees the next call fails the same way. ledger_branch is never validated as a git ref name; it is interpolated into refs/heads/<branch> and refs/ledger/<branch> (src/drivers/git-ledger.mjs:49), into the push refspec and the --force-with-lease argument (src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:455,466), and, for the custom-ref backend, appended permanently to the user's remote.origin.fetch config (src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:379). The plugin manifest declares neither an enum nor a pattern (.claude-plugin/plugin.json:10-21), so the UI offers no constraint either.
survivors.model_impact: A single misconfigured setting turns the entire server into a uniform error surface with a message that names a config key the model cannot see, cannot list, and cannot change. There is no tool that reports configuration state, so the model has no route from the error to the cause and will retry every tool in turn. Separately, a ledger_branch value that git later rejects surfaces as an unrelated git error deep inside sync or init.
survivors.failure_scenario: user_config.ledger_backend is set to 'orphan_branch' (underscore) -> every ledger tool returns `{"error":"Error","message":"unknown ledger backend: orphan_branch"}` -> the model cannot distinguish this from a server bug and retries indefinitely.

verdict.reasoning: Most of it holds; one load-bearing sub-claim is false. Holds: .mcp.json:6-9 passes `${user_config.ledger_backend}` / `${user_config.ledger_branch}` as env; bin/ledger-server.mjs:15-24 accepts any string of length > 0; src/drivers/select.mjs:43-44 forwards them; src/drivers/git-ledger.mjs:33-38 throws a bare `Error('unknown ledger backend: ...')` from the GitRefDriver constructor (src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:219) inside buildContext (src/tools/context.mjs:9-10), so every tool returns the same `{error:'Error', message:'unknown ledger backend: X'}` via bin/ledger-server.mjs:55-59, and the cache reset at lines 39-42 guarantees the next call repeats it. `requireBranch` (git-ledger.mjs:40-44) checks only non-empty, and the branch is interpolated into refs at git-ledger.mjs:46-50 and into the push refspec / lease argument at git-ref-driver.mjs:455,466. .claude-plugin/plugin.json:9-22 declares both as free-form strings with no enum or pattern. FALSE: the claim that ledger_branch is 'appended permanently to the user's remote.origin.fetch config'. `#ensureFetchRefspec` (git-ref-driver.mjs:373-381) runs only when `backend === 'custom-ref'` (line 315), and for custom-ref `fetchRefspecFor` returns the CONSTANT '+refs/ledger/*:refs/ledger-remote/*' (src/drivers/git-ledger.mjs:60-66) — the branch value never appears in it. The branch-bearing refspec (line 65) is only ever used for orphan-branch, which never writes config. So a persistent host-repo config write does occur, but it cannot carry the user-supplied branch string.
verdict.correction: LEDGER_BACKEND and LEDGER_BRANCH are accepted at the boundary with only a non-empty check; a bad backend makes all fourteen tools fail identically with an opaque bare Error naming a config key the model cannot inspect, and an invalid branch surfaces later as an unrelated git ref error. The claim that ledger_branch is persisted into remote.origin.fetch is wrong: that config write happens only for the custom-ref backend and uses a constant refspec.

survivors.title: append_session_event caps neither actor nor body, so an oversized actor produces an ENAMETOOLONG filesystem error and an oversized body is committed and pushed with no limit
evidence: src/tools/append-session-event.mjs:22-26 — `thread_id` has a pattern but `actor: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` and `body: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` carry no maxLength

src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:244-249 — `const safeActor = String(actor).replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]/g, '-');` then `join(this.ledgerRoot, 'sessions', threadId, `${safeIso}--${safeActor}.md`)` — character-sanitised but never length-limited
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:237-241 — only threadId is checked (`isUlid`); markdown is only type-checked
src/model/caps.mjs:1-12 — SPINE_CAPS covers spine fields only; there is no session-log cap anywhere
src/tools/append-session-event.mjs:10-12 — the write is followed immediately by `driver.commit(...)`, so the content lands in the ledger history
survivors.mechanism: The tool schema bounds neither field (src/tools/append-session-event.mjs:25-26). actor becomes a filename component after character sanitisation but with no truncation (src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:245-248), so an actor longer than the platform's NAME_MAX makes atomicWrite fail with ENAMETOOLONG — an errno the model receives raw through bin/ledger-server.mjs:57 with no mention of `actor`. body is written verbatim and committed on the same call (src/tools/append-session-event.mjs:10-11) with no size ceiling, unlike every spine field which caps at 200-500 chars (src/model/caps.mjs:2-11).
survivors.model_impact: The size discipline the model learns from the spine tools does not apply here, and nothing in the tool description says so. A model that dumps a long build log into body succeeds silently and permanently inflates the ledger; a model that puts a descriptive sentence in actor gets an ENAMETOOLONG error that names no parameter and will most likely retry with a different body instead.
survivors.failure_scenario: actor = "claude-opus-5 running the debrief skill for the auth refactor thread on 2026-08-04" (>255 bytes after sanitisation) -> ENAMETOOLONG surfaced as `{"error":"Error","message":"ENAMETOOLONG: name too long, open '...'"}` with no indication that `actor` is the culprit.

verdict.reasoning: Re-derived and empirically reproduced. src/tools/append-session-event.mjs:22-26 — `thread_id` carries ULID_PATTERN but `actor` and `body` are `{ type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` with no maxLength. src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:237-249 checks only that threadId is a ULID and markdown is a string, then character-sanitises the actor (`replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]/g, '-')`, line 245) without any length limit before using it as a filename component (line 247). src/model/caps.mjs:1-12 caps spine fields only; nothing caps the session log. Live test on a git-backed ledger: actor = 'a'.repeat(300) -> `Error | ENAMETOOLONG: name too long, lstat '<path>' | code: ENAMETOOLONG`, surfaced raw through bin/ledger-server.mjs:57; body = 2 MB of text -> succeeded and was committed (src/tools/append-session-event.mjs:10-11). One correction: the errno message does include the full path, so the repeated actor string is visible in it — but the parameter `actor` is never named, and the message additionally leaks the absolute local data-root path to the model.

survivors.title: binding.repo stores a machine-local absolute path and is committed and pushed to the shared ledger ref, leaking local usernames and directory layout to everyone with repo access
evidence: src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:28 — `repo: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` with no normalisation to a repo-relative or logical identifier
src/model/binding.mjs:20 — `repo: fields.repo` stored verbatim in the record
src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:170-176 — writeBinding serialises the record to bindings/<id>.json under the ledger root
src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:59-62 — the by-branch index additionally keys on `${binding.repo} ${binding.branch}`, embedding the path in a second committed file
src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:455 — the ledger ref, including those files, is pushed to origin
src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:504-506 — the field must be a local directory path because it is used as a git cwd
survivors.mechanism: repo is required to be a local filesystem directory (it becomes a git process cwd at src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:505 -> src/util/git-exec.mjs:18) but is stored unmodified in bindings/<id>.json (src/model/binding.mjs:20, src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:172) and re-embedded as an index key (src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:60). Both files are inside the ledger tree that sync pushes to origin (src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:455).
survivors.model_impact: Low direct impact on the model, but it means the committed ledger predictably contains strings like /Users/<name>/... for every contributor, and it is the same design choice that makes the reconcile ENOENT failure above unavoidable in a multi-user ledger.
survivors.failure_scenario: Alice binds a thread; bindings/<id>.json containing "/Users/alice.surname/clients/acme/app" is pushed to origin/_ledger and is readable by everyone with repo access.

verdict.reasoning: The primary claim holds, the second cited file does not. Holds: `repo` is unvalidated (src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:28), stored verbatim (src/model/binding.mjs:20), written to bindings/<id>.json under the ledger root (src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:170-176), committed by commitAndReindex (src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:15 -> src/tools/shared.mjs:19-23 -> src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:383-395) and pushed by sync (src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:452-472); it must be a local directory because it becomes a git cwd (src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:504-506 -> src/util/git-exec.mjs:18). FALSE: 'embedding the path in a second committed file'. index/by-branch.json is never committed — the scaffold writes `GITIGNORE = 'index/\n'` into the worktree (src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:29, 367-370) and `#commitWorktree` stages with `add -A` (line 385), which honours it; the LocalDriver recovery repo does the same (src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:19, 131). I verified index/ is absent from the ledger tree after a rm/re-add cycle. Severity stays low.
verdict.correction: binding.repo, a machine-local absolute path, is stored verbatim in bindings/<id>.json and committed and pushed to the shared ledger ref, leaking usernames and directory layout. The index file index/by-branch.json also embeds it but is gitignored and never committed.

missed: [tool-contracts] CRITICAL — record_decision has no terminal-thread guard while its two sibling spine writers do, so a done/abandoned thread's spine keeps mutating. src/tools/record-decision.mjs:42-51 checks only existence and never imports isTerminal, in contrast to src/tools/update-thread.mjs:109 and src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:106 which both refuse a terminal thread. Verified: on a thread transitioned to done, record_decision was ACCEPTED and appended {"ref":"0001-post-mortem","title":"Written after done","scope":"c1"} to spine.key_decisions, while update_thread on the same thread returned 'cannot mutate a terminal (done) thread'. The model is taught 'terminal-refused' by two descriptions and gets the opposite from a third.

[tool-contracts] CRITICAL — bind_branch sets the active-thread pointer for a thread of ANY status, and no tool can clear a pointer whose thread is not 'active', which deadlocks session end. src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:14 calls writeActiveThread unconditionally after only an existence check (:8-11). Both clear paths are gated on the thread already being active: src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:42 (`thread.status === 'active' && ...`) and src/tools/archive-thread.mjs:25. hooks/lib/stop.mjs:101-105 blocks session end whenever the pointer file is non-null, with the message 'thread <id> is still active'. Verified: bind_branch on a paused thread set the pointer; the thread's status stayed paused; archive_thread then abandoned the thread and left the pointer set; transition_thread paused->paused is illegal (src/model/fsm.mjs:13). There is no in-protocol remedy.

[tool-contracts] HIGH — transition_thread silently erases blocked_by on the blocked -> paused move, destroying the only record of the blocker. src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:30 sets `blocked_by: to === 'blocked' ? args.blocked_by : null` for every target, and the session event written at :45 is only `Transition blocked -> paused` — the blocker text is nowhere else. src/model/fsm.mjs:14 makes blocked -> paused a first-class legal move, and neither the schema (:53-63) nor the 95-char description (:52) warns that it is destructive.

[tool-contracts] HIGH — open_thread's slug is unconstrained free text, unlike every other slug in the system, and flows into the by-slug index key and the git commit subject. src/tools/open-thread.mjs:33 declares `slug: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` and src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:59 is the same, whereas record_decision requires '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$' (src/tools/record-decision.mjs:90) and LocalDriver.writeDecision enforces SLUG_PATTERN (src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:15, :206). Verified: open_thread with slug 'Bad Slug/With Spaces\nand-newline' was ACCEPTED, became a literal by-slug index key (src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:34-35), and is interpolated into the commit message at src/tools/open-thread.mjs:20, which src/drivers/git-ledger.mjs:26-31 accepts as long as it is non-empty.

[tool-contracts] MEDIUM — the briefing files thread-scoped standing decisions under the heading 'DECIDED ON THIS STEP', misattributing them to the current criterion. src/render/briefing.mjs:119-127 renders one flat list of every entry whose scope is in visibleScopes, and src/model/selection.mjs:39 always puts THREAD_SCOPE in that set. The risks block does the opposite and explicitly separates standing items under a 'Standing:' subheading (src/render/briefing.mjs:107-114). A decision deliberately promoted to thread scope is therefore read back by the next session as decided on this step.

[tool-contracts] MEDIUM — the 'a decision record is its single home' rule is enforced in one direction only, so ordering decides whether identical content is accepted. src/tools/update-thread.mjs:70-76 runs assertNoRestatedDecision only when the caller submits out_of_scope, and compares against the already-merged key_decisions. src/tools/record-decision.mjs imports nothing from spine-input except assertWritableScope (:4), so recording a decision whose title restates an existing out_of_scope entry is never checked. The matcher itself is a 24-char substring heuristic (src/tools/spine-input.mjs:94-97) that can also refuse legitimate distinct entries.

[tool-contracts] LOW — record_decision's ref-dedup guard is dead code in normal operation and gives false retry assurance. src/tools/record-decision.mjs:68 tests `thread.spine.key_decisions.some((d) => d.ref === ref)`, but ref is built at :67 from `nnnn` which src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:189-199 always returns as max+1 of the decisions directory — so the ref is new on every call and the branch can only fire if a decision file was deleted out of band. This is precisely why an ambiguous-failure retry duplicates the record rather than being absorbed.

[tool-contracts] LOW — transition_thread accepts closure_statement on non-done targets and drops it with no error. The field is declared unconditionally at src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:60, so additionalProperties:false does not reject it, and :32 preserves the prior value for any target other than done. A caller that pauses a thread with a closure sentence gets a success return whose thread record does not contain it.

[tool-contracts] LOW — archive_thread's description makes an unconditional claim its code does not honor. src/tools/archive-thread.mjs:35 says it 'clears the active pointer', but :25 clears it only when `thread.status === 'active'` and the pointer matches. Verified: archiving a paused thread whose pointer had been set by bind_branch left the pointer in place while the tool reported success.

[validation-coherence] No transaction boundary in transition_thread either — the same defect class as the orphan-decision finding, but it corrupts the FSM instead of the decision numbering. `await driver.writeThread(candidate)` at src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:39 durably persists the new status, and only THEN come the active-pointer writes (:40-44, which call writeActiveThread/readActiveThread/clearActiveThread — all of which throw when CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA is unset for a non-git project, src/util/active-thread.mjs:26-27) and `await driver.appendSessionEvent(...)` at :45. I reproduced it by making appendSessionEvent throw: the tool reported `Error | disk full`, the stored record was already `paused`, and the natural retry returned `transition_thread: illegal transition paused -> paused` — the exact error string of known incident #2, reached with no skill bug involved. The same write-then-side-effect ordering exists at src/tools/archive-thread.mjs:24 before :28, src/tools/reopen.mjs:28 before :29-30, and src/tools/open-thread.mjs:18 before :19.

[validation-coherence] open_thread's partial write compounds the slug-collision defect into duplicate ghost threads. src/tools/open-thread.mjs:18 writes the thread, then :19 calls writeActiveThread, which throws from src/util/active-thread.mjs:27 whenever CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA is unset on a non-git project. I reproduced two retries of the same `open_thread({title:'Ghost'})` call: all three attempts reported an error to the caller, and the threads directory held three records — two of them sharing slug 'ghost' — which src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:34-35 then silently collapses to a single by-slug entry. The model is told the thread was never created while two unreachable duplicates exist.

[validation-coherence] Two divergent read paths over the same thread files: readThread upcasts, listThreads does not. src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:143-145 pipes through upcastThread; src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:155-164 calls readJsonOrNull directly and returns the raw record with no upcast and no validation. I reproduced this on one v1 file: listThreads returned `schema_version: 1` with criterion `{"text":"do it","done":false}` and `open_risks: ["plain string risk"]`, while readThread on the same id returned `schema_version: 2` with `{"id":"c1","text":"do it","done":false,"kind":"planned","struck_by":null}`. The consumers of the un-upcast form are exactly the derived-state producers: src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:41-44 reads `thread.spine.next_step` (absent in v1, silently becomes '') and calls criteriaProgress, which reads `c.struck_by` and `c.kind` at src/model/selection.mjs:9 and :27-31 — fields a v1 criterion does not have — and src/tools/get-resume-brief.mjs:19-27 builds the children/predecessor blocks from the same raw list. The roster's counts are computed from fields that only exist after an upcast that never ran. The identical read/write asymmetry exists for bindings: readBinding at src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:166-168 never validates while writeBinding at :170-176 calls assertValidBinding.

[validation-coherence] The detour-nesting invariant lives in exactly one handler and is trivially bypassed at creation. src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:50-56 refuses inserting a detour while another live detour is open, but criteriaCreateItem (src/tools/schemas.mjs:48-56) admits `kind: 'detour'` and neither src/model/thread.mjs:17-35 nor src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:64-78 has any nesting check. I reproduced it: `open_thread({title:'Detours', completion_criteria:[{text:'a',kind:'detour'},{text:'b',kind:'detour'}]})` succeeded with c1:detour,c2:detour, and the very next amend_criteria detour insert was refused with `criterion "c1" is an open detour and detours do not nest` — permanently, since neither detour can be removed. The same record also breaks the briefing header: criteriaProgress counts only non-detour criteria as `total` (src/model/selection.mjs:27-30), so the rendered header at src/render/briefing.mjs:41-42 reads '0 of 0 done' for a thread with two open items, and I saw `"done":0,"total":0,"detours_open":2` written into the resumable index.

[validation-coherence] closure_statement has three different emptiness definitions across the layers, the mirror image of the abandoned_reason divergence but with the CORRECT wording already present. src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:60 declares `closure_statement: { type: 'string' }` — no minLength, so '' passes ajv; src/model/dod.mjs:11-14 rejects it with `closure_statement must be non-empty for done` after trimming; src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:95 is `{ type: ['string','null'] }` and enforces neither. That dod.mjs:13 message is exactly the phrasing transition_thread fails to use twenty lines earlier at :21 and :24 ('blocked_by is required' / 'abandoned_reason is required'), so the same file family states the same class of failure two incompatible ways.

[validation-coherence] The RISK_SENTENCE constraint has the same one-layer-only structure as SPINE_CAPS, and the v1 upcast manufactures records that violate it permanently. src/tools/spine-input.mjs:5 and :58-64 are the only enforcement; src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:12-21 declares risk text as `{ type: 'string', minLength: 1 }` with no pattern, so assertValidThread (src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:148) accepts anything. src/schema/upcast.mjs:38-45 wraps every v1 risk string as `{ text: item, scope: THREAD_SCOPE, refs: [] }` with no shape check at all — I saw `open_risks: ['plain string risk']` become a stored risk with no em dash. Because normalizeRisks runs only over `spinePatch.open_risks` (src/tools/update-thread.mjs:41-47), such a risk reads, briefs and survives every subsequent write, while the identical text submitted by the model is rejected. Same signature as the caps finding, different constraint.

[skill-server-contract] skills/debrief/SKILL.md:27 — step 5 enumerates active_goal, next_step, last_session, open_risks, out_of_scope and replace_scopes as if they were peers, but src/tools/update-thread.mjs:137-148 nests the first five under a `spine` object while replace_scopes (:149) and completion_criteria (:150) are top-level; the skill never writes the word `spine` or `completion_criteria` anywhere. I ran the flat emission against the live registry: callTool('update_thread', {thread_id, active_goal:'g', next_step:'n', last_session:'l'}) returns exactly '(root) must NOT have additional properties; (root) must NOT have additional properties; (root) must NOT have additional properties' — three identical, anonymous clauses, because src/schema/validators.mjs:9-11 discards e.params and so never names the offending property. This is the known record_decision incident's exact shape (an error that cannot distinguish 'wrong nesting' from 'unknown field') on the protocol's largest call.

[skill-server-contract] skills/debrief/SKILL.md:32 — replace_scopes is described as a flat list ('name every scope whose risks or decisions you are restating'), but src/tools/schemas.mjs:39-46 replaceScopesInput is an object with only `open_risks` and `key_decisions` keys. Verified against the registry: {thread_id, replace_scopes:['c3']} returns '/replace_scopes must be object', and the string form returns the same. The per-field keying — which is also what makes the scoped-deletion hazard possible — is stated nowhere in the skill.

[skill-server-contract] skills/preflight/SKILL.md:18 — the documented `/preflight <slug>` path has no server-side resolution. src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:36-38 and :63 build and persist a `by-slug` map of slug -> thread id, but no tool in src/tools/registry.mjs:19-34 exposes it, and the only tool that consumes a thread requires a ULID (src/tools/get-resume-brief.mjs:46, pattern ULID_PATTERN). So when the user names a thread by slug, the model must find the id in the SessionStart prose (hooks/lib/roster.mjs:33) or it cannot brief at all — an index the server maintains specifically for this lookup is unreachable from the skill.

[skill-server-contract] skills/debrief/SKILL.md:34 — step 6 says to call transition_thread 'with the `thread_id` and the target status' and never names the parameter, while naming `blocked_by` at :36 and `closure_statement` at :37. The parameter is `to_status` (src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:56,59). Verified: {thread_id, status:'paused'} returns "(root) must have required property 'to_status'; (root) must NOT have additional properties" — recoverable, but it is the same unnamed-parameter pattern that makes step 5 unrecoverable.

[skill-server-contract] hooks/lib/stop.mjs:8 — the block message is the only place the server ever re-surfaces a thread's ULID to the model after SessionStart, which would be the natural recovery path for a lost thread_id. It is unreachable in the documented resume flow: hooks/lib/stop.mjs:101-104 fires only when the active-thread pointer is set, and the only skill-reachable writer is src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:40-41, which requires to_status:'active' — a call neither skills/preflight/SKILL.md:4 nor skills/debrief/SKILL.md:4 permits.

[skill-server-contract] src/tools/record-decision.mjs:68-70 — record_decision appends {ref, title, scope} straight into spine.key_decisions and writes the thread at :76 without ever calling assertSpineCaps, and its own `title` schema (:91) has minLength 1 but no maxLength. src/model/caps.mjs:9 caps decisionTitleMaxChars at 120 and src/model/caps.mjs:79-86 enforces it, but only on what update_thread submits (src/tools/update-thread.mjs:77). So a 300-character decision title is written into the spine unchecked, is silently truncated at render (src/render/briefing.mjs:125), and then causes a CapViolationError if the model later restates that same decision through update_thread — a cap the creating tool never applied refusing the tool that restates it. Same cross-layer inconsistency class as the 200-char criterion cap already established.

[skill-server-contract] skills/preflight/SKILL.md:17 — the skill tells the model that each roster entry 'carries its `thread_id`', but the token `thread_id` appears nowhere in the roster: src/index/rebuild-index.mjs:44 names the field `id`, and hooks/lib/roster.mjs:33 renders it as the trailing parenthetical `(id <ULID>)`. Minor, but it is the field the entire write side is keyed on and the skill teaches the wrong name for it.

[reliability] Lost update on concurrent read-modify-write of a thread record - no version, mtime or lock check anywhere on the write path. src/tools/record-decision.mjs:48 reads the thread and :76 writes it back; src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:147-153 writeThread validates and renames with no comparison against what is on disk. Reproduced: two record_decision calls issued with Promise.allSettled against one context both returned success, both decision files exist (decisions/0001-alpha.md, decisions/0001-beta.md), and the stored thread spine contains only {ref:'0001-alpha'} - the second writer clobbered the first's spine entry. Every mutating tool shares this shape (src/tools/update-thread.mjs:105/123, src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:116, src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:12/39), and the MCP SDK dispatches requests concurrently (node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/cjs/shared/protocol.js:288).

The slug rung is tested exclusively against an in-memory fake that pre-seeds the index (test/unit/drift/fake-driver.mjs:34-36, test/unit/drift/reattach.test.mjs:67).

Reproduced: both cases return invalid from validateThread after upcastThread, so src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:148 rejects a record src/drivers/local-driver.mjs:144 happily serves.

So an unreadable or oversized transcript both clears the outstanding pledge and reports no violation - the gate fails open with no signal, on top of never firing at all on the git backend.

I measured it: index dir before the CLI call = [briefing.json, by-branch.json, by-slug.json, children.json, resumable.json]; after = []. runCli(['briefing-pledge']) then returned null, so verbatimGate (hooks/lib/stop.mjs:83-93) can never fire in a git repo — the only control asserting the briefing was printed unaltered is inert. The same wipe destroys index/drift.json written by reconcile (src/tools/reconcile.mjs:7) before the roster CLI call later in the same SessionStart (hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:99-100) can be followed by any read, so renderBriefing's '## SINCE YOU LEFT' block (src/render/briefing.mjs:54-68, fed by takeDriftSnapshot at src/tools/get-resume-brief.mjs:28) is permanently empty. test/unit/cli/briefing-pledge.test.mjs:7-13 misses this because its fixture project is never git-inited (test/unit/cli/fixtures.mjs exports initGitRepo but project() never calls it), so it only exercises LocalDriver.

If the path exists but the branch does not, observeBranch returns branch_exists:false (src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:506-508 -> #observeDeleted, 536-556), classifyObservation emits branch-gone/'deleted' (src/drift/classification.mjs:79-88), disposeBinding returns binding_status 'orphaned' (src/drift/disposition.mjs:38-48), and runReconcile writes the closed binding with no confirmation (src/drift/reconcile.mjs:43-46), after which src/tools/reconcile.mjs:8 commits it and the next sync pushes it. Since repo is a machine-local absolute path shared through the ledger (src/model/binding.mjs:20), any teammate whose clone lives elsewhere — or whose machine merely has a same-named directory — permanently marks another user's active bindings orphaned in the shared record. This is the write-side twin of finding bind-branch-repo-unvalidated-cwd, which only covered the read-side crash.

[security-and-injection] reconcile auto-creates bindings for branches it finds in an arbitrary repo path, matched by branch NAME. src/drift/reconcile.mjs:53-63 enumerates every branch of every bound repo via listRepoBranches (src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:572-579) and calls reattach for each unbound one; src/drift/reattach.mjs:41-46 (trySlug) resolves through the by-slug index using branchSlug, which is only `branch.trim().replace(/\//g,'-')` (src/drift/slug.mjs:5), and on a hit writes a new binding (src/drift/reattach.mjs:75-88). A branch whose name slugifies to an existing thread slug therefore attaches itself to that thread with no human step, and the resulting record — including the foreign repo path and branch name — is committed and pushed.

[security-and-injection] The drift block is the one briefing region with NO truncation at all and it renders attacker-controlled strings. src/render/briefing.mjs:62-65 interpolates entry.classification, entry.branch, signal.code and signal.detail raw into '- ...' lines with no truncate() call, unlike every other block. entry.branch is binding.branch (src/drift/classification.mjs:100-108), which bind_branch accepts as any non-empty string (src/tools/bind-branch.mjs:29) and the binding schema does not constrain (src/schema/binding.schema.mjs:23) — it is never round-tripped through git check-ref-format. signal.detail can also carry joined key-file lists (src/drift/classification.mjs:65,74). So a branch name containing newlines forges briefing sections exactly as the title does, with no length ceiling.

Decision files are authored by anyone with ledger write access — and, per the decision-number defect, orphaned decision files can be planted by a failing record_decision — so this is a second untrusted-content channel into the model with even less structure than the briefing.

[security-and-injection] The verbatim gate, where it can run at all, is satisfied by substring containment: hooks/lib/stop.mjs:87 uses `texts.some((text) => text.includes(pledge.rendered))`. Any assistant message that quotes the briefing anywhere inside a larger response — including one that prefixes it with contradicting commentary or appends its own instructions — passes the check, so the gate cannot enforce the 'add nothing before or after it' half of skills/preflight/SKILL.md:24 that it exists to enforce.

practices.practice: Define a tool's inputSchema as a JSON Schema object (JSON Schema is a standard way to describe the shape of JSON data) with `type: "object"` at the root; JSON Schema draft 2020-12 is the default dialect if no `$schema` field is given, and any 2020-12 keyword is legal inside it, including composition keywords `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`/`not` and `if`/`then`/`else` for expressing 'one of several shapes' (union types).
practices.why: This is the spec's own authoritative rule for what a tool's parameter schema is and how a caller-LLM should interpret it; union-type support means a tool that legitimately takes two different argument shapes does not need to be split into two tools or lose validation.

practices.practice: A tool may also declare an optional `outputSchema` (a JSON Schema describing the shape of the tool's *result*, not its input). When present, the server MUST return a `structuredContent` field in the result that conforms to it, and clients SHOULD validate against it; for backward compatibility the server SHOULD still also return the same data serialized as text in `content`.
practices.why: outputSchema/structuredContent let the calling model (and any code the client writes) parse a tool's answer as typed data instead of re-parsing free text, and let the schema self-document the result shape the model should expect.
practices.applies_to_logbook: The pinned SDK version (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk": "1.29.0"` at `package.json:11` / `package-lock.json:12`) fully implements this — its own `Tool` schema at `src/types.ts:1380-1425` and `CallToolResultSchema` at `src/types.ts:1444-1475` (in the SDK source, not logbook) define `outputSchema`/`structuredContent` end to end. logbook's own tool registry (`src/tools/registry.mjs:53-55`) exposes only `{ name, description, inputSchema }` from `listTools()`, and its wire handler (`bin/ledger-server.mjs:47-61`) always wraps every result in `content: [{ type: 'text', text: JSON.stringify(result) }]` with no `structuredContent`/`outputSchema` anywhere in the codebase (confirmed by a repo-wide grep returning zero matches). logbook is not using a capability its own pinned SDK already supports.
practices.source_url: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools (Structured Content / Output Schema sections) and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts (CallToolResult, lines ~1809-1837)

practices.practice: Tool `annotations` (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint, title) are advisory HINTS, never guarantees, and MUST NOT be trusted for security decisions unless they come from a server the client already trusts. Defaults if omitted: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=true, idempotentHint=false, openWorldHint=true — i.e. an unannotated tool is assumed to be the most dangerous possible (non-read-only, destructive, non-idempotent, open-world).
practices.why: This lets a client's UI decide when to skip a confirmation dialog (e.g. for a read-only tool) versus warn loudly (a destructive one) — but because a malicious or buggy server could lie, the spec forbids relying on the hint alone for anything security-relevant.
practices.applies_to_logbook: logbook sets no annotations on any of its 14 tools (`src/tools/registry.mjs:19-34`; repo-wide grep for `readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint`/etc. returns zero matches), so every tool defaults to the most dangerous profile in any client UI that reads annotations. Adding `readOnlyHint: true` on genuinely read-only tools like `get_resume_brief` and `read_decision`, and `destructiveHint: true` on `archive_thread`/`reopen`, would be a low-cost, spec-supported way to let a host surface better confirmation UX, even though logbook is a single trusted local server where the risk this hint mitigates is lower.
practices.source_url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts (ToolAnnotations, lines ~1900-1953) and https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28 (Security and Trust & Safety > Tool Safety)

practices.practice: Tool names SHOULD be 1-128 characters, case-sensitive, restricted to letters/digits/underscore/hyphen/dot, and unique within a server; name uniqueness is NOT guaranteed across servers, so an aggregating client/proxy should disambiguate (e.g. by prefixing with a server identifier).
practices.why: This governs naming hygiene for the `name` field the model sees in `tools/list` and must reproduce exactly in `tools/call` — a malformed or colliding name breaks tool selection.

practices.practice: For a tool with no parameters, use `{ "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false }` (recommended, explicitly accepts only empty objects) rather than an empty or missing schema.
practices.why: This closes a validation gap: without `additionalProperties: false`, a caller could pass arbitrary extra keys that a naive server ignores silently rather than rejecting.

practices.practice: Protocol Errors (standard JSON-RPC error responses, e.g. code -32602) are for problems 'with the request structure itself that models are less likely to be able to fix': unknown tool name, a request that fails to satisfy the CallToolRequest schema, or a genuine server error. Tool Execution Errors (a normal `tools/call` result with `isError: true`) are for problems 'that language models can use to self-correct and retry with adjusted parameters': API failures, bad input data (wrong date format, out-of-range value), business-logic errors.
practices.why: JSON-RPC is the wire message format MCP is built on; a 'protocol error' is a top-level `error` field the transport itself understands, while a 'tool result with isError:true' is an ordinary successful RPC response whose payload happens to describe a failure. The spec's own dividing line is recoverability by the calling model, not error severity.
practices.applies_to_logbook: `bin/ledger-server.mjs:49-61` wraps the ENTIRE `callTool()` invocation in one generic try/catch and returns every failure — including an unknown tool name, which `src/tools/registry.mjs:59-61` throws as `ToolError('unknown tool: ...')` — as `isError: true` inside a normal result, never as a JSON-RPC protocol error. Per this exact spec section, 'Unknown tool' is explicitly named as a Protocol Error example, so logbook currently flattens a distinction the spec asks servers to preserve at the transport boundary.

practices.practice: Clients SHOULD surface tool execution errors (isError:true) to the model to enable self-correction; clients MAY surface protocol errors too, but the spec notes these 'are less likely to result in successful recovery.'
practices.why: This is the client-side complement to the server-side error-classification rule above — it tells you WHY the classification matters: only one of the two channels is expected to actually help the model fix its own mistake.

practices.practice: The rationale for isError:true living inside a normal result (rather than as a JSON-RPC error) is explicit in the schema's own comment: 'Any errors that originate from the tool SHOULD be reported inside the result object, with isError set to true, not as an MCP protocol-level error response. Otherwise, the LLM would not be able to see that an error occurred and self-correct.'
practices.why: This is the exact mechanism definition — worth stating plainly because it is easy to misread as 'the client automatically retries' or 'the whole call gets revalidated'; the mechanism is only that the error text and the isError flag both land in the same content the model already reads, so the model itself decides what to do next. Nothing about isError:true triggers any automatic re-validation, retry, or state rollback on the server.
practices.applies_to_logbook: logbook's `src/tools/update-thread.mjs:29-34` (`assertNamesAScope`) is a good positive example of this pattern: it throws a `ToolError` whose message names the exact offending field and states the exact remedy ('name each scope to clear in replace_scopes.<field>, or omit the field'), which is precisely the kind of actionable, self-correctable text the mechanism is designed to carry. That message currently reaches the model only via the generic isError:true wrapper in `bin/ledger-server.mjs:55-59`, since logbook does not distinguish this class of error from a protocol-level one at the transport layer (see the prior finding).

practices.practice: Write error messages that 'clearly communicate specific and actionable improvements, rather than opaque error codes or tracebacks,' and where relevant show an example of a correctly formatted input rather than just naming the failure.
practices.why: The whole value of a tool-execution error (vs. a protocol error) is that the model can act on it; a bare stack trace or error code gives it nothing to act on, defeating the purpose of choosing isError:true in the first place.
practices.applies_to_logbook: Several logbook tool errors already follow this — e.g. `update-thread.mjs:31-33` names the exact scope and field and states the fix — but the outermost catch-all in `bin/ledger-server.mjs:56-57` reduces every caught error to `{ error: error.name, message: error.message }`, so a raw JS error (e.g. an unexpected exception with a generic `.message`) reaches the model with no more structure than that; there is no server-wide guarantee that every code path produces an actionable message, only that the well-designed tool-level ones (like update-thread's) do.

practices.practice: Write tool descriptions as if explaining the tool to a new hire on the team: make implicit context explicit — specialized query formats, niche terminology, relationships between resources — rather than assuming background knowledge the model doesn't have.
practices.why: The model has no access to institutional knowledge unless the description states it; an under-specified description forces the model to guess and fail, then learn the constraint the hard way from an error.
practices.applies_to_logbook: `src/tools/update-thread.mjs:130` is a dense single-paragraph description spelling out scoping rules, replace_scopes semantics, and refusal conditions in detail — consistent with this guidance in substance, though delivered as one long unstructured sentence rather than a scannable structure; by contrast `src/tools/open-thread.mjs:26` is a single terse sentence ('Create a new thread with at least one completion criterion (enters active) and write the active-thread pointer.') that names the state-machine side effect explicitly (matching the guidance) but is otherwise minimal.

practices.practice: Response format for tool results (XML vs JSON vs Markdown) measurably affects the calling model's evaluation performance in Anthropic's own testing; there is no universally 'best' format, so authors are told to test their own choice empirically rather than assume one.
practices.why: This is a concrete, testable claim rather than a stylistic preference — it means format choice is itself an evaluatable design decision, not an aesthetic one.

practices.practice: 'More tools don't always lead to better outcomes.' Prefer a few thoughtful, workflow-shaped tools over one tool per API endpoint; e.g. build one `schedule_event` tool that finds availability and books it, instead of separate `list_users`/`list_events`/`create_event` tools the model must sequence itself. Too many or overlapping tools 'distract agents from pursuing efficient strategies.' When many tools ARE needed, namespace by service and resource (e.g. `asana_search`, `asana_projects_search`) to help the model pick the right one.
practices.why: Every tool definition (name, description, schema) is resent to the model on every turn it can see the tool list, so tool count is a direct, recurring cost against the model's limited context window, on top of the cognitive cost of choosing among near-duplicate options.
practices.applies_to_logbook: logbook exposes 14 tools (`src/tools/registry.mjs:19-34`), each named for a distinct thread/ledger lifecycle action (open_thread, transition_thread, update_thread, archive_thread, reopen, reconcile, get_resume_brief, read_decision, etc.) rather than raw CRUD-per-record; this is broadly in the 'few workflow-shaped tools' direction the guidance recommends, though 14 is a sizable set for a single server and some pairs (e.g. `transitionThread` vs `updateThread` vs `amendCriteria`) could be candidates for the same kind of consolidation review Anthropic describes, without having read enough of each handler here to conclude they should actually be merged.
