Independently, make a transition to the CURRENT status an idempotent success rather than an error at src/tools/transition-thread.mjs:17-18, so paused -> paused stops being a wall. With both, a resumed session is genuinely active, the Stop gate at hooks/lib/stop.mjs:101-104 arms for the first time in the normal flow, and debrief's park is legal. Delete the `'active -> paused'` entry from test/unit/skills/skill-invariants.mjs:12: an invariant that forbids stating a precondition is enforcing the defect, not preventing drift.

2. Move every operational rule from prose into the schema, the description, and the refusal text - i.e. the outputs of the other five clusters - and then cut both SKILL.md files down to routing plus the verbatim-print obligation. Rewrite each of the 14 descriptions to the 3-4 sentence shape (what it does; when to use it and when not; what each parameter means; caveats), front-loading the operative constraint because Claude Code truncates at 2KB. Concretely: transition_thread names closure_statement as required-for-done and the criteria precondition; record_decision names the scope default and states that `scope: 'thread'` is what makes a decision standing across criteria (today the default at record-decision.mjs:52-55 silently demotes a cross-cutting decision to a NOT SHOWN count on the very next resume); open_thread and create_successor state the slug derivation rule; get_resume_brief states its side effects.

3. Where a skill must still name a parameter, name it exactly. skills/debrief/SKILL.md:27 must say `spine` and `completion_criteria` are separate TOP-LEVEL arguments (the flat emission it currently implies produces three anonymous 'must NOT have additional properties' clauses); :32 must say `replace_scopes` is an object keyed by field, not a flat list; :34 must say `to_status`; skills/preflight/SKILL.md:26 must say `nnnn` is a zero-padded string.

4. Add `open_thread` (with parent_id) to debrief's allowed-tools, so step 4's documented child-thread escape hatch - which the server's own refusal message at src/tools/amend-criteria.mjs:53-55 also points to - is actually reachable with a permitted tool.

5. Delete the steps that do nothing observable: preflight step 1's `rebuild_index` is replaced by `list_threads`; preflight step 3's `reconcile` is dropped or made conditional on at least one binding existing, since `bind_branch` appears in neither skill's allowed-tools nor prose and src/drift/reconcile.mjs:29-31,50-51 does no work without bindings.

6. De-peak the debrief. With per-field effect reporting in place, allow `update_thread` to apply and report the fields it can validate independently rather than discarding a whole ~45k-character payload for one malformed risk sentence, and move the PostToolUse debrief nudge (hooks/lib/post-tool-use.mjs:49-50) earlier than 70% of transcript budget so the protocol's largest, most heavily gated call is not scheduled at maximum context pressure.

7. Resolve the global rule. It lives outside this repo, so the repo cannot edit it - but the README and the plugin's own server instructions SHOULD state the authoritative semantics (skill names, storage location, cap units and the throw-not-demote rule, decision file naming, that criteria ARE amendable) so the contradiction is resolvable by reading something in-tree, and flag to the user that `<repo>/.claude/ledger/` - the path the global rule names - is outside every root the PreToolUse guard resolves (hooks/lib/ledger-roots.mjs:6-21) and is read by nothing in this server.
clusters.why_this_fix: This is the one place I am deliberately touching skill text rather than only the server, and the reason is scoping, not preference: items 2-5 REMOVE prose and replace it with server-side self-description, and the only prose that stays is parameter names and routing, which the server cannot inject. The justification is direct: skill body content is loaded into context once, is not re-read on later turns, and after auto-compaction re-attached skills share a 25,000-token budget in which only the first 5,000 tokens of each survive - so anything stated only in prose is silently un-enforced exactly when the debrief runs, and the docs themselves redirect to deterministic mechanisms for behavior that must hold regardless of context - https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills. MCP formalizes the same split: hard constraints belong in the declared schema and in isError results the model can self-correct from - https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/latest/server/tools. Description quality is called 'by far the most important factor in tool performance' with a 3-4 sentence floor covering what/when/params/caveats - https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/define-tools - and Claude Code's 2KB description truncation is why the operative constraint goes first - https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp. Note also that both skills must keep enumerating each tool twice (mcp__ledger__* and mcp__plugin_logbook_ledger__*), because allow-rule globs require a literal server segment and 'mcp__*' is rejected in allow position - https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.
rejected_alternatives: Add the missing preconditions and caps to the skill files - the option the brief asks me to justify avoiding, and it fails on three counts: the prose is dropped on compaction precisely when debrief runs, a test forbids the single most important sentence, and the same fact would then need restating in both skills AND the global rule, which is what produced eight contradictions already. A constraint in the input schema and the refusal message reaches every caller including a subagent that never loaded the skill.

Loosen the FSM so every transition is legal - removes the paused -> paused wall but destroys the state machine's entire value: a done thread could be silently reopened, contradicting the deliberate terminal refusal at src/tools/reopen.mjs:12-14 and the empty outgoing sets at src/model/fsm.mjs:15-16.

Delete the thinness invariant test outright and let the skills restate server semantics freely - returns the semantics to the least durable layer and guarantees two copies that drift; the invariant's intent is right, its blacklist is what is wrong.

Leave preflight read-only and have the Stop hook read the resumable index instead of the active-thread pointer - the index is wiped on every git-backend context build (src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs:354-359), so the gate would be dead there for the same measured reason the verbatim pledge already is.
clusters.risk: No on-disk change. Adding a resume transition changes the documented flow, both skills' allowed-tools frontmatter, and the preflight invariant test that currently asserts preflight exposes NO write tool - that assertion exists for a reason (preflight must not silently mutate before the user chooses), so the resume must be an explicit, user-chosen step surfaced in the Resumption Brief, not a side effect of rendering. Making same-status transitions idempotent must not bypass the DoD gate for done -> done or the reason requirements for blocked/abandoned. Arming the Stop gate in the normal flow for the first time means users who previously ended sessions freely will now be blocked until they debrief - intended, but it is a visible behavior change worth calling out in release notes. Finally, per this project's own installed-plugin arrangement, working-tree edits to skills and hooks do not affect the running plugin until reinstall and restart, so any spec must include that step or the change will appear not to work.

clusters.cluster_name: The ledger's working directory is treated as scratch space, not as storage
clusters.root_cause: Every process that touches the ledger begins by deleting the shared working folder and rebuilding it from the last git commit. Nothing owns that folder, so whatever a different process wrote but has not yet committed is destroyed — and files the design deliberately keeps out of commits (the whole derived index and the briefing pledge) are destroyed permanently, because there is nothing to rebuild them from. The one lock that was supposed to prevent this wraps only the deletion, gives up silently after ten seconds and lets the deletion proceed anyway.
clusters.recommended_fix: Three separable changes in src/drivers/. (1) Make provisioning conditional and repair-only. Split GitRefDriver#ensureWorktree (git-ref-driver.mjs:343-352) into #verifyWorktree() — resolveGitDir(this.worktreeDir) succeeds AND `git worktree list` in the host repo names this path AND HEAD resolves — and #provisionWorktree() (:354-359), which is the only destructive path and now runs ONLY when verification fails. init() (:309-319) calls verify-then-repair, never unconditional rm -rf. (2) Move derived state out of the git worktree entirely. Add src/drivers/state-store.mjs backed by <CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA>/<projectKey>/state/, and route readIndexFile/writeIndexFile/deleteIndexFile (local-driver.mjs:252-276) there for BOTH drivers. index/ and the briefing pledge are derived, per-machine and already gitignored (git-ref-driver.mjs:29); putting them inside a directory that gets re-provisioned is the whole bug. This single move revives the verbatim gate, the '## SINCE YOU LEFT' drift block and reattach's by-slug rung without touching any of them. Drop 'index/' from GITIGNORE and delete the index/ entry from SUBDIRS (:27). (3) Make the lock real. acquireWorktreeLock (:55-70) throws a typed LedgerBusyError(retryable:true) on timeout instead of returning false; add withLedgerLock(fn) held across the WHOLE of init(), across #writeInWorktree (:282-287) and across commit() (:397-404), re-entrant within a process via a promise-chained in-memory mutex so concurrent MCP requests serialize rather than deadlock; refresh the lockfile mtime on a 2s heartbeat during long provisions so a slow provision is not declared stale at :40. Also: clear #uncommittedWrite only on the success path (move it out of the finally at :401-403); pass the expected-old-value to every `update-ref` (:393, :476, :495) so a ref advance is a compare-and-swap; and in src/util/atomic-write.mjs fsync the file handle before close and fsync the containing directory after rename (:14-16), and place temp files in a sibling `.tmp/` directory listed in .gitignore instead of next to the target (:12) so a killed process cannot leave a `.json.tmp-<ulid>` orphan that `git add -A` commits.
rejected_alternatives: ADD AN EXISTENCE CHECK BEFORE THE rm -rf AND LEAVE EVERYTHING ELSE - fixes the common case only. The index and pledge still live inside a directory that a genuine repair legitimately destroys, so the verbatim gate stays dead; the lock still fails open, so two processes can still both provision; and writes still take no lock at all.

GIVE EVERY PROCESS ITS OWN WORKTREE - unbounded worktree growth per project, and it makes ref contention worse rather than better since update-ref has no compare-and-swap. It also cannot work for the pledge, which exists precisely to be written by the MCP server process and read by a separately spawned hook process.

COMMIT THE index/ DIRECTORY SO IT SURVIVES RE-PROVISIONING - turns every read into a history-generating write, inflates the shared ledger ref with derived data on every session start, and still loses the pledge to a concurrent rm -rf between write and commit.

ADOPT A FILE-LOCKING LIBRARY (proper-lockfile) - buys a better mutual-exclusion primitive while leaving both real defects untouched: the destructive init and the placement of non-committed state inside the worktree. The existing O_EXCL lock is adequate once it throws and covers the correct span.
clusters.why_this_fix: The MCP handle pattern guidance is explicit that a create-then-reference handle must have a documented lifetime and must produce a clear execution error when it is unknown, precisely so the model can recover — https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/latest/server/tools. thread_id is exactly that handle here, and a store that silently evaporates a just-written record turns a live handle into an unknown one with no error at all, which is the failure the guidance exists to prevent. The lock-throws-instead-of-returning-false half is supported by Claude Code's own recoverable/unrecoverable split — transient contention is retryable and should be reported as such, configuration and not-found errors are not — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.
clusters.risk: Holding the lock across every write and commit serializes concurrent tool calls; the MCP SDK dispatches requests concurrently (node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/cjs/shared/protocol.js:288), so a non-re-entrant mutex would self-deadlock a handler that writes twice. Verify-then-repair risks adopting a worktree left in a genuinely broken state that the old unconditional rm -rf used to paper over — #verifyWorktree must be strict enough to catch a detached/missing HEAD. Moving index/ out of the worktree changes no committed bytes (index/ is gitignored at git-ref-driver.mjs:29, so it was never in any commit), so no on-disk migration is needed for real ledger data; stale index/ directories inside existing worktrees are destroyed by the next repair and can be ignored. fsync adds a syscall per write, measurably slower on spinning disks and worth it under Quality-over-Speed.

clusters.cluster_name: Multi-step tool calls have no transaction, and no name or number is ever reserved before it is used
clusters.root_cause: One tool call changes three or four separate files one after another. There is no all-or-nothing: if the third write fails, the first two stay on disk while the model is told the whole call failed, so the natural retry hits a world that has already half-moved and gets a nonsense error. Separately, nothing claims a decision number or a slug before writing it, and nothing checks that the record on disk is still the one that was read, so two calls happening at once both take the same number and the later one silently erases the earlier one's work.
clusters.recommended_fix: Introduce a unit of work in src/drivers/storage-driver.mjs: `async transaction(fn)` whose tx object buffers every write as {path, contents} (plus deletes) in memory and flushes nothing until fn resolves. LocalDriver implements it as: take the ledger lock from cluster 1 → run fn against the buffer → re-verify every read-modify-written thread's `rev` against disk → flush all buffered atomicWrites → commit. Any throw before flush leaves zero bytes changed. Then rewrite every write ladder to sit inside one transaction: transition-thread.mjs:39-46, archive-thread.mjs:24-29, reopen.mjs:28-30, open-thread.mjs:18-20, record-decision.mjs:66-77, bind-branch.mjs:13-15. The active-thread pointer must join the same unit of work, so move src/util/active-thread.mjs behind the driver (driver.writeActivePointer/clearActivePointer) where it can be staged and rolled back — today it is a durable side effect outside every rollback (active-thread.mjs:32-58). Add optimistic concurrency: a `rev` integer on the thread record, incremented by writeThread, which refuses a stale write with `ToolError: thread <id> changed since you read it (disk rev 7, submitted rev 6) — re-read with get_resume_brief and re-apply your change` (retryable:true). Replace nextDecisionNumber+writeDecision (local-driver.mjs:189-213) with a single driver.createDecision(slug, markdown) that reserves by exclusive create — loop `open(path,'wx')` from max+1 upward, catching EEXIST and incrementing — so a number is claimed atomically and a rename can never overwrite an existing decision; bound it at 9999 and throw a ToolError naming the offending oversized filename rather than emitting an unwritable ref. Delete the now-genuinely-dead ref-dedup branch at record-decision.mjs:68. Give session-event filenames a ULID suffix (`${safeIso}--${safeActor}--${newUlid()}.md`, local-driver.mjs:247) so millisecond collisions are structurally impossible; merge=union (git-ref-driver.mjs:28) then means what it says. Enforce slug uniqueness among non-terminal threads in newThread/open_thread/create_successor, refusing with the colliding thread's id.
rejected_alternatives: WRAP EACH LADDER IN try/catch AND UNDO THE EARLIER WRITES BY HAND - compensating writes are themselves writes that can fail for the same reason the original failed (disk full, worktree removed mid-call), and they cannot un-write a decision file already staged into the git index. Getting it right requires buffering, which is the proposed fix arrived at by a worse route.

SERIALIZE ALL TOOL CALLS BEHIND ONE GLOBAL MUTEX AND CALL IT DONE - closes the two-writers case but does nothing about a mid-ladder failure inside a single call, which is how the exact error string of known incident #2 ('illegal transition paused -> paused') was reproduced with no skill bug involved.

USE GIT ITSELF AS THE TRANSACTION: STAGE EVERYTHING, THEN COMMIT OR `reset --hard` - `reset --hard` in a worktree shared by every process is precisely the destructive-shared-state pattern cluster 1 exists to remove, and it cannot roll back the active-thread pointer, which lives outside the worktree at .git/ledger/active-thread (active-thread.mjs:23).

GENERATE DECISION NUMBERS FROM A ULID OR TIMESTAMP INSTEAD OF A COUNTER - breaks the four-digit DECISION_REF_PATTERN (patterns.mjs:8) that every existing ref, the briefing renderer (briefing.mjs:7) and read_decision's input schema (read-decision.mjs:25) already depend on, forcing a migration of committed decision filenames to fix a problem an exclusive create solves without one.
clusters.why_this_fix: Anthropic's guidance for tool writes that can fail ambiguously is that a retried call must be a safe no-op rather than a duplicate write, achieved with a reservation or idempotency key rather than by hoping the retry lands cleanly — https://ledgenter.com/blog/agent-writes-need-idempotency-keys (single non-Anthropic source, low confidence, flagged as such). The stronger and better-corroborated support is the error-recoverability contract: a tool error is only useful if the model can act on it, and 'illegal transition paused -> paused' after a partial write actively misleads — https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools (Error Handling) and https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/handle-tool-calls, which documents that Claude gets roughly 2-3 retries before giving up, so a retry that lands in a corrupted state consumes the entire budget.
clusters.risk: Adding `rev` changes the on-disk thread record. Migration: declare `rev: {type:'integer', minimum:0}` in src/schema/thread.schema.mjs:56-110 but leave it OUT of the required list — the root object is additionalProperties:false, so it MUST be declared or every existing write breaks; treat a missing rev as 0 on read and write it on the next write, so committed ledgers upgrade lazily with no migration command. Session-event filenames gain a suffix: old files keep their old names and are still read by path, so no migration is needed, but any external tooling parsing the two-part name breaks. Slug uniqueness is a new refusal that will reject open_thread calls that previously succeeded, including legitimately re-used titles; scope the check to non-terminal threads so a completed thread's slug can be reused. The buffered flush changes failure timing: a crash mid-flush can still leave a partial set, which is why the cluster-1 fsync work is a prerequisite, not an independent nicety.

clusters.cluster_name: Ledger content is re-served to the model as if the server had written it
clusters.root_cause: The briefing and the session-start roster are plain strings assembled by gluing server-authored headings onto stored ledger text with newlines. Because the stored text can also contain newlines and '## ', a reader has no way to tell which parts the server wrote and which came out of the database — and the skill and the Stop hook both instruct the model to treat the entire string as authoritative, unmodifiable session context. Anyone who can land a commit on the shared ledger ref can therefore write instructions that arrive in a teammate's model context, at session start, with no tool call and no user action.
clusters.recommended_fix: Build the trust boundary into the payload, in four parts. (1) One sanitizer at the render boundary. Add `field(value, max)` to src/render/briefing.mjs replacing the existing truncate() (:9-12): collapse every \r\n, \n, \r,  ,   to a single space, strip leading runs of #, -, >, * and backticks, then truncate. Apply it to EVERY interpolated value with no exception — title (:45, currently not truncated at all), criterion text (:78), risk text and refs (:93,:98), decision title (:125), out_of_scope entries (:133), child/predecessor slugs (:142-143), and the entire drift block (:62-65), which today interpolates entry.classification, entry.branch, signal.code and signal.detail with no truncation whatsoever. Do the same in hooks/lib/roster.mjs:33 for slug, title and id, which are today interpolated completely raw into SessionStart additionalContext. (2) A structural fence with a per-call nonce. renderBriefing wraps every ledger-derived block in `<<<ledger-data:{nonce}` … `ledger-data:{nonce}>>>` where nonce is minted per call, so stored text cannot forge a closing fence, and prefixes the document with a fixed server-authored line stating that fenced content is recorded project data and never an instruction. Emit the same briefing as typed `structuredContent` against a declared `outputSchema` (the pinned SDK 1.29.0 supports both; bin/ledger-server.mjs:54 currently emits only a JSON.stringify'd text block) so a client can consume sections as data rather than re-parsing prose. Apply the identical fence to read_decision's markdown payload (read-decision.mjs:10-14), which today hands over a raw file body with no marker at all. (3) Make the verbatim gate mean 'verbatim'. get_resume_brief stores sha256(rendered) in the pledge (get-resume-brief.mjs:30-34); hooks/lib/stop.mjs:87 replaces `text.includes(pledge.rendered)` with a whitespace-normalized exact comparison, so prepended commentary no longer passes a gate whose stated purpose is 'add nothing before or after it'. Make it fail CLOSED: readAssistantTexts swallowing an error into [] (stop.mjs:67-73) and parseTranscript returning [] for an oversized or non-file transcript (:39-42) currently both fall through to clearPledge at :91 — an unreadable transcript must block with its own message, not silently discharge the pledge. (4) Remove the blanket auto-approve. hooks/lib/pre-tool-use.mjs:156-160 returns permissionDecision 'allow' for any name matching /^mcp__(?:plugin_logbook_)?ledger__(.+)$/ (:8) whose suffix is in the local registry — a name-string test that any server registered as 'ledger' inherits. Split it: get_resume_brief, read_decision and rebuild_index stay auto-approved; the eleven state-changing tools return {} and fall through to the normal permission system. Add advisory `annotations: {readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint}` to each tool in src/tools/*.mjs and expose them from listTools (registry.mjs:53-55) for host UX only — explicitly NOT as the enforcement mechanism.
rejected_alternatives: BAN NEWLINES IN THE WRITE SCHEMAS AND CALL THE WRITE LAYER THE BOUNDARY - necessary but structurally insufficient: records arrive by git fetch from teammates and from older plugin versions, and readThread/listThreads (local-driver.mjs:143-164) apply no validation at all, so the write layer never sees the content it would need to have sanitized. The renderer is the last point every string passes through regardless of provenance.

ADD A WARNING TO skills/preflight/SKILL.md TELLING THE MODEL NOT TO TRUST BRIEFING CONTENT - skill body text is injected once and is never re-read on later turns, and after auto-compaction re-attached skills share a 25,000-token budget with only the first 5,000 tokens of each kept, so the warning can be silently gone by the time the briefing is printed (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills). It also gives the model no mechanical way to distinguish a forged '## SYSTEM OVERRIDE' from a real heading.

HTML- OR MARKDOWN-ESCAPE EVERY INTERPOLATED VALUE - the consumer is a language model reading prose, not a browser. Escaping wrecks legibility for the human who is shown the same text, and an escaped '\#\# SYSTEM OVERRIDE' still reads as an instruction to a model. A delimiter with an unforgeable nonce creates a boundary; escaping only creates noise.

STRIP THE BRIEFING TO UNSTRUCTURED PLAIN TEXT WITH NO HEADINGS - removes the forgery surface by destroying the structure the entire resume design and the verbatim gate exist to protect, and makes the briefing markedly worse for the human reader it is printed to.
clusters.why_this_fix: The MCP spec makes output sanitization a server-side MUST and result validation a client-side SHOULD precisely because a tool result can carry adversarial instructions back into the model — https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools (Security Considerations). Anthropic's tool-use docs state the rule directly: tool results 'often carry content from sources outside your control', an attacker who can influence that content may embed instructions to redirect Claude, and such content must stay inside tool_result blocks and be treated as data — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/handle-tool-calls. Removing the blanket allow is grounded in the spec's tool-safety principle that self-reported tool metadata must never be a security decision and that hosts must obtain user consent before invoking a tool — https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28 (Security and Trust & Safety > Tool Safety) — reinforced by the file's own admission at pre-tool-use.mjs:16 that its Bash branch 'is not a security boundary' while its ledger branch is a hard allow. structuredContent/outputSchema is a capability the pinned SDK already implements and logbook does not use — https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools.
clusters.risk: Sanitizing at render changes the exact bytes of every briefing, which invalidates any stored pledge hash across the upgrade and will make the Stop-hook gate fire once on the first session after upgrade unless the pledge is versioned and a mismatched version is discharged rather than blocked. The fence text is additive context on every briefing — a real token cost that must be measured against the 25,000-token MCP output cap. Removing the blanket allow reintroduces permission prompts for eleven tools, which the user will experience as a regression; it should ship with the read-only split so the preflight path stays prompt-free, and with a documented settings.json allow-rule for teams that want the old behavior. No on-disk data changes; existing ledgers with newline-bearing titles keep those bytes and simply render sanitized.

clusters.cluster_name: Rules are enforced where the model happens to be typing, never on what is actually on disk
clusters.root_cause: There is no single place that defines what a valid ledger record is. Each rule lives in whichever handler needed it first, so the same constraint is enforced on one tool and silently ignored on another, and the record schema that guards the actual write knows about almost none of them. The read side enforces nothing at all — it hands back whatever bytes are in the file — so any record written by a teammate, by an older version, or by a tool that skipped a check reads back fine and then fails on every write, and a single malformed file takes down thirteen of the fourteen tools with an error that names no file.
clusters.recommended_fix: Collapse four validation layers into one source of truth plus one invariant module, and give the read path a quarantine instead of a crash. (1) src/schema/thread.schema.mjs becomes the single constraint document. Every cap in src/model/caps.mjs (:1-12), the RISK_SENTENCE pattern in src/tools/spine-input.mjs:5, and every length limit move into it as maxLength/pattern/maxItems, plus the conditional requirements as if/then (status===done implies closure_statement minLength 1; status===blocked implies blocked_by minLength 1) — draft 2020-12 composition keywords are legal in an MCP inputSchema. caps.mjs and spine-input.mjs stop OWNING constraints and instead derive the per-tool inputSchema fragments from the same exported constants, so a cap cannot exist in one layer and not another. This alone closes the 120-char decision title that record_decision bypasses (record-decision.mjs:68-76,:91 vs update-thread.mjs:77), the 200-char criterion cap gap the incident report names, the unbounded title/slug (thread.schema.mjs:59-60), the unbounded session-log actor and body (append-session-event.mjs:25-26 — cap actor at 64 chars so ENAMETOOLONG becomes a named field error), and closure_statement's three incompatible emptiness definitions (transition-thread.mjs:60, dod.mjs:11-14, thread.schema.mjs:95). (2) One invariant module for what JSON Schema cannot express: src/model/invariants.mjs exporting assertThreadInvariants(thread, {ledger}) — no two open detours (today only in amend-criteria.mjs:50-56 and trivially bypassed at creation via criteriaCreateItem, schemas.mjs:48-56), no spine mutation on a terminal thread (today in update-thread.mjs:109 and amend-criteria.mjs:106 but absent from record-decision.mjs:42-51), slug uniqueness, and active-pointer consistency. Call it from writeThread (local-driver.mjs:147-153), NOT from individual handlers — a single call site is exactly why record_decision cannot skip it. (3) Read path validates and quarantines rather than throwing. Wrap the JSON.parse at local-driver.mjs:63 (currently outside its own try, so a truncated file throws a pathless SyntaxError) so a malformed file yields {path, reason}. readThread and listThreads both upcast (listThreads at :160 does not today) and both validate; a record that fails becomes a QuarantinedRecord that listThreads skips and rebuildIndex reports as `quarantined: [{path, reason, remedy}]` in its counts (rebuild-index.mjs:69-76). One bad file stops being a total outage. (4) Make the upcast lossless-or-repaired and write it back. src/schema/upcast.mjs:44 and :73 copy v1 risk and out_of_scope strings through verbatim, and :54-58 copies a raw v1 decision string into `ref`, all of which the v2 schema rejects (thread.schema.mjs:17, :106, :28); repair them at upcast time (drop empty entries, route a non-conforming ref to LEGACY_SCOPE with a synthesized ref) and persist the upcast on the next write, so read-fine/write-fail becomes impossible. (5) Fix the pure contract bugs in the same pass: add the terminal guard to record_decision; preserve blocked_by into the session event text on blocked->paused (transition-thread.mjs:30,:45 destroys the only record of the blocker); refuse closure_statement on a non-done target instead of dropping it (:32,:60); stop bind_branch writing the active pointer for a non-active thread (bind-branch.mjs:14) — that combination with archive-thread.mjs:25 and stop.mjs:101-105 is an unrecoverable session-end deadlock with no in-protocol remedy; correct archive_thread's description (:35), which claims unconditionally to clear the pointer; run assertNoRestatedDecision in both directions (update-thread.mjs:70-76 checks only when out_of_scope is submitted, and record_decision never checks); and split thread-scope decisions under a 'Standing:' subheading in briefing.mjs:119-127 exactly as the risks block already does at :107-114, so a deliberately promoted standing decision stops being read back as 'DECIDED ON THIS STEP'. (6) Ship `ledger-cli migrate` for committed data: read every record, upcast, repair, truncate over-cap fields, report every change, write back in one commit.
rejected_alternatives: KEEP THE FOUR LAYERS AND ADD THE MISSING CHECKS TO EACH - this is exactly the process that produced the defect. With no shared source of truth the next constraint added will again land in one, two or three of four places; the incident report already documents the 200-char criterion cap living in the ajv input schema and at creation but not at the write gate.

VALIDATE ON READ AND THROW ON ANY INVALID RECORD - converts one bad teammate record into a hard outage of thirteen tools, which is the corrupt-JSON defect with better prose. Quarantine keeps the ledger usable and makes the bad record nameable and fixable.

BUMP schema_version TO 3 AND HARD-REFUSE v2 RECORDS - strands every committed ledger until a migration runs, and makes the plugin unusable in exactly the projects that have the most history to lose. The additive-plus-quarantine path keeps old data readable throughout.

ENFORCE THE CAPS IN THE SKILL FILES INSTEAD, SINCE THE MODEL IS THE ONLY WRITER - skill prose is loaded once and dropped after compaction (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills), and it cannot constrain records that arrive over git from another machine, which is where the read/write asymmetry actually bites.
clusters.why_this_fix: The spec makes input validation against the declared schema a server MUST, and locates the authoritative boundary at the schema rather than in scattered handler checks — https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools (Security Considerations). Draft 2020-12 composition keywords, including if/then/else for conditional requirements, are explicitly legal inside a tool inputSchema — https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic (JSON Schema Usage). Stating a constraint in the schema rather than surfacing it only through a rejection is directly recommended because a schema-stated constraint is read once per tool-list and planned around, while a constraint discovered by failing costs a full round trip out of a documented 2-3-retry budget — https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents and https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/handle-tool-calls.
clusters.risk: This is the migration-heavy cluster. Tightening thread.schema.mjs makes committed records that violate the new caps invalid — a 300-char decision title written through record_decision's uncapped path, a v1-upcast risk with no em dash, a free-text slug from open-thread.mjs:33 — which is precisely why the read behavior must be quarantine-and-report, never throw, and why `ledger-cli migrate` must truncate and repair rather than reject. The `rev` field from cluster 2 lands in the same schema and should ship together to avoid two migrations. Adding the terminal guard to record_decision and slug uniqueness to open_thread rejects calls that previously succeeded; the bind_branch pointer change alters observable behavior a user may have come to rely on for marking a thread as current. The invariants call in writeThread runs on every write, so it must be cheap or it compounds the per-call cost cluster 6 addresses.

clusters.cluster_name: The shared ledger was designed as if one person on one machine used it
clusters.root_cause: The ledger is a git ref that is fetched, merged and pushed automatically at session start and session end, but the merge policy, the way a repository is identified, and the push trigger all assume a single user. Conflicts are resolved by unconditionally taking whoever synced last, and the result is force-pushed, so a teammate's ledger silently replaces your just-written session state with nothing reported to anyone. A branch binding stores an absolute path that only exists on the machine that created it, so on anyone else's laptop that path either crashes reconcile with a message claiming git is not installed, or — worse — happens to exist and gets inspected, after which reconcile marks another person's live work orphaned.
clusters.recommended_fix: Five changes across src/drivers/git-ref-driver.mjs, src/model/binding.mjs and src/drift/. (1) Stop discarding local work on merge. Replace `-X theirs` at git-ref-driver.mjs:490 with a record-aware merge: ship a custom merge driver in the plugin, registered through .gitattributes alongside the existing `sessions/**/*.md merge=union` (:28), that merges threads/*.json and bindings/*.json field by field — spine arrays unioned by ref/text, scalars resolved by updated_at — and, when it genuinely cannot decide, writes both sides and marks the record conflicted so it surfaces through cluster 4's quarantine channel. Never silently drop a local hunk. (2) Surface the merge. sync() already returns {merged:true} (:440) and both call sites throw it away — hooks/lib/session-start.mjs:98 and hooks/lib/stop.mjs:106. Return it as additionalContext/stderr naming the affected thread ids so the model and the user learn that a merge touched their work. (3) Stop putting machine-local paths in shared records. src/model/binding.mjs:20 stores `repo` verbatim; replace it with `{repo_id, repo_relpath}` where repo_id is the repository's root-commit sha (already obtainable via the `rev-list --max-parents=0` call the driver makes at git-ref-driver.mjs:153), and keep the machine-local absolute path in the per-machine state store from cluster 1, never in a committed record. git-ref-driver.mjs:504-506 resolves repo_id to a local path through that map; with no local mapping it SKIPS the binding rather than spawning git in a nonexistent cwd — which is where `spawn git ENOENT` comes from, since git-exec.mjs:20-22 rejects a spawn failure before the check:false escape at :26 can suppress it. This removes both the leak of /Users/<name>/... into every teammate's clone and the false 'git is not installed' diagnosis. (4) Make reconcile per-binding fault-tolerant and observation-honest. Wrap src/drift/reconcile.mjs:35 and :54 in per-binding try/catch that records {binding_id, repo_id, error} into the result instead of aborting the whole loop — today one unreachable path kills the reconcile the preflight skill requires before briefing (skills/preflight/SKILL.md:22). And a binding whose repo could not be observed on THIS machine must be classified `unknown`, never `orphaned`: today reconcile.mjs:43-46 writes the closed binding and reconcile.mjs:8 commits it, so a teammate's active work is permanently marked orphaned in the shared record. Auto-reattach by slugified branch name (src/drift/reattach.mjs:41-46, where branchSlug is only `branch.trim().replace(/\//g,'-')` per slug.mjs:5) stops writing a binding on its own and returns a `proposed` disposition the model must confirm with an explicit bind_branch. (5) Gate what leaves the machine. Keep `--no-verify` (:390) — the ledger worktree must not run the host repo's hooks, which is why git-scope.mjs:77 nulls hooksPath — but add a server-side secret scan in a new src/util/redact.mjs applied at write time to append_session_event.body, record_decision.context/outcome and the spine free-text fields, refusing with a ToolError naming the field and the matched pattern class and never echoing the matched value. And make the push explicit: sync() pushes only when auto-push is enabled or the user confirmed once per project (a marker in the per-machine state store); otherwise it fetches and merges locally and reports 'N ledger commits not pushed'.
rejected_alternatives: USE `-X ours` INSTEAD OF `-X theirs` - the identical silent-loss defect with the sign flipped. It discards the teammate's hunk rather than mine and is equally invisible to both parties; the problem is silence, not direction.

FAIL THE SYNC ON ANY DIVERGENCE AND MAKE THE HUMAN RESOLVE IT IN GIT - the ledger worktree lives under CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA and is a place no user ever opens. The failure would surface as raw git stderr at SessionStart in every session after the first conflict, and since sync runs before reconcile and roster (session-start.mjs:98-100) it would take the whole session-start path down with it.

MOVE SECRET SCANNING INTO A pre-commit OR commit-msg HOOK - the plugin deliberately runs its git with hooks disabled (--no-verify at git-ref-driver.mjs:390, core.hooksPath nulled at git-scope.mjs:77) so the host repo's hooks cannot interfere with plugin-managed commits. Re-enabling them would run arbitrary repo hooks against ledger commits, which is a larger hazard than the one being fixed.

HASH THE ABSOLUTE PATH INSTEAD OF REPLACING IT - a hash of /Users/alice/work/repo is still per-machine, so it fixes the username leak and leaves every cross-machine reconcile failure exactly as it is. The root commit sha is stable across clones, which is the property actually needed.
clusters.why_this_fix: The spec's server-side security requirements name sanitizing tool outputs and implementing proper access controls as MUSTs, and the same section's client-side SHOULDs include showing tool inputs before calling specifically to catch data-exfiltration attempts — an automatic push at session start and end with the result discarded defeats that entire control — https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools (Security Considerations). The per-binding fault-tolerance and the honest 'unknown' classification are the error-recoverability contract applied to a loop: 'spawn git ENOENT' is a generic error that forces the model to guess, and Anthropic's guidance is that a specific, actionable message is what lets Claude self-correct within its 2-3-retry window rather than acting on a false diagnosis — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/handle-tool-calls and https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents.
clusters.risk: The binding record shape changes, which is committed data in real ledgers. Migration: src/schema/binding.schema.mjs accepts both shapes; a binding carrying only `repo` is read as legacy and resolved against the local path map by string match, and `ledger-cli migrate` rewrites it with the root-commit id only when the path resolves on the running machine, leaving foreign bindings untouched so no one's record is rewritten from a machine that cannot see it. A custom merge driver is not installed on a fresh clone until the plugin runs, so a git merge performed outside the plugin falls back to the default driver and can still conflict badly — the conflicted-record quarantine path is the backstop and must exist before this ships. Making push explicit changes long-standing behavior and will strand ledgers on one machine for users who never notice the prompt; the 'N commits not pushed' report has to be prominent. Server-side secret scanning has false positives that will refuse legitimate session-log content, so the refusal must name the pattern class and offer an explicit override parameter rather than being unbypassable.

clusters.cluster_name: Failures and costs are invisible to the only caller the server has
clusters.root_cause: When something goes wrong the model receives a bare name-and-message pair with no indication of which layer rejected it, which field was wrong, what a correct value looks like, or whether retrying could ever work — so it retries the wrong hypothesis until its budget is gone. The constraints it would have needed to avoid the failure are written in a skill file rather than in the tool contract, and some of them are simply wrong there. Meanwhile every single write re-reads every thread in the ledger, rewrites four index files and spawns five git processes, so the retry loop is also the slowest path in the system, and none of these failure modes has a test.
clusters.recommended_fix: Make the server self-describing and cheap, in five parts. (1) Structured errors with a retryability verdict. One LedgerError base in src/tools/shared.mjs carrying {code, layer, field, expected, example, retryable, remedy}; bin/ledger-server.mjs:55-59 renders it into both the text content block and a `structuredContent` payload declared by an outputSchema. `retryable:false` is the load-bearing field — it is exactly the signal the record_decision incident needed, where a parameter that never arrived surfaced as a schema error that a shape-retry could never fix. src/schema/validators.mjs:9-11 currently discards e.params, which is why the largest call in the protocol returns three identical anonymous clauses; keep params so `(root) must NOT have additional properties` becomes `unknown property "active_goal" — did you mean spine.active_goal? valid top-level properties: thread_id, spine, replace_scopes, completion_criteria`. Preserve the spec's channel split: unknown tool name (registry.mjs:59-61) becomes a JSON-RPC protocol error rather than isError:true, since the spec names it as a protocol-error example and the model is unlikely to recover from it. (2) Move the contract out of the skills and into the schemas. update_thread's nesting is already in its schema and is invisible only because of the error text — fixing (1) fixes it. Give replace_scopes' object shape a sentence in its own description (schemas.mjs:39-46). Name to_status in transition_thread's description (transition-thread.mjs:52). Add slug resolution so `/preflight <slug>` works: the by-slug index the server already builds and persists (rebuild-index.mjs:34-36,:64) is reachable from no tool today, and get_resume_brief requires a ULID (:46) — accept `{thread_id}` or `{slug}` via oneOf, or add a resolve_thread tool. Make the roster emit `thread_id` alongside `id` (rebuild-index.mjs:44, roster.mjs:33) so the skill's own word matches the payload. Include the thread_id in every error payload from a tool that already read the thread, so a lost id is recoverable in-protocol rather than only through the Stop hook's block message (stop.mjs:8), which is unreachable in the documented flow. (3) Make recovery_degraded mean something. Replace the boolean (shared.mjs:15-22) with {durability: 'committed'|'uncommitted'|'unversioned', reason, remedy}. local-driver.mjs:113-116, :134-136 and :298-300 stop discarding the caught error and put its message in reason; git-ref-driver.mjs:397-404 catches and degrades instead of throwing raw git stderr, so the field the model was taught to check is not a compile-time false on the backend that actually ships (:388,:394). Add a commit-retry capability so 'unversioned' is actionable — today no tool in TOOLS (registry.mjs:19-34) can retry a commit. (4) Cut the per-call cost. commitAndReindex (shared.mjs:19-22) stops rebuilding the entire index on every mutating call: keep an in-process cache of parsed records keyed by path+mtime, mark dirty per write, and recompute only affected entries; flush the four writeIndexFile calls (rebuild-index.mjs:64-67) through cluster 2's single staged transaction; read thread files concurrently instead of the sequential await loop at local-driver.mjs:158-163; and collapse #commitWorktree's five execFile spawns (git-ref-driver.mjs:385,386,390,391,393) by dropping the separate `diff --cached --quiet` in favor of commit's own exit code and skipping `update-ref` when the worktree HEAD already equals the ref. Cap the wire payload: bin/ledger-server.mjs:53-54 JSON.stringify's unbounded, so add a documented ceiling with an actionable truncation notice. (5) Validate config at the boundary. bin/ledger-server.mjs:15-24 accepts any non-empty string, so a bad LEDGER_BACKEND makes all fourteen tools fail identically with an opaque bare Error from git-ledger.mjs:33-38, forever, because the cached contextPromise resets at :41. Check the backend against the enum and the branch with `git check-ref-format` at envToUserConfig, and declare the enum in .claude-plugin/plugin.json:10-15 so the UI constrains it. Tests, as a named suite: two concurrent record_decision calls must yield two distinct numbers; a truncated thread JSON must quarantine rather than throw SyntaxError; a driver whose commit throws must leave no partial state (test/unit/tools/shared.test.mjs:5-14 only ever returns a canned object); the briefing-pledge test must call the initGitRepo helper that already exists in test/unit/cli/fixtures.mjs and is used by restore.test.mjs:59 and record-sha.test.mjs:34 but not by briefing-pledge.test.mjs:7-12; a v1 record with an empty-string risk must round-trip; and a render test asserting no ledger-derived value can emit a line beginning '## '.
rejected_alternatives: WRITE THE PARAMETER NAMES, NESTING AND CAPS INTO skills/debrief/SKILL.md MORE CAREFULLY - skill body content is loaded once and dropped after compaction under a shared 25,000-token budget (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills), and the failure it must prevent happens inside a tool call at a moment when the skill text may no longer be in context. The error message is the only channel guaranteed present at the point of failure. The skill's own step 5 already demonstrates the failure mode: it enumerates spine fields as if they were top-level and the model has no way to learn otherwise from the rejection.

RETURN EVERY FAILURE AS A JSON-RPC PROTOCOL ERROR SO THE CLIENT SURFACES IT PROMINENTLY - the spec reserves protocol errors for request-structure problems and explicitly notes the model is less likely to recover from them; recoverable failures belong in isError:true precisely so the model can see them and self-correct (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools). Only the unknown-tool case should move.

BUILD AN APPEND-ONLY JOURNAL SO THE INDEX NEVER NEEDS A FULL REBUILD - a second derived on-disk artifact with its own consistency problem, layered on a store that cluster 1 shows is not yet durable. An mtime-keyed in-process cache with dirty-marking gets the same asymptotic win with no new file format and nothing to migrate.

RAISE MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS INSTEAD OF CAPPING THE PAYLOAD - shifts an unbounded cost onto the user's global setting for every server they run, rather than the tool author owning its own result size, which is where the guidance places the burden (https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents).
clusters.why_this_fix: The spec's error-handling section draws the line at recoverability by the calling model and asks servers to preserve it; the schema comment states the mechanism plainly — errors go inside the result with isError:true so the LLM can see them and self-correct, with no automatic retry or rollback implied — https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts (CallToolResult.isError). Anthropic's tool-writing guidance requires error text that communicates specific and actionable improvements and shows a correctly formatted example rather than opaque codes, and documents that a specific message lands in the 2-3-retry success window while a generic one forces guessing — https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents and https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/handle-tool-calls. The payload cap is grounded in Claude Code's documented 25,000-token MCP output limit and its practice of steering the agent with instructions on truncation rather than cutting silently — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp. structuredContent/outputSchema is already implemented by the pinned SDK 1.29.0 and unused here (registry.mjs:53-55, bin/ledger-server.mjs:54) — https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools.
clusters.risk: Changing recovery_degraded from a boolean to an object is a tool-contract break for anything that reads the field; keep the boolean alongside the new object for one release and mark it deprecated in the tool descriptions, since it is a response field only and touches no on-disk data. Adding structuredContent and outputSchema changes the result envelope — a client that ignores structuredContent still gets the text block per the spec's backward-compatibility guidance, so this is additive. Adding a slug alternative to get_resume_brief via oneOf widens an input schema that is currently additionalProperties:false and required:['thread_id']; it must remain impossible to pass both. The index cache introduces a staleness class of bug that did not exist before — mtime granularity is one second on some filesystems, so the cache key must include size and the dirty-marking must be authoritative for in-process writes. Boundary validation of LEDGER_BACKEND will hard-fail servers that today start with a typo'd value and silently fail on every call; that is the intended improvement but it changes the failure from fourteen opaque errors to one clear startup refusal, which some users will read as a regression until they see the message.
